# @lmzhen/dsh-evolution-preset

Compatibility one-click bundle for existing configurations. New installations should normally use `evolution-all`.

Like `all`, it mounts model tools at profile root so every session receives them. It does not include the settings/skill-history UI umbrella, merge sidebar, or skill-health panel.

This bundle is mutually exclusive with `all`, `host`, and the layered Evolution preset. Use [INSTALL.md](../INSTALL.md) for the attach/variant semantics and upgrade path.

The package also ships a standalone `cordis.yml`. That standalone composition intentionally omits the `evolution-maintenance/tools` row; add it explicitly if a standalone deployment needs `maintenance_probe`.

# dsh-evolution

## What is this plugin for?

The plugin is designed to generate skills automatically and manage their full lifecycle, with an emphasis on retaining capabilities that are specific to a user and a project. It is task-oriented: the model builds and maintains a private set of skills for the user's environment, preferences and working procedures, improving its fit for those tasks.

That lifecycle includes creation, discovery, use, revision after review, restructuring, merging, archiving and restoration. These are independent capabilities rather than stages every skill must pass through. The plugin also provides budgeted memory for project facts and user preferences across sessions.

It does not modify or train the model, and it does not provide a hosted model service. DSH's configured model performs the semantic work, while the plugin's write gates, snapshots, history and approval mechanisms constrain changes and recovery.

## Platform line

The family targets DeepSeek Harness `0.2.2-rc.1` only. Published packages declare the `^0.2.2-rc.0` peer range and the `>=0.2.2-rc.0 <0.2.3-0` engine range. The single host edge is the `evolutionPlatform` service; features reach it through the family's platform ports, never by importing host internals.

## What is a skill?

Early language models generated text autoregressively. Questions, instructions and answers were linked statistically, so prompts that described the domain, task and constraints precisely usually improved the result. That relationship was a foundation of early prompt engineering.

Chain-of-thought and stronger model capabilities reduced the need for exhaustive prompts in some single-step tasks: the model could recall terminology and conventions during reasoning. Tool calling then changed the objective again. Instead of producing one piece of content, the model had to complete a sequence of operations. Execution order, tool constraints, completion criteria and failure recovery still needed explicit instructions. The prompt increasingly resembled an operating manual rather than a complete description of one desired answer.

Different tasks need different manuals, and they cannot all remain in context. One approach is to connect step-specific prompts and inputs and outputs into a fixed workflow. Another is to package a manual as a module that the model can discover by name and description and load when relevant. That module is a skill. In DSH, a skill normally consists of a `SKILL.md` body and optional scripts, templates and reference files, loaded through the native `skill` tool.

Skills and MCP belong to different layers. MCP is a protocol for connecting tools and resources; a skill describes when to use those capabilities, in what order, and what counts as done. The plugin manages procedural knowledge, not tool connectivity itself.

## Why build this plugin?

Two related changes are taking place:

1. **The marginal value of some general-purpose skills is falling.** Public, common operating procedures are increasingly being absorbed into model capability through training. Maintaining a separate manual for those tasks yields less benefit, although this does not make every general-purpose skill obsolete.
2. **Models are becoming capable of extracting operating procedures from execution traces.** With real trajectories and clear feedback, a model can organize the steps, constraints and corrections from a task into a reusable skill. This plugin uses that capability during review and skill writing. The output still passes structural checks and may require human approval; it is not assumed to be correct merely because a model produced it.

At the same time, every user's machine, project conventions, preferences and complex task details remain different. Once general capability is sufficient, the decisive knowledge is often valid only for one person or one project. A private skill set grows with task variety and complexity, and it also develops duplication, staleness and structural problems. Maintaining all of that manually does not scale.

The plugin therefore uses the model's semantic ability to automate the generation and maintenance work that is suitable for automation, while retaining human control and recovery paths. Its objective is not unrestricted skill accumulation, but a useful, inspectable and maintainable private skill set built from real work.

## How does it relate to memory plugins?

The two are largely complementary. A typical memory plugin manages facts: who the user is, what the project is, and what was decided. This plugin is more concerned with process: how a class of task should be performed, in what order, and to what standard. It is intended primarily for people who use Harness to get work done.

The plugin also contains a memory module, but its design differs from the familiar retrieve-on-demand, continuously growing model:

- **Memory has a hard character budget.** The default budgets for project memory in `MEMORY.md` and the user profile in `USER.md` are 2200 and 1375 characters. If a batch would exceed the budget, it is refused rather than silently truncated. The model must delete or compact existing entries before adding new ones. After the budget is lowered, replacement can also be refused when an existing entry exceeds the new limit; deletion is then the recovery path.
- **Memory is supplied as a snapshot instead of relying only on deliberate retrieval.** This keeps critical project facts visible during a task instead of depending on the model to search for them.

Snapshot injection does not mean that every persisted byte necessarily reaches the model context. Entries matched by threat scanning are filtered, and abnormally large files are skipped. The character budget bounds injection size; it is not a guarantee that every task avoids performance loss or additional context cost. The design keeps critical facts within a bounded context while using skills to maintain procedural knowledge.

## What capabilities does it provide?

Each capability below has a corresponding code entry point. They have different triggers and should not be read as a pipeline that runs for every task.

| Capability | Current behavior and defaults |
|---|---|
| Skill generation and updates | The agent can create and patch skills through `skill_manage`. By default, review prompts ask the model to generate or update skills at an interval of ten weighted tool calls after substantive cadence signals, delivered at a task boundary; a review does not have to produce a new skill |
| Skill catalog and search | The full catalog is published by default and loaded through the native `skill` tool; `skill_search` provides local retrieval, while discovery domain cards and catalog trimming are off by default |
| Library curation | Curator performs deterministic lifecycle maintenance on interval and idle conditions, marking stale skills and archiving them; LLM-nominated consolidation is a separate option |
| Skill merge | Started with `/evolution merge scan` or `pair`. Scan requires local potion models and can fall back to stub without an LLM; ordinary pair does not require potion, but round 1/authoring requires a child-session model. Initiated runs are auto-approved by default, with `mergeApproval` available for manual approval |
| Memory | Available in `all`, `preset` and selected layered-preset sessions. Project memory and user-profile budgets default to 2200 and 1375 characters; new writes are refused at the limit rather than silently truncated |
| Write approval and recovery | Ordinary write approval is off by default and stages memory and skill writes when enabled; curator and merge use their own controls. Skill history, body undo, unit undo and archive restore have different scopes, and execution-time failures do not guarantee complete rollback |
| Diagnostics and UI | `/evolution doctor`, curation reports, skill health and a knowledge graph are available; `all` provides settings, skill history and a merge panel on Web/desktop GUI, while the health panel is disabled by default |

See [Feature reference](docs/features.md) for triggers, failure behavior and limits.

## Install

See [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md) for prerequisites, all four installation forms and upgrades. Install the full form by default:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add @lmzhen/dsh-evolution-all
# Restart DSH, then run in a session:
/evolution doctor
```

For the desktop GUI, replace `--profile web` with `--profile desktop`. After installation, ask the agent to remember a project fact and open a new session to verify that it is injected. `doctor` checks the installation form and service state; it does not replace an actual read/write check.

The full source layout reports<!-- gen:install-counts --> 35 packages installed (the published list is 36; the agent preset is separate)<!-- /gen:install-counts -->.

## Installation forms

| Form | Use case | Capabilities and UI |
|---|---|---|
| `all` | Default full installation | Memory and skill tools in every session; evolution workbench (history/pending/merge/health) and the diagnostics card on Web/desktop GUI |
| `host` | No memory/skill write tools for the model | Explicit merge, background curation, manual maintenance and diagnostics remain; automatic review and usage accounting do not run; no evolution workbench or diagnostics |
| `preset` | Migration from an older configuration | Similar tool coverage to `all`, without settings or sidebar panels |
| Layered preset | Tools only in selected sessions | `host` plus the Evolution preset; other sessions do not enable automatic plugin behavior; no settings or sidebar panels |

Use only one form per profile. See [packages/INSTALL.md](packages/INSTALL.md) for exact session behavior and [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md) for commands.

## Common commands

| Command | When to use it |
|---|---|
| `/evolution doctor` | Check installation form, versions and service state |
| `/evolution pending` | List ordinary writes waiting for approval |
| `/evolution skill history <name>` | Inspect body and support-file history |
| `/evolution skill undo <name>` | Revert the skill body; support files are not restored |
| `/evolution curator status` | Inspect automatic curation state |
| `/evolution merge status <runId>` | Inspect an initiated merge run |
| `/graph` | Browse or edit the skill and memory graph |

See [docs/commands.md](docs/commands.md) for the command reference and [docs/configuration.md](docs/configuration.md) for common settings.

## Data and safety

- In the default assembly, plugin data is stored under `$DSH_HOME` and does not depend on a family-hosted service. See [Operations](docs/operations.md) for backup and restore scope.
- Controlled memory/skill model tools scan call arguments, and the corresponding write paths apply structural checks and policy protection. Approval is an optional additional control; it neither replaces those checks nor covers curator or merge internal writes.
- Skill deletion archives the skill. Body history is recorded best-effort; verify an available version before undo, and note that body undo does not restore support files. Pre-curation snapshots can be restored, and merge runs retain records used for undo.
- Local storage does not mean that content never leaves the machine. Review, LLM curation and discovery domain generation send the relevant task or skill content to the configured model provider; branch review also copies session events into a child session.
- API keys are managed by DSH model and credential configuration. Do not place them in skills, memories or plugin configuration. See [Models and API keys](docs/api-keys.md).

## Compatibility

| Item | Current requirement |

| Validated platform line | **`0.2.1-rc.3`** |
| Published dependency window | `^0.2.1-rc.2` |
| Family version | `0.37.1` |
| Node | `^22.19.0` or `>=24.0.0` |

Published packages do not cross older prerelease platform lines. See [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md) for installation and upgrade order.

- [Getting started](docs/getting-started.md): installation, first memory write and first skill operation.
- [Feature reference](docs/features.md): actual capabilities, defaults and limits.
- [Commands](docs/commands.md): everyday, curation, merge and maintenance commands.

# dsh-publish-github

A **GitHub publishing plugin** for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness): type one command in the composer and publish any local directory as a GitHub repository — `git init`, repo creation, commit and push, without leaving the session.

## What it does

```
/publish <dir>   →  git init (if needed) → git add -A → commit (first commit)
                 →  origin exists → push; otherwise → gh repo create --source . --push
```

One command covers the whole flow, reporting each step as a ✓/✗ line in the session.

## Why a slash command instead of a model tool

DSH's `@deepseek-ai/*` packages live inside the Electron `app.asar`, so a plugin mounted from disk **cannot import them** — which rules out the official `ctx.tools.register` path. This plugin registers `/publish` through the host's `ctx.commands.register` instead, needing no internal package and working as soon as it is mounted.

## Install

```bash
# GitHub
dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:lucyVan/dsh-publish-github

# Local checkout
dsh plugin --profile desktop add /absolute/path/to/dsh-publish-github
```

Restart DSH afterwards. Authorize GitHub once, either way:

```bash
# Option A: gh CLI login (recommended)
brew install gh
gh auth login

# Option B: save GITHUB_TOKEN in DSH credentials — the plugin injects it as GH_TOKEN
```

## Usage

```
/publish /path/to/your/project
```

Options:

| Flag | Effect |
|---|---|
| `--private` | Create a private repository (public by default) |
| `--name <repo>` | Repository name (defaults to the directory basename) |
| `--message "<msg>"` | Commit message / repository description (default `Publish <repo>`) |
| `--author <name>` | Author name for the first commit (defaults to your git config) |
| `--email <addr>` | Author email for the first commit (defaults to your git config) |

Quote paths that contain spaces — Windows paths work the same way:

```
/publish "C:\Users\me\My Projects" --private
/publish "/Users/me/My Projects" --name my-project
```

Example:

```
/publish ~/IdeaProjects/my-plugin --private --name best-plugin --message "My first DSH plugin"
```

## Safety

- **Never** force-pushes, deletes branches or resets history — such words are refused up front;
- When `origin` already exists it only performs a normal `push` and never recreates the remote;
- The child environment strips `DSH_*` variables so harness configuration never reaches `gh`;
- Any directory is allowed (deliberate: the path the user names is the authorization).

## Requirements

| Dependency | Notes |
|---|---|
| `git` | required |
| `gh` | required (`brew install gh`) |
| GitHub auth | `gh auth login`, or a `GITHUB_TOKEN` in DSH credentials |
| Node | `>= 22` |

## Known limitations

- Only the `/publish` command; there is no settings page (account details come from gh CLI or DSH credentials);
- GitHub repositories only — no npm publishing;
- The first commit is authored as `DSH <dsh@localhost>` (amend it afterwards if you prefer);
- No conflict handling: if the remote already has unrelated history, the push fails and the error is reported verbatim.

## Compatibility

| Item | Status |
|---|---|
| DSH version | Verified on `0.2.2-rc.1`; declares `engines.dsh: >=0.2.2-rc.1 <0.3.0-0` |
| Platform | Tested on macOS; **Windows untested**, with three adaptations in place: `gh`/`gh.exe`/`gh.cmd`/`gh.bat` are probed in order, arguments honour quotes (including backslash paths), and the commit author is configurable |
| npm dependencies | **None**: only `node:*` built-ins, no `@deepseek-ai/*` imports |
| Browser module dependencies | **None**: host-only plugin, no client half |
| Required external tools | `git` and `gh`, both on `PATH` |
| Install | Declares `dsh.bundle`, so `dsh plugin add` registers it as a profile layer automatically — no manual patch editing |

Install verification: `dsh plugin --profile web add github:lucyVan/dsh-publish-github` was run in an isolated `DSH_HOME`.

## Uninstall

```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop remove dsh-publish-github
```

Then restart DSH.

## License

MIT (see [LICENSE](LICENSE))

decision.reason: Held for runtime execution policy acceptance. MIT, explicit Git installation and DSH at least 0.2.2-rc.1 below 0.3.0. Native /publish command directly invokes git/gh using host credentials; git add -A stages the workspace, visibility defaults to public, and the inspected publication path lacks a separate file-content preview/confirmation boundary. Existing repositories can push without committing staged changes. Publication/data-exposure policy acceptance remains unresolved. No lifecycle hook. No candidate code or lifecycle hooks were executed; runtime safety and compatibility are unproven.

# dsh-side-chat-slash

A **side chat** for the [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) Web GUI, built on [`@flyer103/dsh-side-chat`](https://github.com/flyer103/dsh-side-chat) 0.7.0.

> **This is a fork, not an original work.** The bulk of the code comes from flyer103's [`dsh-side-chat`](https://github.com/flyer103/dsh-side-chat) (MIT licensed). This repository adds only the changes listed below and keeps the original LICENSE.

[English](README.md) | [中文](README.zh.md)

[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)

## What it does

Opens a **side conversation** next to the main session: it forks the current session into a child conversation that runs the **same agent, same tools and same workspace**, and can really edit files. Close it when done — the main transcript is never touched.

## Differences from upstream

| # | Change | Why |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **New `/side` slash command** | Upstream only offers the right-sidebar guide card. `/side` + Enter now opens a side-chat tab from the composer. Registered as a **host** command (`ctx.commands.register`) rather than a client `commandUi` contribution, which depends on the session summary and a client locale service and can silently disappear |
| 2 | **Open-request bridge** | `/side` does not create a side session itself; it raises a "please open a tab" flag that the client polls (`/side-chat/api/pending`, every 2s) and then calls `sidebarRight.openTab('side-chat')`. The tab still owns the session, so upstream's one-tab-one-session (and close-disposes) lifecycle is preserved |
| 3 | **Approval pinned to `never`** | Upstream inherits the parent's approval policy, but the side-chat tab renders no approval prompt — a parent on `ask` would leave the side agent waiting forever. A parent `ask` is now downgraded to `never` for the side chat |

## Install

```bash
# GitHub
dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:lucyVan/dsh-side-chat-slash

# Local checkout
dsh plugin --profile desktop add /absolute/path/to/dsh-side-chat-slash
```

Restart DSH afterwards (quit the Desktop app with ⌘Q, then reopen).

## Usage

1. Open any session that has at least one message
2. Type **`/side`** in the composer and press Enter — a side-chat tab appears in the right sidebar
3. Send the first message in that tab; the fork happens then, so an empty tab costs nothing
4. Close the tab to destroy that side chat; run `/side` again for a new one

The upstream entry point (the "Side chat" card on the right sidebar's guide page) still works.

## Relationship to the main session

- **Inherits** the full history at fork time, the same preset, cwd, provider/model and sandbox mode
- **Isolated**: side-chat turns never enter the main transcript, the session list or the subagent catalog
- **Independent**: main-session messages after the fork do not flow into it; each side chat has its own context
- **Really edits files**: `write` / `edit` / `bash` act on the same workspace, so the main session sees the change on its next read
- **Destroyed on close**: the side session's persisted log is removed (best effort)

## Known limitations (inherited)

- The side-chat tab does not render approval prompts (mitigated by pinning `never`)
- A closed tab cannot be restored
- Each side chat's first request is roughly the size of the parent's next request; N concurrent side chats multiply that
- GUI restarts lose every side session
- Web platform only (including the Desktop window); no CLI/TUI surface

## Compatibility

| Item | Status |
|---|---|
| DSH version | Verified on `0.2.2-rc.1`; `package.json` declares `engines.dsh: >=0.2.2-rc.1 <0.3.0-0`, so an incompatible host fails at install time instead of at runtime |
| Platform | Tested on macOS; Windows/Linux untested (no platform-specific code, expected to work) |
| UI | Web GUI only (Desktop window or `dsh web`); no CLI/TUI surface |
| Node | `>= 22` (satisfied by DSH's bundled runtime) |
| npm dependencies | **None**: imports no `@deepseek-ai/*` package |
| Browser module dependencies | **None**: requires only `react` (shell-provided) and `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-primitives` (platform seed table, with a built-in fallback) |
| Host services | Requires `agents`/`webServer`/`timer`/`commands`; degrades gracefully when `agentPresets`/`sandboxPolicy`/`approval`/`fileReferences`/`sessionPersistence` are absent |
| Coexistence | **Cannot** be installed alongside upstream `@flyer103/dsh-side-chat` (duplicate routes and tab type) |

Install verification: `dsh plugin --profile web add github:lucyVan/dsh-side-chat-slash` was run in an isolated `DSH_HOME`; dependency install, bundle registration and `--dump-config` composition all succeeded.

## Uninstall

```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop remove dsh-side-chat-slash
```

Then restart DSH.

- Original author [flyer103](https://github.com/flyer103): [dsh-side-chat](https://github.com/flyer103/dsh-side-chat)

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-limitup-widget — A 股涨停直播浮窗（DeepSeek Harness 插件）

> A frame-wide floating **A-share limit-up card** for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (`dsh`).
> 在 DSH 桌面 / Web UI 的 **frame 级浮动层**（`shell.overlay`）里常驻一张深色小卡片：实时显示 A 股涨停 / 炸板 /
> 跌停家数、炸板率、连板高度、昨日涨停溢价、热门题材与自选股；Host 侧提供**同源代理**，并可探活 / 自动拉起
> 随仓库附带的 Python 看板后端。可拖动、可收起、可关闭（关闭后浮层无任何残留，可从左侧边栏底部恢复）。

![涨停直播浮窗卡片](assets/screenshot-card.png)

---

## 1. 它是什么

本插件由 **两半** 组成，安装一个 npm 包即同时生效：

| 半 | 文件 | 职责 |
|---|---|---|
| **Client** | `lib/client.js` | 浏览器端手写模块（无构建步骤，React 由宿主提供），在 `shell.overlay` 注册 `limitup-widget` 卡片，轮询数据并渲染 |
| **Host** | `lib/index.js` | ESM cordis 插件：在 DSH webServer 上挂 `/limitup-widget` 同源前缀路由，反代本地 Python 后端；启动时探活，可选自动拉起后端 |
| **后端** | `dashboard/`（仓库内，单独维护） | Python + Flask + akshare 的 A 股涨停直播看板；默认 `http://127.0.0.1:8000`，不随 npm 包分发 |

插件本体**不采集、不上传任何用户数据**：浏览器只请求同源 `/limitup-widget/api/*`，Host 只访问
`backendUrl`（默认本机 `127.0.0.1:8000`）与本机 Python 进程。

---

## 2. 功能

### 2.1 浮动卡片内容

- **状态**：状态点 + 文案（盘中 / 午休 / 收盘 / 盘前 / 休市 / 过期 / 未连接 / 连接中），数据日 `MM-DD`
  （非当前交易日时显示「回退」标签，悬停可看回退说明）；
- **三大数字**：涨停 / 炸板 / 跌停 家数；
- **次级指标**：炸板率（`炸板 ÷ (涨停 + 炸板)`，后端给出）、连板高度（最高连板数）、昨日涨停均溢价；
- **热门题材 Top5**：题材名 × 涨停家数、最早首封时间；概念映射未建完时后端按「所属行业」兜底并标注「行业」；
- **自选股**：名称 / 代码 / 最新价 / 涨跌幅，涨停显示红色「涨停」徽章，单只获取失败显示「失败」；
- **页脚**：最后刷新时间、刷新、完整看板、收起。

### 2.2 交互

| 操作 | 行为 | 持久化（localStorage） |
|---|---|---|
| 拖动 | 按住头部拖动（4px 位移阈值区分点击与拖动；按钮/输入框上不触发） | `limitup.widget.pos` |
| 收起 | ▾ 收起为小胶囊（「涨停 N · 炸板 N」），**整颗胶囊可点击**展开 | `limitup.widget.collapsed` |
| 关闭 | 头部 ✕ 关闭整卡：浮层内**不渲染任何内容**（无小挂件残留）；左侧边栏底部出现「涨停」恢复按钮，点击恢复整卡；关闭期间轮询继续。关闭状态只在本次页面生命周期内有效，刷新/重启 DSH 后看板自动重新出现（不会永久关没） | 会话内状态 |
| 刷新 | 页脚「刷新」→ `GET /api/refresh` 强制后端刷新一次（可能耗时约 30s） | — |
| 完整看板 | 用**绝对 http 地址**在系统浏览器打开后端看板（桌面端 `dsh-app://` 下相对地址会被静默拒绝；弹窗被拦时自动复制地址并提示） | — |
| 自选 | 输入逗号 / 空格分隔的 6 位代码，保存后立即刷新 | `limitup.watchlist`（与看板页面同一 key） |

### 2.3 轮询与容错

- 轮询间隔由 Host 的 `/limitup-widget/api/config` 下发，默认 **交易时段 60s / 其余 300s**；
  页面隐藏时暂停，`visibilitychange` 回到前台立即补拉一次；
- **数据过期**：红色横幅「数据已过期：自 HH:MM 起未更新」（悬停看原因）；
- **后端未连接**：错误条 + 「重试」；
- 从未成功采集：显示「加载中…」/「暂无数据」；
- 所有服务端字符串渲染前经 `esc()` 转义（React 本身也会转义），无 `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`；
  定时器、`visibilitychange` 监听、样式标签在卸载时全部清理。

### 2.4 Host 侧同源代理

浏览器只认 `/limitup-widget` 前缀，避免 CORS / 混合内容问题：

| 路由（GET/HEAD） | 行为 |
|---|---|
| `/limitup-widget/` | 302 到 `backendUrl/`（完整看板） |
| `/limitup-widget/api/config` | 返回 `backendUrl`、`backendPageUrl`、`pollTradingMs`、`pollIdleMs`、`autostart` |
| `/limitup-widget/api/snapshot` | 反代后端 `/api/snapshot`（12s 超时） |
| `/limitup-widget/api/refresh` | 反代后端 `/api/refresh`（45s 超时） |
| `/limitup-widget/api/health` | 反代后端 `/api/health`（6s 超时） |
| 其它路径 / 非 GET·HEAD | 404 / 405 |
| 后端不可达 | 502 `{"ok":false,"error":"backend_unreachable",...}`，并限频尝试补拉后端 |

**后端自动拉起（可选）**：插件加载时探活 `backendUrl/api/health`。若健康检查失败、`autostart` 为 true 且
`script` 非空，则用 `pythonBin script` 拉起后端（环境对齐 `HOST=127.0.0.1`、`PORT`=backendUrl 端口、
`TZ=Asia/Shanghai`），最多等待 `startupTimeoutMs`；**只会在自己拉起过进程时于卸载时终止它，
已在运行的后端永远不会被插件杀掉**。

---

## 3. 安装

### 3.1 环境要求

- DeepSeek Harness `>=0.2.0-rc.2 <0.3.0`（桌面版或 Web profile），Node.js ≥ 20；
- 后端需要 Python ≥ 3.9（推荐 3.10+）与可访问东方财富数据源的网络（akshare 免费接口，无需 API key）。

### 3.2 安装插件

**方式 A：插件市场 / Settings → Plugins**（上架后推荐）

在 DSH 的 **设置 → 插件**（市场 / Discover）里搜索 `dsh-limitup-widget` 一键安装。
桌面版 profile 由 Electron 应用管理，请通过设置界面安装，不要手动改桌面 profile。

**方式 B：CLI（Web / 自定义 profile）**

```sh
# 从 npm（如果已发布）
dsh plugin add dsh-limitup-widget
# 或显式指定 profile
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-limitup-widget

# 从 GitHub 源码（npm 未发布时同样可用）
dsh plugin --profile web add github:LusJourney/dsh-limitup-widget

# 从本地 tarball
dsh plugin --profile web add /absolute/path/to/dsh-limitup-widget-0.2.0.tgz
```

安装后**重启 DSH 应用**（新 bundle 才会进入正在运行的 roster），右下角应出现「涨停直播」卡片。

> 市场索引：DSH `0.2.1+` 的 **插件 → Discover → Index sources** 可添加
> `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/dsh-plugin-catalog/index.json`，之后即可搜索到本插件。

### 3.3 准备后端（二选一）

**A. 手动运行（推荐先跑通）**

```sh
git clone https://github.com/LusJourney/dsh-limitup-widget.git
cd dsh-limitup-widget/dashboard
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate            # Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
python app.py                        # → http://127.0.0.1:8000
```

首次启动约 10–20 秒出第一版快照（概念映射在后台慢慢建，期间题材按行业兜底）；依赖与接口说明见
[`dashboard/README.md`](dashboard/README.md)。

**B. 交给插件自动拉起**

在 profile 的 `cordis.patch.yml` 里写同 id 配置（完整示例见下一节），把 `pythonBin` 指向
**后端 venv 的 python 绝对路径**、`script` 指向 **`dashboard/app.py` 绝对路径**。插件启动时若后端没起会自动拉起；
反之 `script: ''` 时只探活、不拉起（本包默认配置即如此）。

### 3.4 验证

```sh
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/health
# 期望：{"ok":true,...}
```

重启 DSH 后，右下角出现卡片即安装成功；Host 日志里可见 `[limitup-widget] host plugin loaded`。

---

## 4. 配置

默认值在包内 `cordis.patch.yml` 的 `insert.config` 中（Host 行 `id: limitup-widget`）。
**用户覆盖方式**：在 profile 的 `cordis.patch.yml` 追加同 `id` 的 patch 条目。
⚠️ 覆盖会**替换整个 config 对象，请写全量字段**：

```yaml
- id: limitup-widget
  name: dsh-limitup-widget
  config:
    backendUrl: http://127.0.0.1:8000
    autostart: true
    pythonBin: /absolute/path/to/dashboard/.venv/bin/python
    script: /absolute/path/to/dashboard/app.py
    startupTimeoutMs: 45000
    pollTradingMs: 60000
    pollIdleMs: 300000
```

| 字段 | 默认 | 允许范围 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `backendUrl` | `http://127.0.0.1:8000` | 任意 `http(s)` URL | 后端根地址；端口同时用于自动拉起子进程的 `PORT` |
| `autostart` | `true` | 布尔 | 探活失败且 `script` 非空时是否拉起后端 |
| `pythonBin` | `python3` | 非空字符串 | 拉起后端用的 Python（建议后端 venv 内解释器的绝对路径） |
| `script` | `''`（空） | 字符串 | `app.py` 绝对路径；为空则只探活、不拉起 |
| `startupTimeoutMs` | `45000` | 1000–300000 | 拉起后等待健康的超时 |
| `pollTradingMs` | `60000` | 15000–600000 | 交易时段客户端轮询间隔 |
| `pollIdleMs` | `300000` | 30000–3600000 | 非交易时段客户端轮询间隔 |

---

## 5. 目录结构

```
dsh-limitup-widget/
├── package.json          # dsh.bundle.patch + dsh.client(platform: web) 清单
├── cordis.patch.yml      # bundle patch：insert Host 行 limitup-widget + 默认 config
├── lib/
│   ├── index.js          # Host：/limitup-widget 路由 + 后端探活/自动拉起
│   └── client.js         # Client：shell.overlay 浮动卡片（拖动/收起/关闭/轮询）
├── tests/
│   ├── test-loader.mjs   # 假 window.__ModuleLoader__ / React：加载、注册、渲染、转义
│   └── test-node-plugin.mjs  # 假 ctx/webServer：路由映射、autostart 决策矩阵
├── assets/
│   ├── icon-180.png      # 市场图标（180×180）
│   └── screenshot-card.png
├── dashboard/            # Python 看板后端（GitHub 仓库内，不在 npm tarball 中）
├── screenshots.json      # 市场店铺截图声明
├── README.md
└── LICENSE
```

`npm pack` 生成的 tarball 只包含插件本体（`lib/`、`cordis.patch.yml`、`README.md`、`LICENSE`、`assets/`、
`screenshots.json`）；需要后端源码请从 GitHub 仓库获取 `dashboard/`。

---

## 6. 开发与验证（不启动 DSH 也能跑）

```sh
node --check lib/index.js
node --check lib/client.js
node tests/test-loader.mjs      # 假 ModuleLoader/React：加载、注册 shell.overlay、渲染、XSS 转义
node tests/test-node-plugin.mjs # 假 ctx/webServer：路由映射、autostart 决策
npm test                        # 上面两个测试
```

---

## 7. 故障排查

- **卡片不出现**：确认插件已装进当前 profile 并**重启** DSH；Host 日志有
  `[limitup-widget] host plugin loaded` 说明 Host 半已加载。浏览器 console 若报
  `slot entry crashed in 'shell.overlay'`，用 `node --check lib/client.js` 检查语法。
- **卡片显示「后端未连接」**：`curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/health` 应返回 `{"ok":true,...}`。
  未启动且未配置自动拉起时，手动 `python app.py`；检查 `pythonBin` / `script` 是否为绝对路径且可执行。
- **关闭后找不到卡片**：看左侧边栏底部（Settings 旁边）的「涨停」小按钮，点一下恢复；刷新窗口（Cmd+R）或重启 DSH 也会让看板重新出现；
  清除 localStorage 的 `limitup.widget.hidden` 与 `limitup.widget.pos` 后刷新页面。
- **8000 端口被占用**：改 `backendUrl`（自动拉起的 `PORT` 会取自 URL 端口），或让已有后端先运行。
- **健康检查一直超时**：首次启动 akshare 拉数据可能较慢，可调大 `startupTimeoutMs`。
  插件只在**自己拉起**进程后才会在卸载时终止它，已在运行的后端不会被杀。
- **数据过期红色横幅**：后端数据源异常 / 被限流，保留上一份好数据并标 stale；
  打开完整看板看后端日志与数据源状态。
- **完整看板点了没反应**：桌面端会用系统默认浏览器打开 `backendUrl`；普通浏览器弹窗被拦时插件会复制
  看板地址到剪贴板并提示。
- **Python 环境**：不要用 **DSH 内置 runtime 的 python** 建后端 venv（hardened runtime 签名会拒绝 pip
  安装的 C 扩展，numpy 报 *different Team IDs*）。请用系统 / Homebrew / python.org 的 Python 3.9+。

---

## 8. 数据、隐私与免责声明

- 插件只读取 DSH 前端数据并请求**同源** `/limitup-widget/*`；Host 只访问配置的 `backendUrl` 与本机 Python；
  无遥测、无第三方请求、不读取任何凭据；
- 持久化仅使用 localStorage 的 4 个 key：`limitup.widget.pos`、`limitup.widget.collapsed`、
  `limitup.widget.hidden`、`limitup.watchlist`；
- 数据来自后端通过 **akshare 免费公开接口**抓取的东方财富数据，可能存在延迟、缺失或错误；
- 本插件只做数据展示与提醒，**不构成任何投资建议**，据此交易的风险由使用者自行承担。

## 9. License

[MIT](LICENSE) © 2026 Luka Zhao (LusJourney)

---

## English summary

`dsh-limitup-widget` is a DeepSeek Harness plugin that mounts a floating A-share limit-up card in the
frame-level overlay (`shell.overlay`). It shows limit-up / broken-board / limit-down counts, break rate,
consecutive-board height, previous-day limit-up premium, the top 5 themes and a localStorage-backed watchlist.
The card can be dragged (position persisted), collapsed into a pill, or closed entirely (no floating remnant; while closed a small 涨停 restore button appears at the sidebar footer, and a refresh brings the card back)
button; all three states persist across reloads. Polling runs every 60 s during A-share trading hours and
every 300 s otherwise, pauses when the page is hidden and catches up on `visibilitychange`. The Host half
exposes a same-origin proxy under `/limitup-widget/api/*`, health-checks the backend and can optionally spawn
`python app.py` (only the child it spawned is ever stopped). The Python dashboard backend lives in the
GitHub repository under `dashboard/` and is not bundled in the npm tarball. MIT licensed.

decision.reason: Held for package or companion artifact mapping. MIT, explicit Git installation and DSH at least 0.2.0-rc.2 below 0.3.0. Native market-data panel/proxy is present; npm record lacks gitHead. Patch enables companion autostart with python3, an empty script field and localhost:8000, leaving the Python service/artifact installation chain unresolved. No lifecycle hook. No candidate code or lifecycle hooks were executed; runtime safety and compatibility are unproven.

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
Tool Ultra
On-demand tool loading for DeepSeek Harness — every tool as a directory, loaded only when an agent asks.

English · 中文

--- ## What It Is Tool Ultra is an All-in-One tool-plugin product for DeepSeek Harness, and an important component of [Swiftnest](https://github.com/lvy-jsd/swiftnest). Its goal is one coherent tool product across everyday tasks, web/MCP services, media and device capabilities. The small core and replaceable extension packages are its internal architecture; the product is more than a tool-directory browser. Tools are browsable as a directory (category → group → tool), searchable by intent and loaded on demand, keeping unneeded schemas out of the model's context. Savings depend on catalog size, discovery/load steps and provider caching: compare per-request schemas, total task tokens and task success separately. Broad capability does not mean every external service or upload is enabled by default. The current preview is distributed as source and modular packages; Swiftnest builds a pinned source commit. An AI can install and configure the required modules. The published-package quick-start syntax below applies when those package versions are available on npm; it is not a claim that the renamed 0.5.0 packages have already been published. > **Renamed.** This project was `dsh-tool-manager`. Version 0.5.0 renames every > package from `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager-` to `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-` > (the core is `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core`). Nothing else changes: the entry > tools, the `toolCatalog` service (now also provided as `toolUltra`), the hooks, > the config and the state directory `/tool-manager/` stay the same. > An existing profile can keep `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager`: from 0.5.0 it only > re-exports the new core. Older extension releases keep working with the new core. ## Quick start ```sh # 1. install the core plus the rule-based classifier (optional but recommended) dsh plugin --profile web add @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-rules # 2. restart DSH, then ask the agent: "what tools do you have?" # it answers with tools_ls("/") — a directory, not 200 tool schemas # 3. want the UI? add the panel, then open Settings → "Tool manager" dsh plugin --profile web add @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-panel ``` > **Install the scoped `@lvy-jsd/…` packages.** The unscoped `dsh-tool-manager` > on npm is a different project. Do not install both: each one narrows which > tools an agent can see, so together they hide tools from each other. On a fresh install every group is `uncategorized` until a classifier is installed — the tools are still browsable and loadable, only the categories are missing. See [Extending](#extending) to write your own classifier. `tools_load(["web"])` also accepts bare names: try registered `pack:` → `cap:` → `device:` namespaces, first non-empty match only, then normal directory lookup; explicit prefixes keep their behavior and plugin ownership. ## Packages | Package | What it does | |---|---| | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-core) | Core: directory, `tools_ls` / `tools_load` / `tools_unload`, per-agent allowlist, the `toolCatalog` extension service, plus intent retrieval + routing (`tools_find` / `tools_route` / `skills_find` / `skills_route`, BM25 with a Rust sidecar). Without extensions every group is `uncategorized`. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-rules`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-rules) | Places groups into categories from built-in rules and your config overrides. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-risk-gate`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-risk-gate) | Confirms loading high-risk tools through the DSH approval channel, with a per-session allowlist. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-persist`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-persist) | Keeps loaded tools across a DSH restart, one state file per session. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-panel`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-panel) | Web panel: browse the tree, see each live session's loaded tools and token cost, load/unload from the UI, edit the always-on and high-risk lists, edit one tool's metadata, exempt one session. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-llm`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-llm) | Places groups with a small model, one request per group, cached by a hash of the group and its tool descriptions. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-capability-bridge`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-capability-bridge) | Load a named bundle of tools in one call: `tools_load(["cap:android-debug"])`. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-attribution-scan`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-attribution-scan) | Group tools by the plugin package whose source defines them. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-essentials`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-essentials) | Native tool pack, no API keys: time zones and date math, a calculator with units (mathjs), weather (Open-Meteo), place search (Nominatim), Wikipedia. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-web`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-web) | Native tool pack: `web_read` turns a page into clean Markdown (Readability + turndown), `web_links` lists its links. Refuses private addresses by default. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-mcp`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-mcp) | MCP presets through DSH's MCP client: memory, sequential thinking, Context7, Playwright and filesystem start without keys; GitHub, SearXNG, Brave, Tavily, Firecrawl, Notion and AMap start once their key is set. `mcp_presets` shows the status. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-media`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-media) | Native tool pack, no API keys: images, music and video made from code. `html_render` designs an image in HTML/CSS (no browser) or turns its CSS animations into a GIF, `svg_render` turns an SVG drawing into PNG/JPEG/WebP, `chart_render` draws a Vega-Lite chart, `music_render` plays a score with real recorded instruments (SoundFont, mastered) and saves WAV and MIDI, `video_render` makes an MP4 from CSS-animated HTML, SVG or photo scenes with transitions, captions and a soundtrack (host ffmpeg), `audio_transcribe` turns speech into timestamped text with local SenseVoice / Whisper models, with who speaks when, emotions and sounds such as laughter, `video_understand` reads a video as a timestamped storyboard image plus its transcript. External links and data URLs are refused. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-gc`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-gc) | Artifact and media garbage collection: date-partitioned storage management (`[YYYY-MM-DD]`), retention sweeps, and LRU capacity eviction. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-db`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-db) | In-memory OLAP analytics via embedded DuckDB: query CSV, Parquet, and JSON datasets directly via SQL without context inflation. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-office`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-office) | Office documents pack: Word (.docx) text extraction, Excel (.xlsx) read/write, and PDF document metadata inspection. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-devices`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-devices) | Device namespace: Swiftnest device tools under `/device/`, loadable as `device:current`, `device:all` or `device:`, with offline devices marked. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager-dsbot-entry`](packages/dsh-tool-manager-dsbot-entry) | Deprecated, no longer released. A "Tool manager" row in the ds-bot settings dialog that opens the panel. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager`](packages/dsh-tool-manager) | The old core name: re-exports `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core` so existing profiles keep working. | | [`@lvy-jsd/create-dsh-tool-ultra-plugin`](packages/create-dsh-tool-ultra-plugin) | Scaffold your own extension: `npm create @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-plugin@latest my-ext -- --type classifier`. | See [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md) for the design. ## Extending Every feature beyond the core is an ordinary plugin using the `toolCatalog` service, and the bundled `classifier-rules` package is written exactly as a third party would write it. Four extension points: | Point | For | |---|---| | `registerClassifier({ name, priority, group?, categorize? })` | placing tools into groups and groups into categories | | `annotate(match, { group?, category?, risk?, summary? })` | runtime metadata; `package.json` `dsh.toolCatalog` does the same without code | | `registerVisibilityFilter({ name, filter(agent, names) })` | narrowing what one agent may see — can only remove names | | `registerTargetResolver({ name, prefix, resolve })` | owning a target prefix, e.g. `cap:` | | `registerRiskGate` / `registerStateProvider` | confirming high-risk loads / keeping state across a restart | Hooks are plain events: `tool-catalog/before-load` (throw to veto), `after-load`, `before-unload`, `after-unload`, `before-rebuild`, `after-rebuild`, `state-changed`. Start from a generated package — it comes with a passing test: ```sh npm create @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-plugin@latest my-ext -- --type classifier cd my-ext && npm test ``` Two worked examples live in [`examples/`](examples), and the full interface list is in the core README and [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md) §11. ## Development Every package is written in TypeScript (`src/`) and compiled to `lib/` (JavaScript plus `.d.ts` type declarations); `lib/` is build output and not committed. The root `tsconfig.json` lists the packages (project references); the two browser halves (`client.ts`) have their own `tsconfig.client.json`, because DSH loads them as classic scripts, not modules. ```sh npm install # also links your local DSH host packages (scripts/link-host.mjs) npm run build # src/*.ts -> lib/*.js + lib/*.d.ts npm run typecheck # strict type check (tsc -b; writes lib/ too, references need it) node --test test/unit/*.test.mjs # pure catalog and registry tests (needs a build) node test/e2e.mjs # boots throwaway DSH instances; never touches your profile ``` Host packages (`@deepseek-ai/*`) are peers and are never installed from the registry (`.npmrc` sets `legacy-peer-deps`): a registry copy next to the plugin would shadow the DSH you actually run. `npm install` links them from `$DSH_APP` (default `~/.local/share/deepseek-harness/app`) instead. ## License Apache-2.0 — see [LICENSE](LICENSE). Releases before Tool Ultra (`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager*`) were MIT.

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
Tool Ultra
On-demand tool loading for DeepSeek Harness — every tool as a directory, loaded only when an agent asks.

English · 中文

--- ## What It Is Tool Ultra is an All-in-One tool-plugin product for DeepSeek Harness, and an important component of [Swiftnest](https://github.com/lvy-jsd/swiftnest). Its goal is one coherent tool product across everyday tasks, web/MCP services, media and device capabilities. The small core and replaceable extension packages are its internal architecture; the product is more than a tool-directory browser. Tools are browsable as a directory (category → group → tool), searchable by intent and loaded on demand, keeping unneeded schemas out of the model's context. Savings depend on catalog size, discovery/load steps and provider caching: compare per-request schemas, total task tokens and task success separately. Broad capability does not mean every external service or upload is enabled by default. The current preview is distributed as source and modular packages; Swiftnest builds a pinned source commit. An AI can install and configure the required modules. The published-package quick-start syntax below applies when those package versions are available on npm; it is not a claim that the renamed 0.5.0 packages have already been published. > **Renamed.** This project was `dsh-tool-manager`. Version 0.5.0 renames every > package from `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager-` to `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-` > (the core is `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core`). Nothing else changes: the entry > tools, the `toolCatalog` service (now also provided as `toolUltra`), the hooks, > the config and the state directory `/tool-manager/` stay the same. > An existing profile can keep `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager`: from 0.5.0 it only > re-exports the new core. Older extension releases keep working with the new core. ## Quick start ```sh # 1. install the core plus the rule-based classifier (optional but recommended) dsh plugin --profile web add @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-rules # 2. restart DSH, then ask the agent: "what tools do you have?" # it answers with tools_ls("/") — a directory, not 200 tool schemas # 3. want the UI? add the panel, then open Settings → "Tool manager" dsh plugin --profile web add @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-panel ``` > **Install the scoped `@lvy-jsd/…` packages.** The unscoped `dsh-tool-manager` > on npm is a different project. Do not install both: each one narrows which > tools an agent can see, so together they hide tools from each other. On a fresh install every group is `uncategorized` until a classifier is installed — the tools are still browsable and loadable, only the categories are missing. See [Extending](#extending) to write your own classifier. `tools_load(["web"])` also accepts bare names: try registered `pack:` → `cap:` → `device:` namespaces, first non-empty match only, then normal directory lookup; explicit prefixes keep their behavior and plugin ownership. ## Packages | Package | What it does | |---|---| | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-core) | Core: directory, `tools_ls` / `tools_load` / `tools_unload`, per-agent allowlist, the `toolCatalog` extension service, plus intent retrieval + routing (`tools_find` / `tools_route` / `skills_find` / `skills_route`, BM25 with a Rust sidecar). Without extensions every group is `uncategorized`. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-rules`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-rules) | Places groups into categories from built-in rules and your config overrides. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-risk-gate`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-risk-gate) | Confirms loading high-risk tools through the DSH approval channel, with a per-session allowlist. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-persist`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-persist) | Keeps loaded tools across a DSH restart, one state file per session. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-panel`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-panel) | Web panel: browse the tree, see each live session's loaded tools and token cost, load/unload from the UI, edit the always-on and high-risk lists, edit one tool's metadata, exempt one session. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-llm`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-llm) | Places groups with a small model, one request per group, cached by a hash of the group and its tool descriptions. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-capability-bridge`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-capability-bridge) | Load a named bundle of tools in one call: `tools_load(["cap:android-debug"])`. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-attribution-scan`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-attribution-scan) | Group tools by the plugin package whose source defines them. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-essentials`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-essentials) | Native tool pack, no API keys: time zones and date math, a calculator with units (mathjs), weather (Open-Meteo), place search (Nominatim), Wikipedia. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-web`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-web) | Native tool pack: `web_read` turns a page into clean Markdown (Readability + turndown), `web_links` lists its links. Refuses private addresses by default. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-mcp`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-mcp) | MCP presets through DSH's MCP client: memory, sequential thinking, Context7, Playwright and filesystem start without keys; GitHub, SearXNG, Brave, Tavily, Firecrawl, Notion and AMap start once their key is set. `mcp_presets` shows the status. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-media`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-media) | Native tool pack, no API keys: images, music and video made from code. `html_render` designs an image in HTML/CSS (no browser) or turns its CSS animations into a GIF, `svg_render` turns an SVG drawing into PNG/JPEG/WebP, `chart_render` draws a Vega-Lite chart, `music_render` plays a score with real recorded instruments (SoundFont, mastered) and saves WAV and MIDI, `video_render` makes an MP4 from CSS-animated HTML, SVG or photo scenes with transitions, captions and a soundtrack (host ffmpeg), `audio_transcribe` turns speech into timestamped text with local SenseVoice / Whisper models, with who speaks when, emotions and sounds such as laughter, `video_understand` reads a video as a timestamped storyboard image plus its transcript. External links and data URLs are refused. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-gc`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-gc) | Artifact and media garbage collection: date-partitioned storage management (`[YYYY-MM-DD]`), retention sweeps, and LRU capacity eviction. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-db`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-db) | In-memory OLAP analytics via embedded DuckDB: query CSV, Parquet, and JSON datasets directly via SQL without context inflation. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-office`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-office) | Office documents pack: Word (.docx) text extraction, Excel (.xlsx) read/write, and PDF document metadata inspection. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-devices`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-devices) | Device namespace: Swiftnest device tools under `/device/`, loadable as `device:current`, `device:all` or `device:`, with offline devices marked. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager-dsbot-entry`](packages/dsh-tool-manager-dsbot-entry) | Deprecated, no longer released. A "Tool manager" row in the ds-bot settings dialog that opens the panel. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager`](packages/dsh-tool-manager) | The old core name: re-exports `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core` so existing profiles keep working. | | [`@lvy-jsd/create-dsh-tool-ultra-plugin`](packages/create-dsh-tool-ultra-plugin) | Scaffold your own extension: `npm create @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-plugin@latest my-ext -- --type classifier`. | See [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md) for the design. ## Extending Every feature beyond the core is an ordinary plugin using the `toolCatalog` service, and the bundled `classifier-rules` package is written exactly as a third party would write it. Four extension points: | Point | For | |---|---| | `registerClassifier({ name, priority, group?, categorize? })` | placing tools into groups and groups into categories | | `annotate(match, { group?, category?, risk?, summary? })` | runtime metadata; `package.json` `dsh.toolCatalog` does the same without code | | `registerVisibilityFilter({ name, filter(agent, names) })` | narrowing what one agent may see — can only remove names | | `registerTargetResolver({ name, prefix, resolve })` | owning a target prefix, e.g. `cap:` | | `registerRiskGate` / `registerStateProvider` | confirming high-risk loads / keeping state across a restart | Hooks are plain events: `tool-catalog/before-load` (throw to veto), `after-load`, `before-unload`, `after-unload`, `before-rebuild`, `after-rebuild`, `state-changed`. Start from a generated package — it comes with a passing test: ```sh npm create @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-plugin@latest my-ext -- --type classifier cd my-ext && npm test ``` Two worked examples live in [`examples/`](examples), and the full interface list is in the core README and [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md) §11. ## Development Every package is written in TypeScript (`src/`) and compiled to `lib/` (JavaScript plus `.d.ts` type declarations); `lib/` is build output and not committed. The root `tsconfig.json` lists the packages (project references); the two browser halves (`client.ts`) have their own `tsconfig.client.json`, because DSH loads them as classic scripts, not modules. ```sh npm install # also links your local DSH host packages (scripts/link-host.mjs) npm run build # src/*.ts -> lib/*.js + lib/*.d.ts npm run typecheck # strict type check (tsc -b; writes lib/ too, references need it) node --test test/unit/*.test.mjs # pure catalog and registry tests (needs a build) node test/e2e.mjs # boots throwaway DSH instances; never touches your profile ``` Host packages (`@deepseek-ai/*`) are peers and are never installed from the registry (`.npmrc` sets `legacy-peer-deps`): a registry copy next to the plugin would shadow the DSH you actually run. `npm install` links them from `$DSH_APP` (default `~/.local/share/deepseek-harness/app`) instead. ## License Apache-2.0 — see [LICENSE](LICENSE). Releases before Tool Ultra (`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager*`) were MIT.

# @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager-dsbot-entry > **Deprecated.** This entry targets the ds-bot settings dialog and is no longer released. It still finds the panel under its new name, `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-panel`. Adds a **Tool manager** row (工具管理 in Chinese) to the [ds-bot](https://www.npmjs.com/package/ds-bot) settings dialog. Clicking it shows the [`dsh-tool-ultra-panel`](../dsh-tool-ultra-panel) panel inside the dialog, in ds-bot's own colors. Use it when your DSH web UI runs in the ds-bot layout, where DSH's own Settings page (and the panel's section in it) is one step further away (Bot settings → Harness settings → Tool manager). ## Install Needs `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-panel` (it serves the data and the panel component). ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-panel @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager-dsbot-entry ``` ## How it works, and why it is safe to break ds-bot's settings dialog has a fixed page list and no extension point, so this plugin adds its row **from the outside** and changes no ds-bot code: - A component in the host's always-mounted `shell.overlay` slot watches the document with a `MutationObserver`. - When a `.bt-settings` dialog with the expected nav appears, it inserts one row (ds-bot's own `.bt-settings-item` class) above "Harness settings", and one host element over the page area. The panel renders into it through a React portal; clicking any other row closes it. - The panel's `--dsw-alias-*` variables are mapped onto ds-bot's `--bt-*` variables inside that host, so it follows ds-bot's theme. - Copy comes from the panel's dictionaries and follows the DSH interface language. If ds-bot changes its dialog markup, the row simply does not appear; nothing else is affected, and the panel stays available in DSH's Settings page. The better long-term fix is a settings-page extension point in ds-bot; when one exists, this plugin should switch to it. ## License Apache-2.0

Tool Ultra
On-demand tool loading for DeepSeek Harness — every tool as a directory, loaded only when an agent asks.

English · 中文

--- ## What It Is Tool Ultra is an All-in-One tool-plugin product for DeepSeek Harness, and an important component of [Swiftnest](https://github.com/lvy-jsd/swiftnest). Its goal is one coherent tool product across everyday tasks, web/MCP services, media and device capabilities. The small core and replaceable extension packages are its internal architecture; the product is more than a tool-directory browser. Tools are browsable as a directory (category → group → tool), searchable by intent and loaded on demand, keeping unneeded schemas out of the model's context. Savings depend on catalog size, discovery/load steps and provider caching: compare per-request schemas, total task tokens and task success separately. Broad capability does not mean every external service or upload is enabled by default. The current preview is distributed as source and modular packages; Swiftnest builds a pinned source commit. An AI can install and configure the required modules. The published-package quick-start syntax below applies when those package versions are available on npm; it is not a claim that the renamed 0.5.0 packages have already been published. > **Renamed.** This project was `dsh-tool-manager`. Version 0.5.0 renames every > package from `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager-` to `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-` > (the core is `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core`). Nothing else changes: the entry > tools, the `toolCatalog` service (now also provided as `toolUltra`), the hooks, > the config and the state directory `/tool-manager/` stay the same. > An existing profile can keep `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager`: from 0.5.0 it only > re-exports the new core. Older extension releases keep working with the new core. ## Quick start ```sh # 1. install the core plus the rule-based classifier (optional but recommended) dsh plugin --profile web add @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-rules # 2. restart DSH, then ask the agent: "what tools do you have?" # it answers with tools_ls("/") — a directory, not 200 tool schemas # 3. want the UI? add the panel, then open Settings → "Tool manager" dsh plugin --profile web add @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-panel ``` > **Install the scoped `@lvy-jsd/…` packages.** The unscoped `dsh-tool-manager` > on npm is a different project. Do not install both: each one narrows which > tools an agent can see, so together they hide tools from each other. On a fresh install every group is `uncategorized` until a classifier is installed — the tools are still browsable and loadable, only the categories are missing. See [Extending](#extending) to write your own classifier. `tools_load(["web"])` also accepts bare names: try registered `pack:` → `cap:` → `device:` namespaces, first non-empty match only, then normal directory lookup; explicit prefixes keep their behavior and plugin ownership. ## Packages | Package | What it does | |---|---| | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-core) | Core: directory, `tools_ls` / `tools_load` / `tools_unload`, per-agent allowlist, the `toolCatalog` extension service, plus intent retrieval + routing (`tools_find` / `tools_route` / `skills_find` / `skills_route`, BM25 with a Rust sidecar). Without extensions every group is `uncategorized`. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-rules`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-rules) | Places groups into categories from built-in rules and your config overrides. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-risk-gate`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-risk-gate) | Confirms loading high-risk tools through the DSH approval channel, with a per-session allowlist. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-persist`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-persist) | Keeps loaded tools across a DSH restart, one state file per session. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-panel`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-panel) | Web panel: browse the tree, see each live session's loaded tools and token cost, load/unload from the UI, edit the always-on and high-risk lists, edit one tool's metadata, exempt one session. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-llm`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-llm) | Places groups with a small model, one request per group, cached by a hash of the group and its tool descriptions. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-capability-bridge`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-capability-bridge) | Load a named bundle of tools in one call: `tools_load(["cap:android-debug"])`. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-attribution-scan`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-attribution-scan) | Group tools by the plugin package whose source defines them. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-essentials`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-essentials) | Native tool pack, no API keys: time zones and date math, a calculator with units (mathjs), weather (Open-Meteo), place search (Nominatim), Wikipedia. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-web`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-web) | Native tool pack: `web_read` turns a page into clean Markdown (Readability + turndown), `web_links` lists its links. Refuses private addresses by default. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-mcp`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-mcp) | MCP presets through DSH's MCP client: memory, sequential thinking, Context7, Playwright and filesystem start without keys; GitHub, SearXNG, Brave, Tavily, Firecrawl, Notion and AMap start once their key is set. `mcp_presets` shows the status. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-media`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-media) | Native tool pack, no API keys: images, music and video made from code. `html_render` designs an image in HTML/CSS (no browser) or turns its CSS animations into a GIF, `svg_render` turns an SVG drawing into PNG/JPEG/WebP, `chart_render` draws a Vega-Lite chart, `music_render` plays a score with real recorded instruments (SoundFont, mastered) and saves WAV and MIDI, `video_render` makes an MP4 from CSS-animated HTML, SVG or photo scenes with transitions, captions and a soundtrack (host ffmpeg), `audio_transcribe` turns speech into timestamped text with local SenseVoice / Whisper models, with who speaks when, emotions and sounds such as laughter, `video_understand` reads a video as a timestamped storyboard image plus its transcript. External links and data URLs are refused. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-gc`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-gc) | Artifact and media garbage collection: date-partitioned storage management (`[YYYY-MM-DD]`), retention sweeps, and LRU capacity eviction. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-db`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-db) | In-memory OLAP analytics via embedded DuckDB: query CSV, Parquet, and JSON datasets directly via SQL without context inflation. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-office`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-office) | Office documents pack: Word (.docx) text extraction, Excel (.xlsx) read/write, and PDF document metadata inspection. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-devices`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-devices) | Device namespace: Swiftnest device tools under `/device/`, loadable as `device:current`, `device:all` or `device:`, with offline devices marked. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager-dsbot-entry`](packages/dsh-tool-manager-dsbot-entry) | Deprecated, no longer released. A "Tool manager" row in the ds-bot settings dialog that opens the panel. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager`](packages/dsh-tool-manager) | The old core name: re-exports `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core` so existing profiles keep working. | | [`@lvy-jsd/create-dsh-tool-ultra-plugin`](packages/create-dsh-tool-ultra-plugin) | Scaffold your own extension: `npm create @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-plugin@latest my-ext -- --type classifier`. | See [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md) for the design. ## Extending Every feature beyond the core is an ordinary plugin using the `toolCatalog` service, and the bundled `classifier-rules` package is written exactly as a third party would write it. Four extension points: | Point | For | |---|---| | `registerClassifier({ name, priority, group?, categorize? })` | placing tools into groups and groups into categories | | `annotate(match, { group?, category?, risk?, summary? })` | runtime metadata; `package.json` `dsh.toolCatalog` does the same without code | | `registerVisibilityFilter({ name, filter(agent, names) })` | narrowing what one agent may see — can only remove names | | `registerTargetResolver({ name, prefix, resolve })` | owning a target prefix, e.g. `cap:` | | `registerRiskGate` / `registerStateProvider` | confirming high-risk loads / keeping state across a restart | Hooks are plain events: `tool-catalog/before-load` (throw to veto), `after-load`, `before-unload`, `after-unload`, `before-rebuild`, `after-rebuild`, `state-changed`. Start from a generated package — it comes with a passing test: ```sh npm create @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-plugin@latest my-ext -- --type classifier cd my-ext && npm test ``` Two worked examples live in [`examples/`](examples), and the full interface list is in the core README and [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md) §11. ## Development Every package is written in TypeScript (`src/`) and compiled to `lib/` (JavaScript plus `.d.ts` type declarations); `lib/` is build output and not committed. The root `tsconfig.json` lists the packages (project references); the two browser halves (`client.ts`) have their own `tsconfig.client.json`, because DSH loads them as classic scripts, not modules. ```sh npm install # also links your local DSH host packages (scripts/link-host.mjs) npm run build # src/*.ts -> lib/*.js + lib/*.d.ts npm run typecheck # strict type check (tsc -b; writes lib/ too, references need it) node --test test/unit/*.test.mjs # pure catalog and registry tests (needs a build) node test/e2e.mjs # boots throwaway DSH instances; never touches your profile ``` Host packages (`@deepseek-ai/*`) are peers and are never installed from the registry (`.npmrc` sets `legacy-peer-deps`): a registry copy next to the plugin would shadow the DSH you actually run. `npm install` links them from `$DSH_APP` (default `~/.local/share/deepseek-harness/app`) instead. ## License Apache-2.0 — see [LICENSE](LICENSE). Releases before Tool Ultra (`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager*`) were MIT.

# @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager **Renamed to [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core`](../dsh-tool-ultra-core)**, part of Tool Ultra. This package only re-exports the new one, so a DSH profile that already loads `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager` keeps its loader entry, its config and its state (`/tool-manager/`) after an update. New installs should use: ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-rules ``` Do not load both this package and `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core` in one profile: they are the same plugin. The extensions were renamed the same way (`dsh-tool-manager-` → `dsh-tool-ultra-`). Their last `dsh-tool-manager-*` releases keep working with the new core, because they talk to it through the unchanged `toolCatalog` service. ## License Apache-2.0. Releases up to 0.4.1 were MIT.

Tool Ultra
On-demand tool loading for DeepSeek Harness — every tool as a directory, loaded only when an agent asks.

English · 中文

--- ## What It Is Tool Ultra is an All-in-One tool-plugin product for DeepSeek Harness, and an important component of [Swiftnest](https://github.com/lvy-jsd/swiftnest). Its goal is one coherent tool product across everyday tasks, web/MCP services, media and device capabilities. The small core and replaceable extension packages are its internal architecture; the product is more than a tool-directory browser. Tools are browsable as a directory (category → group → tool), searchable by intent and loaded on demand, keeping unneeded schemas out of the model's context. Savings depend on catalog size, discovery/load steps and provider caching: compare per-request schemas, total task tokens and task success separately. Broad capability does not mean every external service or upload is enabled by default. The current preview is distributed as source and modular packages; Swiftnest builds a pinned source commit. An AI can install and configure the required modules. The published-package quick-start syntax below applies when those package versions are available on npm; it is not a claim that the renamed 0.5.0 packages have already been published. > **Renamed.** This project was `dsh-tool-manager`. Version 0.5.0 renames every > package from `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager-` to `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-` > (the core is `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core`). Nothing else changes: the entry > tools, the `toolCatalog` service (now also provided as `toolUltra`), the hooks, > the config and the state directory `/tool-manager/` stay the same. > An existing profile can keep `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager`: from 0.5.0 it only > re-exports the new core. Older extension releases keep working with the new core. ## Quick start ```sh # 1. install the core plus the rule-based classifier (optional but recommended) dsh plugin --profile web add @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-rules # 2. restart DSH, then ask the agent: "what tools do you have?" # it answers with tools_ls("/") — a directory, not 200 tool schemas # 3. want the UI? add the panel, then open Settings → "Tool manager" dsh plugin --profile web add @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-panel ``` > **Install the scoped `@lvy-jsd/…` packages.** The unscoped `dsh-tool-manager` > on npm is a different project. Do not install both: each one narrows which > tools an agent can see, so together they hide tools from each other. On a fresh install every group is `uncategorized` until a classifier is installed — the tools are still browsable and loadable, only the categories are missing. See [Extending](#extending) to write your own classifier. `tools_load(["web"])` also accepts bare names: try registered `pack:` → `cap:` → `device:` namespaces, first non-empty match only, then normal directory lookup; explicit prefixes keep their behavior and plugin ownership. ## Packages | Package | What it does | |---|---| | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-core) | Core: directory, `tools_ls` / `tools_load` / `tools_unload`, per-agent allowlist, the `toolCatalog` extension service, plus intent retrieval + routing (`tools_find` / `tools_route` / `skills_find` / `skills_route`, BM25 with a Rust sidecar). Without extensions every group is `uncategorized`. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-rules`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-rules) | Places groups into categories from built-in rules and your config overrides. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-risk-gate`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-risk-gate) | Confirms loading high-risk tools through the DSH approval channel, with a per-session allowlist. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-persist`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-persist) | Keeps loaded tools across a DSH restart, one state file per session. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-panel`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-panel) | Web panel: browse the tree, see each live session's loaded tools and token cost, load/unload from the UI, edit the always-on and high-risk lists, edit one tool's metadata, exempt one session. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-llm`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-llm) | Places groups with a small model, one request per group, cached by a hash of the group and its tool descriptions. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-capability-bridge`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-capability-bridge) | Load a named bundle of tools in one call: `tools_load(["cap:android-debug"])`. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-attribution-scan`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-attribution-scan) | Group tools by the plugin package whose source defines them. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-essentials`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-essentials) | Native tool pack, no API keys: time zones and date math, a calculator with units (mathjs), weather (Open-Meteo), place search (Nominatim), Wikipedia. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-web`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-web) | Native tool pack: `web_read` turns a page into clean Markdown (Readability + turndown), `web_links` lists its links. Refuses private addresses by default. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-mcp`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-mcp) | MCP presets through DSH's MCP client: memory, sequential thinking, Context7, Playwright and filesystem start without keys; GitHub, SearXNG, Brave, Tavily, Firecrawl, Notion and AMap start once their key is set. `mcp_presets` shows the status. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-media`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-media) | Native tool pack, no API keys: images, music and video made from code. `html_render` designs an image in HTML/CSS (no browser) or turns its CSS animations into a GIF, `svg_render` turns an SVG drawing into PNG/JPEG/WebP, `chart_render` draws a Vega-Lite chart, `music_render` plays a score with real recorded instruments (SoundFont, mastered) and saves WAV and MIDI, `video_render` makes an MP4 from CSS-animated HTML, SVG or photo scenes with transitions, captions and a soundtrack (host ffmpeg), `audio_transcribe` turns speech into timestamped text with local SenseVoice / Whisper models, with who speaks when, emotions and sounds such as laughter, `video_understand` reads a video as a timestamped storyboard image plus its transcript. External links and data URLs are refused. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-gc`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-gc) | Artifact and media garbage collection: date-partitioned storage management (`[YYYY-MM-DD]`), retention sweeps, and LRU capacity eviction. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-db`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-db) | In-memory OLAP analytics via embedded DuckDB: query CSV, Parquet, and JSON datasets directly via SQL without context inflation. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-office`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-office) | Office documents pack: Word (.docx) text extraction, Excel (.xlsx) read/write, and PDF document metadata inspection. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-devices`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-devices) | Device namespace: Swiftnest device tools under `/device/`, loadable as `device:current`, `device:all` or `device:`, with offline devices marked. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager-dsbot-entry`](packages/dsh-tool-manager-dsbot-entry) | Deprecated, no longer released. A "Tool manager" row in the ds-bot settings dialog that opens the panel. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager`](packages/dsh-tool-manager) | The old core name: re-exports `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core` so existing profiles keep working. | | [`@lvy-jsd/create-dsh-tool-ultra-plugin`](packages/create-dsh-tool-ultra-plugin) | Scaffold your own extension: `npm create @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-plugin@latest my-ext -- --type classifier`. | See [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md) for the design. ## Extending Every feature beyond the core is an ordinary plugin using the `toolCatalog` service, and the bundled `classifier-rules` package is written exactly as a third party would write it. Four extension points: | Point | For | |---|---| | `registerClassifier({ name, priority, group?, categorize? })` | placing tools into groups and groups into categories | | `annotate(match, { group?, category?, risk?, summary? })` | runtime metadata; `package.json` `dsh.toolCatalog` does the same without code | | `registerVisibilityFilter({ name, filter(agent, names) })` | narrowing what one agent may see — can only remove names | | `registerTargetResolver({ name, prefix, resolve })` | owning a target prefix, e.g. `cap:` | | `registerRiskGate` / `registerStateProvider` | confirming high-risk loads / keeping state across a restart | Hooks are plain events: `tool-catalog/before-load` (throw to veto), `after-load`, `before-unload`, `after-unload`, `before-rebuild`, `after-rebuild`, `state-changed`. Start from a generated package — it comes with a passing test: ```sh npm create @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-plugin@latest my-ext -- --type classifier cd my-ext && npm test ``` Two worked examples live in [`examples/`](examples), and the full interface list is in the core README and [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md) §11. ## Development Every package is written in TypeScript (`src/`) and compiled to `lib/` (JavaScript plus `.d.ts` type declarations); `lib/` is build output and not committed. The root `tsconfig.json` lists the packages (project references); the two browser halves (`client.ts`) have their own `tsconfig.client.json`, because DSH loads them as classic scripts, not modules. ```sh npm install # also links your local DSH host packages (scripts/link-host.mjs) npm run build # src/*.ts -> lib/*.js + lib/*.d.ts npm run typecheck # strict type check (tsc -b; writes lib/ too, references need it) node --test test/unit/*.test.mjs # pure catalog and registry tests (needs a build) node test/e2e.mjs # boots throwaway DSH instances; never touches your profile ``` Host packages (`@deepseek-ai/*`) are peers and are never installed from the registry (`.npmrc` sets `legacy-peer-deps`): a registry copy next to the plugin would shadow the DSH you actually run. `npm install` links them from `$DSH_APP` (default `~/.local/share/deepseek-harness/app`) instead. ## License Apache-2.0 — see [LICENSE](LICENSE). Releases before Tool Ultra (`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager*`) were MIT.
