evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-attribution-scan Groups tools by the plugin package that defines them, so a plugin's tools show up together in the `tools_ls` directory even when their names share no prefix. An extension for [`dsh-tool-ultra-core`](../dsh-tool-ultra-core). ## How it works After the first catalog build, the plugin reads the source (`lib/`, `src/`, `dist/`; never `node_modules` or tests) of every enabled plugin package once, in the background, and indexes the string literals. Then, per tool: 1. exactly one package **defines** it (`name: ''`) → that package; 2. otherwise exactly one package **mentions** it → that package; 3. otherwise (ambiguous or unknown) → pass to the next rule. MCP tools (`mcp____…`) are skipped; the core groups them by server. The group name is the package name without its scope and without `stripPrefix`: `dsh-engram` → `engram`, `@acme/dsh-notes` → `notes`. It is an ordinary classifier at priority 10: user overrides, plugin `package.json` declarations and `classifier-rules` (100) all win; the core's structural fallback (shared prefix / `misc`) comes after it. A category declared in `package.json` still applies to the attributed group. ## Install Add the package to your DSH profile and enable its bundle patch: ```yaml - id: tool-manager-attribution-scan name: '@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-attribution-scan' config: enabled: true # priority: 10 # stripPrefix: dsh- # exclude: [] # package names or regex strings never scanned ``` ## Cost Nothing per request: one scan per DSH start (about 1 s for ~500 packages), off the startup path. Grouping never changes visibility — a misattributed tool is only listed in a different place. ## License Apache-2.0

Tool Ultra
On-demand tool loading for DeepSeek Harness — every tool as a directory, loaded only when an agent asks.

English · 中文

--- ## What It Is Tool Ultra is an All-in-One tool-plugin product for DeepSeek Harness, and an important component of [Swiftnest](https://github.com/lvy-jsd/swiftnest). Its goal is one coherent tool product across everyday tasks, web/MCP services, media and device capabilities. The small core and replaceable extension packages are its internal architecture; the product is more than a tool-directory browser. Tools are browsable as a directory (category → group → tool), searchable by intent and loaded on demand, keeping unneeded schemas out of the model's context. Savings depend on catalog size, discovery/load steps and provider caching: compare per-request schemas, total task tokens and task success separately. Broad capability does not mean every external service or upload is enabled by default. The current preview is distributed as source and modular packages; Swiftnest builds a pinned source commit. An AI can install and configure the required modules. The published-package quick-start syntax below applies when those package versions are available on npm; it is not a claim that the renamed 0.5.0 packages have already been published. > **Renamed.** This project was `dsh-tool-manager`. Version 0.5.0 renames every > package from `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager-` to `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-` > (the core is `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core`). Nothing else changes: the entry > tools, the `toolCatalog` service (now also provided as `toolUltra`), the hooks, > the config and the state directory `/tool-manager/` stay the same. > An existing profile can keep `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager`: from 0.5.0 it only > re-exports the new core. Older extension releases keep working with the new core. ## Quick start ```sh # 1. install the core plus the rule-based classifier (optional but recommended) dsh plugin --profile web add @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-rules # 2. restart DSH, then ask the agent: "what tools do you have?" # it answers with tools_ls("/") — a directory, not 200 tool schemas # 3. want the UI? add the panel, then open Settings → "Tool manager" dsh plugin --profile web add @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-panel ``` > **Install the scoped `@lvy-jsd/…` packages.** The unscoped `dsh-tool-manager` > on npm is a different project. Do not install both: each one narrows which > tools an agent can see, so together they hide tools from each other. On a fresh install every group is `uncategorized` until a classifier is installed — the tools are still browsable and loadable, only the categories are missing. See [Extending](#extending) to write your own classifier. `tools_load(["web"])` also accepts bare names: try registered `pack:` → `cap:` → `device:` namespaces, first non-empty match only, then normal directory lookup; explicit prefixes keep their behavior and plugin ownership. ## Packages | Package | What it does | |---|---| | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-core) | Core: directory, `tools_ls` / `tools_load` / `tools_unload`, per-agent allowlist, the `toolCatalog` extension service, plus intent retrieval + routing (`tools_find` / `tools_route` / `skills_find` / `skills_route`, BM25 with a Rust sidecar). Without extensions every group is `uncategorized`. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-rules`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-rules) | Places groups into categories from built-in rules and your config overrides. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-risk-gate`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-risk-gate) | Confirms loading high-risk tools through the DSH approval channel, with a per-session allowlist. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-persist`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-persist) | Keeps loaded tools across a DSH restart, one state file per session. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-panel`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-panel) | Web panel: browse the tree, see each live session's loaded tools and token cost, load/unload from the UI, edit the always-on and high-risk lists, edit one tool's metadata, exempt one session. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-llm`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-llm) | Places groups with a small model, one request per group, cached by a hash of the group and its tool descriptions. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-capability-bridge`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-capability-bridge) | Load a named bundle of tools in one call: `tools_load(["cap:android-debug"])`. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-attribution-scan`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-attribution-scan) | Group tools by the plugin package whose source defines them. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-essentials`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-essentials) | Native tool pack, no API keys: time zones and date math, a calculator with units (mathjs), weather (Open-Meteo), place search (Nominatim), Wikipedia. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-web`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-web) | Native tool pack: `web_read` turns a page into clean Markdown (Readability + turndown), `web_links` lists its links. Refuses private addresses by default. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-mcp`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-mcp) | MCP presets through DSH's MCP client: memory, sequential thinking, Context7, Playwright and filesystem start without keys; GitHub, SearXNG, Brave, Tavily, Firecrawl, Notion and AMap start once their key is set. `mcp_presets` shows the status. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-media`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-media) | Native tool pack, no API keys: images, music and video made from code. `html_render` designs an image in HTML/CSS (no browser) or turns its CSS animations into a GIF, `svg_render` turns an SVG drawing into PNG/JPEG/WebP, `chart_render` draws a Vega-Lite chart, `music_render` plays a score with real recorded instruments (SoundFont, mastered) and saves WAV and MIDI, `video_render` makes an MP4 from CSS-animated HTML, SVG or photo scenes with transitions, captions and a soundtrack (host ffmpeg), `audio_transcribe` turns speech into timestamped text with local SenseVoice / Whisper models, with who speaks when, emotions and sounds such as laughter, `video_understand` reads a video as a timestamped storyboard image plus its transcript. External links and data URLs are refused. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-gc`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-gc) | Artifact and media garbage collection: date-partitioned storage management (`[YYYY-MM-DD]`), retention sweeps, and LRU capacity eviction. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-db`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-db) | In-memory OLAP analytics via embedded DuckDB: query CSV, Parquet, and JSON datasets directly via SQL without context inflation. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-office`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-office) | Office documents pack: Word (.docx) text extraction, Excel (.xlsx) read/write, and PDF document metadata inspection. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-devices`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-devices) | Device namespace: Swiftnest device tools under `/device/`, loadable as `device:current`, `device:all` or `device:`, with offline devices marked. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager-dsbot-entry`](packages/dsh-tool-manager-dsbot-entry) | Deprecated, no longer released. A "Tool manager" row in the ds-bot settings dialog that opens the panel. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager`](packages/dsh-tool-manager) | The old core name: re-exports `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core` so existing profiles keep working. | | [`@lvy-jsd/create-dsh-tool-ultra-plugin`](packages/create-dsh-tool-ultra-plugin) | Scaffold your own extension: `npm create @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-plugin@latest my-ext -- --type classifier`. | See [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md) for the design. ## Extending Every feature beyond the core is an ordinary plugin using the `toolCatalog` service, and the bundled `classifier-rules` package is written exactly as a third party would write it. Four extension points: | Point | For | |---|---| | `registerClassifier({ name, priority, group?, categorize? })` | placing tools into groups and groups into categories | | `annotate(match, { group?, category?, risk?, summary? })` | runtime metadata; `package.json` `dsh.toolCatalog` does the same without code | | `registerVisibilityFilter({ name, filter(agent, names) })` | narrowing what one agent may see — can only remove names | | `registerTargetResolver({ name, prefix, resolve })` | owning a target prefix, e.g. `cap:` | | `registerRiskGate` / `registerStateProvider` | confirming high-risk loads / keeping state across a restart | Hooks are plain events: `tool-catalog/before-load` (throw to veto), `after-load`, `before-unload`, `after-unload`, `before-rebuild`, `after-rebuild`, `state-changed`. Start from a generated package — it comes with a passing test: ```sh npm create @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-plugin@latest my-ext -- --type classifier cd my-ext && npm test ``` Two worked examples live in [`examples/`](examples), and the full interface list is in the core README and [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md) §11. ## Development Every package is written in TypeScript (`src/`) and compiled to `lib/` (JavaScript plus `.d.ts` type declarations); `lib/` is build output and not committed. The root `tsconfig.json` lists the packages (project references); the two browser halves (`client.ts`) have their own `tsconfig.client.json`, because DSH loads them as classic scripts, not modules. ```sh npm install # also links your local DSH host packages (scripts/link-host.mjs) npm run build # src/*.ts -> lib/*.js + lib/*.d.ts npm run typecheck # strict type check (tsc -b; writes lib/ too, references need it) node --test test/unit/*.test.mjs # pure catalog and registry tests (needs a build) node test/e2e.mjs # boots throwaway DSH instances; never touches your profile ``` Host packages (`@deepseek-ai/*`) are peers and are never installed from the registry (`.npmrc` sets `legacy-peer-deps`): a registry copy next to the plugin would shadow the DSH you actually run. `npm install` links them from `$DSH_APP` (default `~/.local/share/deepseek-harness/app`) instead. ## License Apache-2.0 — see [LICENSE](LICENSE). Releases before Tool Ultra (`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager*`) were MIT.

# @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-capability-bridge Load a named bundle of tools in one call for [`dsh-tool-ultra-core`](../dsh-tool-ultra-core). A capability pack is a named set of things a session needs. This plugin lets a pack also declare **tools**, so the model arms the whole set at once instead of walking the directory: ``` tools_load(["cap:android-debug"]) ``` Optional — without it `cap:` is just an unknown target. ## How it stays out of the core's way It registers a **target resolver** on the `toolCatalog` service, so the core never learns what a capability is. The alias expands to ordinary targets * before* anything else runs, which means loading, unloading, `tool-catalog/before-load` hooks, the risk gate and persistence all keep working unchanged. A pack whose tools include a high-risk tool still needs the risk gate's approval, because the alias expands to the tool's own name. ## Configuration ```yaml - id: tool-manager-capability-bridge name: '@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-capability-bridge' config: enabled: true prefix: "cap:" # change only if it collides with a real name listInDirectory: true # add a "capabilities" category packs: android-debug: ["/device/adb", "/device/phone", "adb_logcat"] review: [gh_get_file, merge_pull_request] ``` Each pack entry is a list of ordinary targets: directory paths, group names or exact tool names — anything `tools_load` accepts. A single string is accepted too. ## Registering packs at runtime Another plugin (a capability store, a UI) can declare packs through the `toolCapabilityPacks` service: ```js ctx.inject(['toolCapabilityPacks'], (c) => { c.effect(() => c.toolCapabilityPacks.registerPack('android-debug', [ '/device/adb', 'adb_logcat', ])) }) ``` `registerPack` returns a disposer and refreshes the catalog, so the directory follows immediately. ## What a pack resolves to | Pack declares | `cap:` resolves to | |---|---| | one target | that target's node (a group, a tool, a category) | | several targets | one synthetic node holding exactly those tools | The synthetic node contains **only** the tools the pack names — it does not reuse the catalog's own group objects, so an alias can never load more than it declares. Unknown pack names fall through to a normal lookup, so a typo reports "not found" like any other bad target. ## Writing your own target vocabulary `registerTargetResolver` is a general extension point, not capability-specific: ```js ctx.effect(() => ctx.toolCatalog.registerTargetResolver({ name: 'my-prefix', prefix: 'db:', resolve: (target) => targetsForDatabase(target.slice(3)), // or undefined to pass })) ``` Resolvers are consulted before the built-in rules; `undefined` means "not mine", and `[]` means "mine, but empty" (reported as missing). ## License Apache-2.0 — see [LICENSE](LICENSE). Releases before Tool Ultra (`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager*`) were MIT.

Tool Ultra
On-demand tool loading for DeepSeek Harness — every tool as a directory, loaded only when an agent asks.

English · 中文

--- ## What It Is Tool Ultra is an All-in-One tool-plugin product for DeepSeek Harness, and an important component of [Swiftnest](https://github.com/lvy-jsd/swiftnest). Its goal is one coherent tool product across everyday tasks, web/MCP services, media and device capabilities. The small core and replaceable extension packages are its internal architecture; the product is more than a tool-directory browser. Tools are browsable as a directory (category → group → tool), searchable by intent and loaded on demand, keeping unneeded schemas out of the model's context. Savings depend on catalog size, discovery/load steps and provider caching: compare per-request schemas, total task tokens and task success separately. Broad capability does not mean every external service or upload is enabled by default. The current preview is distributed as source and modular packages; Swiftnest builds a pinned source commit. An AI can install and configure the required modules. The published-package quick-start syntax below applies when those package versions are available on npm; it is not a claim that the renamed 0.5.0 packages have already been published. > **Renamed.** This project was `dsh-tool-manager`. Version 0.5.0 renames every > package from `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager-` to `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-` > (the core is `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core`). Nothing else changes: the entry > tools, the `toolCatalog` service (now also provided as `toolUltra`), the hooks, > the config and the state directory `/tool-manager/` stay the same. > An existing profile can keep `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager`: from 0.5.0 it only > re-exports the new core. Older extension releases keep working with the new core. ## Quick start ```sh # 1. install the core plus the rule-based classifier (optional but recommended) dsh plugin --profile web add @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-rules # 2. restart DSH, then ask the agent: "what tools do you have?" # it answers with tools_ls("/") — a directory, not 200 tool schemas # 3. want the UI? add the panel, then open Settings → "Tool manager" dsh plugin --profile web add @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-panel ``` > **Install the scoped `@lvy-jsd/…` packages.** The unscoped `dsh-tool-manager` > on npm is a different project. Do not install both: each one narrows which > tools an agent can see, so together they hide tools from each other. On a fresh install every group is `uncategorized` until a classifier is installed — the tools are still browsable and loadable, only the categories are missing. See [Extending](#extending) to write your own classifier. `tools_load(["web"])` also accepts bare names: try registered `pack:` → `cap:` → `device:` namespaces, first non-empty match only, then normal directory lookup; explicit prefixes keep their behavior and plugin ownership. ## Packages | Package | What it does | |---|---| | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-core) | Core: directory, `tools_ls` / `tools_load` / `tools_unload`, per-agent allowlist, the `toolCatalog` extension service, plus intent retrieval + routing (`tools_find` / `tools_route` / `skills_find` / `skills_route`, BM25 with a Rust sidecar). Without extensions every group is `uncategorized`. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-rules`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-rules) | Places groups into categories from built-in rules and your config overrides. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-risk-gate`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-risk-gate) | Confirms loading high-risk tools through the DSH approval channel, with a per-session allowlist. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-persist`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-persist) | Keeps loaded tools across a DSH restart, one state file per session. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-panel`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-panel) | Web panel: browse the tree, see each live session's loaded tools and token cost, load/unload from the UI, edit the always-on and high-risk lists, edit one tool's metadata, exempt one session. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-llm`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-llm) | Places groups with a small model, one request per group, cached by a hash of the group and its tool descriptions. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-capability-bridge`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-capability-bridge) | Load a named bundle of tools in one call: `tools_load(["cap:android-debug"])`. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-attribution-scan`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-attribution-scan) | Group tools by the plugin package whose source defines them. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-essentials`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-essentials) | Native tool pack, no API keys: time zones and date math, a calculator with units (mathjs), weather (Open-Meteo), place search (Nominatim), Wikipedia. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-web`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-web) | Native tool pack: `web_read` turns a page into clean Markdown (Readability + turndown), `web_links` lists its links. Refuses private addresses by default. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-mcp`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-mcp) | MCP presets through DSH's MCP client: memory, sequential thinking, Context7, Playwright and filesystem start without keys; GitHub, SearXNG, Brave, Tavily, Firecrawl, Notion and AMap start once their key is set. `mcp_presets` shows the status. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-media`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-media) | Native tool pack, no API keys: images, music and video made from code. `html_render` designs an image in HTML/CSS (no browser) or turns its CSS animations into a GIF, `svg_render` turns an SVG drawing into PNG/JPEG/WebP, `chart_render` draws a Vega-Lite chart, `music_render` plays a score with real recorded instruments (SoundFont, mastered) and saves WAV and MIDI, `video_render` makes an MP4 from CSS-animated HTML, SVG or photo scenes with transitions, captions and a soundtrack (host ffmpeg), `audio_transcribe` turns speech into timestamped text with local SenseVoice / Whisper models, with who speaks when, emotions and sounds such as laughter, `video_understand` reads a video as a timestamped storyboard image plus its transcript. External links and data URLs are refused. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-gc`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-gc) | Artifact and media garbage collection: date-partitioned storage management (`[YYYY-MM-DD]`), retention sweeps, and LRU capacity eviction. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-db`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-db) | In-memory OLAP analytics via embedded DuckDB: query CSV, Parquet, and JSON datasets directly via SQL without context inflation. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-office`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-office) | Office documents pack: Word (.docx) text extraction, Excel (.xlsx) read/write, and PDF document metadata inspection. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-devices`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-devices) | Device namespace: Swiftnest device tools under `/device/`, loadable as `device:current`, `device:all` or `device:`, with offline devices marked. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager-dsbot-entry`](packages/dsh-tool-manager-dsbot-entry) | Deprecated, no longer released. A "Tool manager" row in the ds-bot settings dialog that opens the panel. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager`](packages/dsh-tool-manager) | The old core name: re-exports `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core` so existing profiles keep working. | | [`@lvy-jsd/create-dsh-tool-ultra-plugin`](packages/create-dsh-tool-ultra-plugin) | Scaffold your own extension: `npm create @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-plugin@latest my-ext -- --type classifier`. | See [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md) for the design. ## Extending Every feature beyond the core is an ordinary plugin using the `toolCatalog` service, and the bundled `classifier-rules` package is written exactly as a third party would write it. Four extension points: | Point | For | |---|---| | `registerClassifier({ name, priority, group?, categorize? })` | placing tools into groups and groups into categories | | `annotate(match, { group?, category?, risk?, summary? })` | runtime metadata; `package.json` `dsh.toolCatalog` does the same without code | | `registerVisibilityFilter({ name, filter(agent, names) })` | narrowing what one agent may see — can only remove names | | `registerTargetResolver({ name, prefix, resolve })` | owning a target prefix, e.g. `cap:` | | `registerRiskGate` / `registerStateProvider` | confirming high-risk loads / keeping state across a restart | Hooks are plain events: `tool-catalog/before-load` (throw to veto), `after-load`, `before-unload`, `after-unload`, `before-rebuild`, `after-rebuild`, `state-changed`. Start from a generated package — it comes with a passing test: ```sh npm create @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-plugin@latest my-ext -- --type classifier cd my-ext && npm test ``` Two worked examples live in [`examples/`](examples), and the full interface list is in the core README and [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md) §11. ## Development Every package is written in TypeScript (`src/`) and compiled to `lib/` (JavaScript plus `.d.ts` type declarations); `lib/` is build output and not committed. The root `tsconfig.json` lists the packages (project references); the two browser halves (`client.ts`) have their own `tsconfig.client.json`, because DSH loads them as classic scripts, not modules. ```sh npm install # also links your local DSH host packages (scripts/link-host.mjs) npm run build # src/*.ts -> lib/*.js + lib/*.d.ts npm run typecheck # strict type check (tsc -b; writes lib/ too, references need it) node --test test/unit/*.test.mjs # pure catalog and registry tests (needs a build) node test/e2e.mjs # boots throwaway DSH instances; never touches your profile ``` Host packages (`@deepseek-ai/*`) are peers and are never installed from the registry (`.npmrc` sets `legacy-peer-deps`): a registry copy next to the plugin would shadow the DSH you actually run. `npm install` links them from `$DSH_APP` (default `~/.local/share/deepseek-harness/app`) instead. ## License Apache-2.0 — see [LICENSE](LICENSE). Releases before Tool Ultra (`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager*`) were MIT.

# @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-llm Small-model classifier for [`dsh-tool-ultra-core`](../dsh-tool-ultra-core): it asks a model once per tool group and caches the answer. Optional — without it (or without a model) every group stays `uncategorized`, which still works: the tools are browsable and loadable. ## Why it caches The directory has to be **stable**. A category that changes between sessions invalidates paths the model memorised, and a group moving costs another prompt cache miss. So this classifier never classifies on the hot path: 1. `categorize(group)` is synchronous and answers from the cache file; 2. a miss is queued and the group stays `uncategorized` for now; 3. the queue is pumped **after** the catalog is built, so a rebuild never waits on the network; 4. when answers land they are written to the cache and `toolCatalog.refresh()` is called, so the next rebuild shows them. Classification is **per group, not per call**: a host with 40 groups makes about 40 small requests in total, ever. ## Cache keys The key is a hash of the group name plus each tool's name and a hash of its description: ```js groupKey(group) // sha1(name + sorted("name:sha1(description)"))[:16] ``` So a rewritten description re-classifies that group, a new tool joining the group re-classifies it, and reordering never does. A corrupt cache file is treated as an empty cache, never a crash. ## Configuration ```yaml - id: tool-manager-classifier-llm name: '@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-llm' config: enabled: true # Which model classifies. Omit it and every group stays uncategorized. model: { provider: deepseek-official, model: deepseek-flash } # Defaults to /tool-manager/classifier-cache.json cacheFile: ~/.config/deepseek-harness/tool-manager/classifier-cache.json maxTokens: 16 # the answer is one word batchSize: 5 # groups classified before one refresh priority: 50 # ordinary tier: below user overrides (1000) and declarations ``` Any model route DSH already has configured works — the plugin stores no keys. `model: { provider, model }` is the same shape every model-using component in this project takes (see DESIGN §2.5). ## Categories the model may choose `device`, `code`, `media`, `maps`, `browser`, `memory`, `collaboration`, `automation`, `connectors`, `search`, `system` — the core vocabulary, exported as `CATEGORIES`. The model must answer with exactly one of them; anything else is recorded as a failure and the group stays `uncategorized`. Priority puts it **below** plugin self-declarations and user rules, so a `package.json` `dsh.toolCatalog` entry or a `classifier-rules` override always wins over the model. ## Writing your own classifier The extension point is generic; a classifier is just `{ name, priority, categorize(group) }`: ```js ctx.effect(() => ctx.toolCatalog.registerClassifier({ name: 'my-classifier', priority: 60, categorize: (group) => myLookup(group), // sync; return undefined to pass })) ``` This plugin's pieces are exported for reuse: `groupKey`, `readCache`, `writeCache`, `buildPrompt`, `parseCategory`, `createLlmClassifier` and `createLlmCaller`. `createLlmClassifier` takes any `classifyGroup(group)` function, which is how the test suite runs it without a provider. ## License Apache-2.0 — see [LICENSE](LICENSE). Releases before Tool Ultra (`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager*`) were MIT.

Tool Ultra
On-demand tool loading for DeepSeek Harness — every tool as a directory, loaded only when an agent asks.

English · 中文

--- ## What It Is Tool Ultra is an All-in-One tool-plugin product for DeepSeek Harness, and an important component of [Swiftnest](https://github.com/lvy-jsd/swiftnest). Its goal is one coherent tool product across everyday tasks, web/MCP services, media and device capabilities. The small core and replaceable extension packages are its internal architecture; the product is more than a tool-directory browser. Tools are browsable as a directory (category → group → tool), searchable by intent and loaded on demand, keeping unneeded schemas out of the model's context. Savings depend on catalog size, discovery/load steps and provider caching: compare per-request schemas, total task tokens and task success separately. Broad capability does not mean every external service or upload is enabled by default. The current preview is distributed as source and modular packages; Swiftnest builds a pinned source commit. An AI can install and configure the required modules. The published-package quick-start syntax below applies when those package versions are available on npm; it is not a claim that the renamed 0.5.0 packages have already been published. > **Renamed.** This project was `dsh-tool-manager`. Version 0.5.0 renames every > package from `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager-` to `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-` > (the core is `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core`). Nothing else changes: the entry > tools, the `toolCatalog` service (now also provided as `toolUltra`), the hooks, > the config and the state directory `/tool-manager/` stay the same. > An existing profile can keep `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager`: from 0.5.0 it only > re-exports the new core. Older extension releases keep working with the new core. ## Quick start ```sh # 1. install the core plus the rule-based classifier (optional but recommended) dsh plugin --profile web add @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-rules # 2. restart DSH, then ask the agent: "what tools do you have?" # it answers with tools_ls("/") — a directory, not 200 tool schemas # 3. want the UI? add the panel, then open Settings → "Tool manager" dsh plugin --profile web add @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-panel ``` > **Install the scoped `@lvy-jsd/…` packages.** The unscoped `dsh-tool-manager` > on npm is a different project. Do not install both: each one narrows which > tools an agent can see, so together they hide tools from each other. On a fresh install every group is `uncategorized` until a classifier is installed — the tools are still browsable and loadable, only the categories are missing. See [Extending](#extending) to write your own classifier. `tools_load(["web"])` also accepts bare names: try registered `pack:` → `cap:` → `device:` namespaces, first non-empty match only, then normal directory lookup; explicit prefixes keep their behavior and plugin ownership. ## Packages | Package | What it does | |---|---| | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-core) | Core: directory, `tools_ls` / `tools_load` / `tools_unload`, per-agent allowlist, the `toolCatalog` extension service, plus intent retrieval + routing (`tools_find` / `tools_route` / `skills_find` / `skills_route`, BM25 with a Rust sidecar). Without extensions every group is `uncategorized`. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-rules`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-rules) | Places groups into categories from built-in rules and your config overrides. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-risk-gate`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-risk-gate) | Confirms loading high-risk tools through the DSH approval channel, with a per-session allowlist. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-persist`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-persist) | Keeps loaded tools across a DSH restart, one state file per session. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-panel`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-panel) | Web panel: browse the tree, see each live session's loaded tools and token cost, load/unload from the UI, edit the always-on and high-risk lists, edit one tool's metadata, exempt one session. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-llm`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-llm) | Places groups with a small model, one request per group, cached by a hash of the group and its tool descriptions. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-capability-bridge`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-capability-bridge) | Load a named bundle of tools in one call: `tools_load(["cap:android-debug"])`. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-attribution-scan`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-attribution-scan) | Group tools by the plugin package whose source defines them. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-essentials`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-essentials) | Native tool pack, no API keys: time zones and date math, a calculator with units (mathjs), weather (Open-Meteo), place search (Nominatim), Wikipedia. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-web`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-web) | Native tool pack: `web_read` turns a page into clean Markdown (Readability + turndown), `web_links` lists its links. Refuses private addresses by default. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-mcp`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-mcp) | MCP presets through DSH's MCP client: memory, sequential thinking, Context7, Playwright and filesystem start without keys; GitHub, SearXNG, Brave, Tavily, Firecrawl, Notion and AMap start once their key is set. `mcp_presets` shows the status. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-media`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-media) | Native tool pack, no API keys: images, music and video made from code. `html_render` designs an image in HTML/CSS (no browser) or turns its CSS animations into a GIF, `svg_render` turns an SVG drawing into PNG/JPEG/WebP, `chart_render` draws a Vega-Lite chart, `music_render` plays a score with real recorded instruments (SoundFont, mastered) and saves WAV and MIDI, `video_render` makes an MP4 from CSS-animated HTML, SVG or photo scenes with transitions, captions and a soundtrack (host ffmpeg), `audio_transcribe` turns speech into timestamped text with local SenseVoice / Whisper models, with who speaks when, emotions and sounds such as laughter, `video_understand` reads a video as a timestamped storyboard image plus its transcript. External links and data URLs are refused. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-gc`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-gc) | Artifact and media garbage collection: date-partitioned storage management (`[YYYY-MM-DD]`), retention sweeps, and LRU capacity eviction. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-db`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-db) | In-memory OLAP analytics via embedded DuckDB: query CSV, Parquet, and JSON datasets directly via SQL without context inflation. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-office`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-office) | Office documents pack: Word (.docx) text extraction, Excel (.xlsx) read/write, and PDF document metadata inspection. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-devices`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-devices) | Device namespace: Swiftnest device tools under `/device/`, loadable as `device:current`, `device:all` or `device:`, with offline devices marked. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager-dsbot-entry`](packages/dsh-tool-manager-dsbot-entry) | Deprecated, no longer released. A "Tool manager" row in the ds-bot settings dialog that opens the panel. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager`](packages/dsh-tool-manager) | The old core name: re-exports `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core` so existing profiles keep working. | | [`@lvy-jsd/create-dsh-tool-ultra-plugin`](packages/create-dsh-tool-ultra-plugin) | Scaffold your own extension: `npm create @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-plugin@latest my-ext -- --type classifier`. | See [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md) for the design. ## Extending Every feature beyond the core is an ordinary plugin using the `toolCatalog` service, and the bundled `classifier-rules` package is written exactly as a third party would write it. Four extension points: | Point | For | |---|---| | `registerClassifier({ name, priority, group?, categorize? })` | placing tools into groups and groups into categories | | `annotate(match, { group?, category?, risk?, summary? })` | runtime metadata; `package.json` `dsh.toolCatalog` does the same without code | | `registerVisibilityFilter({ name, filter(agent, names) })` | narrowing what one agent may see — can only remove names | | `registerTargetResolver({ name, prefix, resolve })` | owning a target prefix, e.g. `cap:` | | `registerRiskGate` / `registerStateProvider` | confirming high-risk loads / keeping state across a restart | Hooks are plain events: `tool-catalog/before-load` (throw to veto), `after-load`, `before-unload`, `after-unload`, `before-rebuild`, `after-rebuild`, `state-changed`. Start from a generated package — it comes with a passing test: ```sh npm create @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-plugin@latest my-ext -- --type classifier cd my-ext && npm test ``` Two worked examples live in [`examples/`](examples), and the full interface list is in the core README and [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md) §11. ## Development Every package is written in TypeScript (`src/`) and compiled to `lib/` (JavaScript plus `.d.ts` type declarations); `lib/` is build output and not committed. The root `tsconfig.json` lists the packages (project references); the two browser halves (`client.ts`) have their own `tsconfig.client.json`, because DSH loads them as classic scripts, not modules. ```sh npm install # also links your local DSH host packages (scripts/link-host.mjs) npm run build # src/*.ts -> lib/*.js + lib/*.d.ts npm run typecheck # strict type check (tsc -b; writes lib/ too, references need it) node --test test/unit/*.test.mjs # pure catalog and registry tests (needs a build) node test/e2e.mjs # boots throwaway DSH instances; never touches your profile ``` Host packages (`@deepseek-ai/*`) are peers and are never installed from the registry (`.npmrc` sets `legacy-peer-deps`): a registry copy next to the plugin would shadow the DSH you actually run. `npm install` links them from `$DSH_APP` (default `~/.local/share/deepseek-harness/app`) instead. ## License Apache-2.0 — see [LICENSE](LICENSE). Releases before Tool Ultra (`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager*`) were MIT.

# @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-rules Rule-based classifier for [`dsh-tool-ultra-core`](../dsh-tool-ultra-core). It registers up to two classifiers on the `toolCatalog` service: | Classifier | Priority | Source | |---|---|---| | `rules:user` | 1000 (override) | your `groupRules` and `categories` config; beats plugin declarations | | `rules:defaults` | 100 | built-in rules for tools common on DSH hosts (adb, phone, desktop, github, nix, browser, engram, bots, groups, team, automation, schedule, MCP connector, secrets, x search…) and for common MCP server names (search, searxng, brave-search, tavily, exa → `search`; email, mail, gmail, imap, outlook → `mail`; playwright, puppeteer, chrome-devtools → `browser`); plugin declarations beat it | The defaults also define the `mail` category ("Email: read, search, draft and send mail"), which the core vocabulary does not have, so they work with any core version. Your own `categories` entry with a description wins over it. ## Configuration ```yaml - id: tool-manager-classifier-rules name: '@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-rules' config: defaults: true # set false to use only your own rules groupRules: # regex over tool names -> group, first match wins - { match: '^lingshu_', group: lingshu } categories: # place groups; add categories with a description system: { groups: [lingshu] } games: { description: Game servers and bots, groups: [minecraft] } ``` The rule tables (`DEFAULT_GROUP_RULES`, `DEFAULT_GROUP_CATEGORIES`) and the `rulesClassifier()` helper are exported, so a fork or another plugin can reuse them with different data. ## License Apache-2.0

Tool Ultra
On-demand tool loading for DeepSeek Harness — every tool as a directory, loaded only when an agent asks.

English · 中文

--- ## What It Is Tool Ultra is an All-in-One tool-plugin product for DeepSeek Harness, and an important component of [Swiftnest](https://github.com/lvy-jsd/swiftnest). Its goal is one coherent tool product across everyday tasks, web/MCP services, media and device capabilities. The small core and replaceable extension packages are its internal architecture; the product is more than a tool-directory browser. Tools are browsable as a directory (category → group → tool), searchable by intent and loaded on demand, keeping unneeded schemas out of the model's context. Savings depend on catalog size, discovery/load steps and provider caching: compare per-request schemas, total task tokens and task success separately. Broad capability does not mean every external service or upload is enabled by default. The current preview is distributed as source and modular packages; Swiftnest builds a pinned source commit. An AI can install and configure the required modules. The published-package quick-start syntax below applies when those package versions are available on npm; it is not a claim that the renamed 0.5.0 packages have already been published. > **Renamed.** This project was `dsh-tool-manager`. Version 0.5.0 renames every > package from `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager-` to `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-` > (the core is `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core`). Nothing else changes: the entry > tools, the `toolCatalog` service (now also provided as `toolUltra`), the hooks, > the config and the state directory `/tool-manager/` stay the same. > An existing profile can keep `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager`: from 0.5.0 it only > re-exports the new core. Older extension releases keep working with the new core. ## Quick start ```sh # 1. install the core plus the rule-based classifier (optional but recommended) dsh plugin --profile web add @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-rules # 2. restart DSH, then ask the agent: "what tools do you have?" # it answers with tools_ls("/") — a directory, not 200 tool schemas # 3. want the UI? add the panel, then open Settings → "Tool manager" dsh plugin --profile web add @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-panel ``` > **Install the scoped `@lvy-jsd/…` packages.** The unscoped `dsh-tool-manager` > on npm is a different project. Do not install both: each one narrows which > tools an agent can see, so together they hide tools from each other. On a fresh install every group is `uncategorized` until a classifier is installed — the tools are still browsable and loadable, only the categories are missing. See [Extending](#extending) to write your own classifier. `tools_load(["web"])` also accepts bare names: try registered `pack:` → `cap:` → `device:` namespaces, first non-empty match only, then normal directory lookup; explicit prefixes keep their behavior and plugin ownership. ## Packages | Package | What it does | |---|---| | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-core) | Core: directory, `tools_ls` / `tools_load` / `tools_unload`, per-agent allowlist, the `toolCatalog` extension service, plus intent retrieval + routing (`tools_find` / `tools_route` / `skills_find` / `skills_route`, BM25 with a Rust sidecar). Without extensions every group is `uncategorized`. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-rules`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-rules) | Places groups into categories from built-in rules and your config overrides. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-risk-gate`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-risk-gate) | Confirms loading high-risk tools through the DSH approval channel, with a per-session allowlist. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-persist`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-persist) | Keeps loaded tools across a DSH restart, one state file per session. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-panel`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-panel) | Web panel: browse the tree, see each live session's loaded tools and token cost, load/unload from the UI, edit the always-on and high-risk lists, edit one tool's metadata, exempt one session. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-llm`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-llm) | Places groups with a small model, one request per group, cached by a hash of the group and its tool descriptions. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-capability-bridge`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-capability-bridge) | Load a named bundle of tools in one call: `tools_load(["cap:android-debug"])`. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-attribution-scan`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-attribution-scan) | Group tools by the plugin package whose source defines them. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-essentials`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-essentials) | Native tool pack, no API keys: time zones and date math, a calculator with units (mathjs), weather (Open-Meteo), place search (Nominatim), Wikipedia. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-web`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-web) | Native tool pack: `web_read` turns a page into clean Markdown (Readability + turndown), `web_links` lists its links. Refuses private addresses by default. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-mcp`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-mcp) | MCP presets through DSH's MCP client: memory, sequential thinking, Context7, Playwright and filesystem start without keys; GitHub, SearXNG, Brave, Tavily, Firecrawl, Notion and AMap start once their key is set. `mcp_presets` shows the status. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-media`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-media) | Native tool pack, no API keys: images, music and video made from code. `html_render` designs an image in HTML/CSS (no browser) or turns its CSS animations into a GIF, `svg_render` turns an SVG drawing into PNG/JPEG/WebP, `chart_render` draws a Vega-Lite chart, `music_render` plays a score with real recorded instruments (SoundFont, mastered) and saves WAV and MIDI, `video_render` makes an MP4 from CSS-animated HTML, SVG or photo scenes with transitions, captions and a soundtrack (host ffmpeg), `audio_transcribe` turns speech into timestamped text with local SenseVoice / Whisper models, with who speaks when, emotions and sounds such as laughter, `video_understand` reads a video as a timestamped storyboard image plus its transcript. External links and data URLs are refused. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-gc`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-gc) | Artifact and media garbage collection: date-partitioned storage management (`[YYYY-MM-DD]`), retention sweeps, and LRU capacity eviction. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-db`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-db) | In-memory OLAP analytics via embedded DuckDB: query CSV, Parquet, and JSON datasets directly via SQL without context inflation. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-office`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-office) | Office documents pack: Word (.docx) text extraction, Excel (.xlsx) read/write, and PDF document metadata inspection. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-devices`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-devices) | Device namespace: Swiftnest device tools under `/device/`, loadable as `device:current`, `device:all` or `device:`, with offline devices marked. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager-dsbot-entry`](packages/dsh-tool-manager-dsbot-entry) | Deprecated, no longer released. A "Tool manager" row in the ds-bot settings dialog that opens the panel. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager`](packages/dsh-tool-manager) | The old core name: re-exports `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core` so existing profiles keep working. | | [`@lvy-jsd/create-dsh-tool-ultra-plugin`](packages/create-dsh-tool-ultra-plugin) | Scaffold your own extension: `npm create @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-plugin@latest my-ext -- --type classifier`. | See [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md) for the design. ## Extending Every feature beyond the core is an ordinary plugin using the `toolCatalog` service, and the bundled `classifier-rules` package is written exactly as a third party would write it. Four extension points: | Point | For | |---|---| | `registerClassifier({ name, priority, group?, categorize? })` | placing tools into groups and groups into categories | | `annotate(match, { group?, category?, risk?, summary? })` | runtime metadata; `package.json` `dsh.toolCatalog` does the same without code | | `registerVisibilityFilter({ name, filter(agent, names) })` | narrowing what one agent may see — can only remove names | | `registerTargetResolver({ name, prefix, resolve })` | owning a target prefix, e.g. `cap:` | | `registerRiskGate` / `registerStateProvider` | confirming high-risk loads / keeping state across a restart | Hooks are plain events: `tool-catalog/before-load` (throw to veto), `after-load`, `before-unload`, `after-unload`, `before-rebuild`, `after-rebuild`, `state-changed`. Start from a generated package — it comes with a passing test: ```sh npm create @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-plugin@latest my-ext -- --type classifier cd my-ext && npm test ``` Two worked examples live in [`examples/`](examples), and the full interface list is in the core README and [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md) §11. ## Development Every package is written in TypeScript (`src/`) and compiled to `lib/` (JavaScript plus `.d.ts` type declarations); `lib/` is build output and not committed. The root `tsconfig.json` lists the packages (project references); the two browser halves (`client.ts`) have their own `tsconfig.client.json`, because DSH loads them as classic scripts, not modules. ```sh npm install # also links your local DSH host packages (scripts/link-host.mjs) npm run build # src/*.ts -> lib/*.js + lib/*.d.ts npm run typecheck # strict type check (tsc -b; writes lib/ too, references need it) node --test test/unit/*.test.mjs # pure catalog and registry tests (needs a build) node test/e2e.mjs # boots throwaway DSH instances; never touches your profile ``` Host packages (`@deepseek-ai/*`) are peers and are never installed from the registry (`.npmrc` sets `legacy-peer-deps`): a registry copy next to the plugin would shadow the DSH you actually run. `npm install` links them from `$DSH_APP` (default `~/.local/share/deepseek-harness/app`) instead. ## License Apache-2.0 — see [LICENSE](LICENSE). Releases before Tool Ultra (`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager*`) were MIT.

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core Browse every DeepSeek Harness tool as a directory and load tools on demand. A DSH host with many plugins and MCP connectors sends every tool schema to the model on every request. This plugin hides everything except a small always-on set and gives the model three entry tools to find and load the rest: ``` tools_ls("/") # categories tools_ls("/code") # groups (a connector or plugin) tools_ls("/code/github") # tools, with a one-line summary and schema size tools_ls({ query: "pull request" }) # search the whole tree in one step tools_load(["/code/github"]) # callable from the next step, for the rest of the session tools_load(["mcp__github__get_me"]) # or one tool by exact name tools_load(["web"]) # bare pack/cap/device name, first match tools_unload(["/code/github"]) tools_find("send an email") # ranked matches by intent (BM25), no loading tools_route("send an email") # retrieve, re-rank with the model, then load ``` Loaded tools are **native**: the model receives their full parameter schema and calls them directly. Nothing is proxied. Bare names try registered `pack:` → `cap:` → `device:` resolvers, stopping at the first non-empty expansion before normal directory lookup; paths and explicit prefixes keep their existing behavior and plugin ownership. The core ships **no placement rules**. Without an extension every group is listed under `uncategorized/` — still fully browsable and loadable. Install [`dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-rules`](../dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-rules) for built-in rules and config overrides, or write your own classifier. ## How it works - Visibility is a per-agent allowlist installed with the host's `agent.ctx.tools.restrict({ allow })`: `allow = (pinned ∪ loaded tools ∪ tools of loaded groups) ∩ registered tools`, then narrowed by any registered visibility filters. Tools that appear later (an MCP server reconnecting, a new plugin, a renamed tool) stay hidden until loaded. - Loading a group subscribes to it: tools the group gains later become visible too. - Restrictions from other plugins intersect with this one, so a hard deny (for example the MCP connector's governance policy) always wins. A pinned or loaded tool that another layer still hides is marked `[denied]` in `tools_ls`, and `tools_load` reports it as not callable instead of listing it (with one log warning per tool, pointing at connector governance rules and per-session injection). - DSH's PTC mode (`DSH_TOOLS_MODE=ptc` on DSH 0.2.1, the `tool-executor-ptc` profile row from 0.2.2) works unchanged: the model gets only `run_code`, and the SDK the host declares for it is built from the same narrowed view, so loads show up there from the next step. `run_code` itself is a host transport and never enters the directory. - A direct call of a hidden ordinary tool loads it. On DSH 0.2.1 the call then runs; DSH 0.2.2 fixes a step's callable tools when the step starts, so there the call is refused with "it is loaded now: call it again" and the retry runs. - Every agent is restricted separately. A subagent starts from the pinned set plus whatever the parent loaded with `forSubagents: true`. - Loaded state is in memory. Install [`dsh-tool-ultra-persist`](../dsh-tool-ultra-persist) to save it per session and restore it when the session resumes. - If the plugin is unloaded, all its restrictions are lifted (fail open to "every tool visible", never to "no tools"). ## Finding and routing by intent The directory above is browsable, but the model still has to guess the right keywords and spend turns searching. The core now ships a retrieval + routing layer that makes an unbounded catalog usable without that guesswork: ``` tools_find("send an email") # ranked matches (BM25), no loading tools_route("send an email") # retrieve, re-rank with the model, then load skills_find("write a PR") # ranked skills, no loading skills_route("write a PR") # retrieve, re-rank, then load the top skill's body ``` Retrieval is BM25 by default: no model, no network, works offline, and scales to a large catalog. The BM25 index lives in a Rust sidecar process (`sidecar/`, tantivy over a Unix socket) for headroom — the hot path is native and the TypeScript here is a thin client. A dependency-free JS BM25 index is kept as the always-available fallback, so retrieval never breaks if the sidecar binary is missing or the process dies. When a model is configured (`config.model { provider, model }`), `tools_route` and `skills_route` re-rank the BM25 candidates with the model, so a natural-language intent that shares no words with a tool name still finds it — the RAG-MCP pattern: retrieve a small candidate set, then rank it. Any model failure falls back to the BM25 order, so the router never breaks on a model hiccup. The router reuses the core's `toolCatalog` service: it indexes the same catalog, loads through the same path, and reports the same token budget. The sidecar is spawned by the plugin and exits with it (a parent-process monitor kills it on a DSH restart). ## Configuration ```yaml - id: tool-manager name: '@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core' config: pinned: [] # extra always-on tools (core DSH tools are built in) unpin: [] # built-in always-on tools to move into the directory exemptProviders: [claude-code] # routes never narrowed (tool list fixed at session start) highRisk: [] # never included in group loads; load individually ``` ### Override files Three files under `$DSH_HOME/tool-manager/` override the config above. Each is read at startup and re-read when the settings panel saves through the API (or `reload*` is called); write them from the panel, or by hand and then reload. | File | Config key it replaces | What it holds | |---|---|---| | `settings.json` | `pinned`, `unpin`, `highRisk` | the lists an operator edits most often | | `metadata.json` | `annotate()` for the same tool | `{ "": { "group", "category", "risk", "summary" } }` | | `exempt.json` | `exemptProviders` | `{ "providers": [...], "sessions": [...] }` | ### The tool manifest A client that receives its tool list once per session — Claude Code, driven by `dsh-oh-my-claude` — cannot discover the directory by asking, because nothing tells it the directory exists. So the catalog is also written out as text, to `~/.claude/dsh-tool-catalog.md`, after every rebuild: ``` ## device (14 tools, Devices) ### adb — load with `tools_load({ targets: ["/device/adb"] })` - adb_install — Install an APK on a device. - adb_shell ! — Run a shell command on a device. ``` The file opens by saying the listed tools are **not callable yet**, then gives the two calls that change that (`tools_ls`, `tools_load`) and the rule to load the smallest thing that covers the task. A `!` marks a high-risk tool. Reading it runs nothing. Add one line to `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` so every Claude session reads it: ``` @~/.claude/dsh-tool-catalog.md ``` The write is skipped when the text did not change, so a rebuild that moves nothing does not cost a prompt re-read. `manifestFile` points it elsewhere, and `''` turns it off. The files win as a whole, not key by key: once `exempt.json` exists, the config list is ignored rather than merged, so what the file shows is what is in force. A missing file means "no opinion, use the config"; a corrupt file is reported as a warning and treated as empty rather than silently restoring the config. `sessions` exempts one session by id for its remaining lifetime, for checking whether a client handles late loading without de-exempting the whole route. A tool's `metadata.json` entry replaces the previous entry as a whole: submitting the form with a field blank drops that override, and the package declaration (or a classifier) applies again. `parameters` are deliberately not part of it — the host owns the schema sent to the model. ## Extending: the `toolCatalog` service Declare `inject: ['toolCatalog']` (or use `ctx.inject(['toolCatalog'], …)` for an optional dependency) and register inside an effect so that unloading your plugin undoes the registration. ### Classifiers A classifier may place tools into groups and/or groups into categories. Return `undefined` to pass. ```js export const name = 'my-classifier' export const inject = ['toolCatalog'] export function apply(ctx) { ctx.effect(() => ctx.toolCatalog.registerClassifier({ name: 'my-classifier', priority: 200, group: (tool) => (tool.name.startsWith('lingshu_') ? 'lingshu' : undefined), categorize: (group) => (group.name === 'lingshu' ? 'system' : undefined), })) } ``` Resolution order: classifiers with `priority >= 1000` (user overrides) → plugin declarations → other classifiers, highest priority first → structural fallback (`mcp__server__…` → `server`, shared `prefix_` → `prefix`, else `misc`; category `uncategorized`). A classifier that throws is skipped. ### Declaring your own tools Plugin authors know their tools best. Declare them in your `package.json`: ```json { "dsh": { "toolCatalog": { "match": "^adb_", "group": "adb", "category": "device", "tools": { "adb_install": { "risk": "high", "summary": "Install an APK." } } } } } ``` or at runtime: ```js ctx.effect(() => ctx.toolCatalog.annotate('^adb_', { category: 'device' })) ctx.effect(() => ctx.toolCatalog.annotate('adb_install', { risk: 'high' })) ``` Fields: `group`, `category`, `risk` (`"high"`), `summary`. Exact-name entries win over `match`; runtime annotations win over `package.json`. ### Tool packs A package of tools can register itself as a pack. It is then listed in the panel's Packs tab, and it can be loaded in one call with `tools_load(["pack:"])`: ```js ctx.inject(['toolCatalog'], (c) => c.effect(() => c.toolCatalog.registerToolPack({ id: 'web', title: 'Web reading', source: '@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-web', tools: ['web_read', 'web_links'], // exact names or RegExps items: () => [], // optional per-part status for the panel })) ``` ### New categories ```js ctx.effect(() => ctx.toolCatalog.defineCategory('games', 'Game servers and bots')) ``` ### High-risk gates A gate declares that a plugin confirms high-risk loads (normally by returning `{ kind: 'ask' }` from `tools/pre-execute` for `tools_load`). **With no gate registered, high-risk tools cannot be loaded at all** — they are skipped in group loads and refused individually. That is deliberate: a deployment without an approval path should not be able to arm them. ```js ctx.effect(() => ctx.toolCatalog.registerRiskGate({ name: 'my-policy' })) ctx.effect(() => ctx.on('tools/pre-execute', async (exec, next) => { if (exec.name !== 'tools_load' || !needsConfirmation(exec.arguments)) return next() return { kind: 'ask', reason: 'Loading a high-risk tool' } })) ``` See [`dsh-tool-ultra-risk-gate`](../dsh-tool-ultra-risk-gate). ### Persistence Loaded state lives in memory; a state provider makes it outlive the process. ```js ctx.effect(() => ctx.toolCatalog.registerStateProvider({ name: 'my-store', load: (agent) => readFromMyStore(agent.id), // serialized state or null save: (agent, state) => writeToMyStore(agent.id, state), })) ``` Providers are consulted in registration order (first non-null wins) and all receive every save. `exportState(agent)` / `importState(agent, state)` are the plain-JSON equivalents. See [`dsh-tool-ultra-persist`](../dsh-tool-ultra-persist). ### Hooks Plain Cordis events on the host context: | Event | Kind | Payload | |---|---|---| | `tool-catalog/before-load` | serial; throw to veto | `{ agent, targets, names }` | | `tool-catalog/after-load` | emit | `{ agent, targets, added }` | | `tool-catalog/before-unload` | serial; throw to veto | `{ agent, targets }` | | `tool-catalog/after-unload` | emit | `{ agent, targets, removed }` | | `tool-catalog/before-rebuild` | emit | `{}` | | `tool-catalog/after-rebuild` | emit | `{ catalog }` | | `tool-catalog/state-changed` | emit | `{ agent, state }` (plain JSON, after every load/unload) | ```js // A per-session quota: at most 60 visible tools. ctx.on('tool-catalog/before-load', ({ agent, names }) => { const now = ctx.toolCatalog.allowFor(agent)?.length ?? 0 if (now + names.length > 60) throw new Error('tool quota reached; unload something first') }) ``` ### Visibility filters A filter receives the agent and the computed allowlist and returns the names to keep. It can only narrow; it can never add tools or hide the entry tools. ```js // Keep GitHub write tools away from bot sessions. ctx.effect(() => ctx.toolCatalog.registerVisibilityFilter({ name: 'no-github-writes-for-bots', filter: (agent, names) => (agent.id.startsWith('bot-') ? names.filter((n) => !/^mcp__github__(create|delete|merge|push|update)/.test(n)) : names), })) ``` ### Reading the catalog `ctx.toolCatalog.get()` returns `{ tools, groups, categories }`; `resolve(target)`, `stateOf(agent)`, `allowFor(agent)`, `deniedFor(agent)` (allowed here but hidden by another layer), `isExempt(agent)`, `packages()` (enabled plugin packages: `{ name, dir, manifest }`) and `refresh()` are also available. ## Tests See the repository root. ## License Apache-2.0

Tool Ultra
On-demand tool loading for DeepSeek Harness — every tool as a directory, loaded only when an agent asks.

English · 中文

--- ## What It Is Tool Ultra is an All-in-One tool-plugin product for DeepSeek Harness, and an important component of [Swiftnest](https://github.com/lvy-jsd/swiftnest). Its goal is one coherent tool product across everyday tasks, web/MCP services, media and device capabilities. The small core and replaceable extension packages are its internal architecture; the product is more than a tool-directory browser. Tools are browsable as a directory (category → group → tool), searchable by intent and loaded on demand, keeping unneeded schemas out of the model's context. Savings depend on catalog size, discovery/load steps and provider caching: compare per-request schemas, total task tokens and task success separately. Broad capability does not mean every external service or upload is enabled by default. The current preview is distributed as source and modular packages; Swiftnest builds a pinned source commit. An AI can install and configure the required modules. The published-package quick-start syntax below applies when those package versions are available on npm; it is not a claim that the renamed 0.5.0 packages have already been published. > **Renamed.** This project was `dsh-tool-manager`. Version 0.5.0 renames every > package from `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager-` to `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-` > (the core is `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core`). Nothing else changes: the entry > tools, the `toolCatalog` service (now also provided as `toolUltra`), the hooks, > the config and the state directory `/tool-manager/` stay the same. > An existing profile can keep `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager`: from 0.5.0 it only > re-exports the new core. Older extension releases keep working with the new core. ## Quick start ```sh # 1. install the core plus the rule-based classifier (optional but recommended) dsh plugin --profile web add @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-rules # 2. restart DSH, then ask the agent: "what tools do you have?" # it answers with tools_ls("/") — a directory, not 200 tool schemas # 3. want the UI? add the panel, then open Settings → "Tool manager" dsh plugin --profile web add @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-panel ``` > **Install the scoped `@lvy-jsd/…` packages.** The unscoped `dsh-tool-manager` > on npm is a different project. Do not install both: each one narrows which > tools an agent can see, so together they hide tools from each other. On a fresh install every group is `uncategorized` until a classifier is installed — the tools are still browsable and loadable, only the categories are missing. See [Extending](#extending) to write your own classifier. `tools_load(["web"])` also accepts bare names: try registered `pack:` → `cap:` → `device:` namespaces, first non-empty match only, then normal directory lookup; explicit prefixes keep their behavior and plugin ownership. ## Packages | Package | What it does | |---|---| | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-core) | Core: directory, `tools_ls` / `tools_load` / `tools_unload`, per-agent allowlist, the `toolCatalog` extension service, plus intent retrieval + routing (`tools_find` / `tools_route` / `skills_find` / `skills_route`, BM25 with a Rust sidecar). Without extensions every group is `uncategorized`. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-rules`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-rules) | Places groups into categories from built-in rules and your config overrides. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-risk-gate`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-risk-gate) | Confirms loading high-risk tools through the DSH approval channel, with a per-session allowlist. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-persist`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-persist) | Keeps loaded tools across a DSH restart, one state file per session. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-panel`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-panel) | Web panel: browse the tree, see each live session's loaded tools and token cost, load/unload from the UI, edit the always-on and high-risk lists, edit one tool's metadata, exempt one session. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-llm`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-llm) | Places groups with a small model, one request per group, cached by a hash of the group and its tool descriptions. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-capability-bridge`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-capability-bridge) | Load a named bundle of tools in one call: `tools_load(["cap:android-debug"])`. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-attribution-scan`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-attribution-scan) | Group tools by the plugin package whose source defines them. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-essentials`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-essentials) | Native tool pack, no API keys: time zones and date math, a calculator with units (mathjs), weather (Open-Meteo), place search (Nominatim), Wikipedia. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-web`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-web) | Native tool pack: `web_read` turns a page into clean Markdown (Readability + turndown), `web_links` lists its links. Refuses private addresses by default. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-mcp`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-mcp) | MCP presets through DSH's MCP client: memory, sequential thinking, Context7, Playwright and filesystem start without keys; GitHub, SearXNG, Brave, Tavily, Firecrawl, Notion and AMap start once their key is set. `mcp_presets` shows the status. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-media`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-media) | Native tool pack, no API keys: images, music and video made from code. `html_render` designs an image in HTML/CSS (no browser) or turns its CSS animations into a GIF, `svg_render` turns an SVG drawing into PNG/JPEG/WebP, `chart_render` draws a Vega-Lite chart, `music_render` plays a score with real recorded instruments (SoundFont, mastered) and saves WAV and MIDI, `video_render` makes an MP4 from CSS-animated HTML, SVG or photo scenes with transitions, captions and a soundtrack (host ffmpeg), `audio_transcribe` turns speech into timestamped text with local SenseVoice / Whisper models, with who speaks when, emotions and sounds such as laughter, `video_understand` reads a video as a timestamped storyboard image plus its transcript. External links and data URLs are refused. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-gc`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-gc) | Artifact and media garbage collection: date-partitioned storage management (`[YYYY-MM-DD]`), retention sweeps, and LRU capacity eviction. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-db`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-db) | In-memory OLAP analytics via embedded DuckDB: query CSV, Parquet, and JSON datasets directly via SQL without context inflation. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-office`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-office) | Office documents pack: Word (.docx) text extraction, Excel (.xlsx) read/write, and PDF document metadata inspection. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-devices`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-devices) | Device namespace: Swiftnest device tools under `/device/`, loadable as `device:current`, `device:all` or `device:`, with offline devices marked. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager-dsbot-entry`](packages/dsh-tool-manager-dsbot-entry) | Deprecated, no longer released. A "Tool manager" row in the ds-bot settings dialog that opens the panel. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager`](packages/dsh-tool-manager) | The old core name: re-exports `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core` so existing profiles keep working. | | [`@lvy-jsd/create-dsh-tool-ultra-plugin`](packages/create-dsh-tool-ultra-plugin) | Scaffold your own extension: `npm create @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-plugin@latest my-ext -- --type classifier`. | See [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md) for the design. ## Extending Every feature beyond the core is an ordinary plugin using the `toolCatalog` service, and the bundled `classifier-rules` package is written exactly as a third party would write it. Four extension points: | Point | For | |---|---| | `registerClassifier({ name, priority, group?, categorize? })` | placing tools into groups and groups into categories | | `annotate(match, { group?, category?, risk?, summary? })` | runtime metadata; `package.json` `dsh.toolCatalog` does the same without code | | `registerVisibilityFilter({ name, filter(agent, names) })` | narrowing what one agent may see — can only remove names | | `registerTargetResolver({ name, prefix, resolve })` | owning a target prefix, e.g. `cap:` | | `registerRiskGate` / `registerStateProvider` | confirming high-risk loads / keeping state across a restart | Hooks are plain events: `tool-catalog/before-load` (throw to veto), `after-load`, `before-unload`, `after-unload`, `before-rebuild`, `after-rebuild`, `state-changed`. Start from a generated package — it comes with a passing test: ```sh npm create @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-plugin@latest my-ext -- --type classifier cd my-ext && npm test ``` Two worked examples live in [`examples/`](examples), and the full interface list is in the core README and [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md) §11. ## Development Every package is written in TypeScript (`src/`) and compiled to `lib/` (JavaScript plus `.d.ts` type declarations); `lib/` is build output and not committed. The root `tsconfig.json` lists the packages (project references); the two browser halves (`client.ts`) have their own `tsconfig.client.json`, because DSH loads them as classic scripts, not modules. ```sh npm install # also links your local DSH host packages (scripts/link-host.mjs) npm run build # src/*.ts -> lib/*.js + lib/*.d.ts npm run typecheck # strict type check (tsc -b; writes lib/ too, references need it) node --test test/unit/*.test.mjs # pure catalog and registry tests (needs a build) node test/e2e.mjs # boots throwaway DSH instances; never touches your profile ``` Host packages (`@deepseek-ai/*`) are peers and are never installed from the registry (`.npmrc` sets `legacy-peer-deps`): a registry copy next to the plugin would shadow the DSH you actually run. `npm install` links them from `$DSH_APP` (default `~/.local/share/deepseek-harness/app`) instead. ## License Apache-2.0 — see [LICENSE](LICENSE). Releases before Tool Ultra (`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager*`) were MIT.

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-devices This is the device namespace for [Tool Ultra](https://github.com/lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra). Phones and computers connect through [Swiftnest](https://github.com/lvy-jsd/swiftnest), and their tools show up under `/device/`: ``` tools_ls("/device") /device/ Phones and computers laptop/ 2 tools 0 loaded … (EliteBook, desktop) pixel/ 2 tools 0 loaded … (Pixel 8, android) [offline, last seen …] tools_load(["device:current"]) # the device the user is chatting from tools_load(["device:all"]) # every device tools_load(["device:pixel"]) # one device tools_load(["device:current/screen_capture"]) # one capability tools_load(["device:laptop/files"]) # one area: files_read, files_write, ... ``` ## Contract with the device hub The device hub and this plugin agree on two things. - **Tool names.** Each tool is named `device____` (registered natively), where a capability is `_`, such as `files_read` or `shell_run`, or `mcp__swiftnest____` (reached over MCP). The first Swiftnest build serves its MCP server as `devices`, so `mcp__devices____` is accepted too until it switches to native names. A slug is `[a-z0-9_-]{1,24}`, is set when the device pairs, and never changes. The same capability has the same name on every device. - **Device service.** The hub provides a DSH service, `swiftnestDevices` by default: - `list()` returns `{ slug, name, kind, online, lastSeen }[]`. - `currentFor(sessionId)` returns the slug of the session's current device. - The hub emits `swiftnest/devices-changed` whenever the device list changes. Approval stays with the device hub, which shows the user a card on their current device. Loading a device tool asks for nothing extra. The full draft is in the project files (`tool-ultra/device-interface.md`). The names can be changed in config: `prefixes`, `service`, `changeEvent`. ## Live test with Swiftnest `scripts/swiftnest-integration.mjs` boots a real Swiftnest server (its pinned DSH kernel and device hub) in a throwaway home, pairs a Node Perch named `laptop` with files and shell, adds Tool Ultra through `user.patch.yml`, and drives a scripted model through `tools_ls /device`, `device:laptop/files`, a real `files_read`, `device:current` and an offline listing.
