Its goal is one coherent tool product across everyday tasks, web/MCP services, media and device capabilities. The small core and replaceable extension packages are its internal architecture; the product is more than a tool-directory browser. Tools are browsable as a directory (category → group → tool), searchable by intent and loaded on demand, keeping unneeded schemas out of the model's context. Savings depend on catalog size, discovery/load steps and provider caching: compare per-request schemas, total task tokens and task success separately. Broad capability does not mean every external service or upload is enabled by default. The current preview is distributed as source and modular packages; Swiftnest builds a pinned source commit. An AI can install and configure the required modules. The published-package quick-start syntax below applies when those package versions are available on npm; it is not a claim that the renamed 0.5.0 packages have already been published. > **Renamed.** This project was `dsh-tool-manager`. Version 0.5.0 renames every > package from `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager-` to `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-` > (the core is `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core`). Nothing else changes: the entry > tools, the `toolCatalog` service (now also provided as `toolUltra`), the hooks, > the config and the state directory `/tool-manager/` stay the same. > An existing profile can keep `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager`: from 0.5.0 it only > re-exports the new core. Older extension releases keep working with the new core. ## Quick start ```sh # 1. install the core plus the rule-based classifier (optional but recommended) dsh plugin --profile web add @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-rules # 2. restart DSH, then ask the agent: "what tools do you have?" # it answers with tools_ls("/") — a directory, not 200 tool schemas # 3. want the UI? add the panel, then open Settings → "Tool manager" dsh plugin --profile web add @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-panel ``` > **Install the scoped `@lvy-jsd/…` packages.** The unscoped `dsh-tool-manager` > on npm is a different project. Do not install both: each one narrows which > tools an agent can see, so together they hide tools from each other. On a fresh install every group is `uncategorized` until a classifier is installed — the tools are still browsable and loadable, only the categories are missing. See [Extending](#extending) to write your own classifier. `tools_load(["web"])` also accepts bare names: try registered `pack:` → `cap:` → `device:` namespaces, first non-empty match only, then normal directory lookup; explicit prefixes keep their behavior and plugin ownership. ## Packages | Package | What it does | |---|---| | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-core) | Core: directory, `tools_ls` / `tools_load` / `tools_unload`, per-agent allowlist, the `toolCatalog` extension service, plus intent retrieval + routing (`tools_find` / `tools_route` / `skills_find` / `skills_route`, BM25 with a Rust sidecar). Without extensions every group is `uncategorized`. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-rules`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-rules) | Places groups into categories from built-in rules and your config overrides. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-risk-gate`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-risk-gate) | Confirms loading high-risk tools through the DSH approval channel, with a per-session allowlist. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-persist`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-persist) | Keeps loaded tools across a DSH restart, one state file per session. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-panel`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-panel) | Web panel: browse the tree, see each live session's loaded tools and token cost, load/unload from the UI, edit the always-on and high-risk lists, edit one tool's metadata, exempt one session. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-llm`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-llm) | Places groups with a small model, one request per group, cached by a hash of the group and its tool descriptions. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-capability-bridge`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-capability-bridge) | Load a named bundle of tools in one call: `tools_load(["cap:android-debug"])`. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-attribution-scan`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-attribution-scan) | Group tools by the plugin package whose source defines them. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-essentials`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-essentials) | Native tool pack, no API keys: time zones and date math, a calculator with units (mathjs), weather (Open-Meteo), place search (Nominatim), Wikipedia. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-web`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-web) | Native tool pack: `web_read` turns a page into clean Markdown (Readability + turndown), `web_links` lists its links. Refuses private addresses by default. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-mcp`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-mcp) | MCP presets through DSH's MCP client: memory, sequential thinking, Context7, Playwright and filesystem start without keys; GitHub, SearXNG, Brave, Tavily, Firecrawl, Notion and AMap start once their key is set. `mcp_presets` shows the status. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-media`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-media) | Native tool pack, no API keys: images, music and video made from code. `html_render` designs an image in HTML/CSS (no browser) or turns its CSS animations into a GIF, `svg_render` turns an SVG drawing into PNG/JPEG/WebP, `chart_render` draws a Vega-Lite chart, `music_render` plays a score with real recorded instruments (SoundFont, mastered) and saves WAV and MIDI, `video_render` makes an MP4 from CSS-animated HTML, SVG or photo scenes with transitions, captions and a soundtrack (host ffmpeg), `audio_transcribe` turns speech into timestamped text with local SenseVoice / Whisper models, with who speaks when, emotions and sounds such as laughter, `video_understand` reads a video as a timestamped storyboard image plus its transcript. External links and data URLs are refused. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-gc`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-gc) | Artifact and media garbage collection: date-partitioned storage management (`[YYYY-MM-DD]`), retention sweeps, and LRU capacity eviction. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-db`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-db) | In-memory OLAP analytics via embedded DuckDB: query CSV, Parquet, and JSON datasets directly via SQL without context inflation. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-office`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-office) | Office documents pack: Word (.docx) text extraction, Excel (.xlsx) read/write, and PDF document metadata inspection. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-devices`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-devices) | Device namespace: Swiftnest device tools under `/device/`, loadable as `device:current`, `device:all` or `device:`, with offline devices marked. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager-dsbot-entry`](packages/dsh-tool-manager-dsbot-entry) | Deprecated, no longer released. A "Tool manager" row in the ds-bot settings dialog that opens the panel. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager`](packages/dsh-tool-manager) | The old core name: re-exports `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core` so existing profiles keep working. | | [`@lvy-jsd/create-dsh-tool-ultra-plugin`](packages/create-dsh-tool-ultra-plugin) | Scaffold your own extension: `npm create @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-plugin@latest my-ext -- --type classifier`. | See [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md) for the design. ## Extending Every feature beyond the core is an ordinary plugin using the `toolCatalog` service, and the bundled `classifier-rules` package is written exactly as a third party would write it. Four extension points: | Point | For | |---|---| | `registerClassifier({ name, priority, group?, categorize? })` | placing tools into groups and groups into categories | | `annotate(match, { group?, category?, risk?, summary? })` | runtime metadata; `package.json` `dsh.toolCatalog` does the same without code | | `registerVisibilityFilter({ name, filter(agent, names) })` | narrowing what one agent may see — can only remove names | | `registerTargetResolver({ name, prefix, resolve })` | owning a target prefix, e.g. `cap:` | | `registerRiskGate` / `registerStateProvider` | confirming high-risk loads / keeping state across a restart | Hooks are plain events: `tool-catalog/before-load` (throw to veto), `after-load`, `before-unload`, `after-unload`, `before-rebuild`, `after-rebuild`, `state-changed`. Start from a generated package — it comes with a passing test: ```sh npm create @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-plugin@latest my-ext -- --type classifier cd my-ext && npm test ``` Two worked examples live in [`examples/`](examples), and the full interface list is in the core README and [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md) §11. ## Development Every package is written in TypeScript (`src/`) and compiled to `lib/` (JavaScript plus `.d.ts` type declarations); `lib/` is build output and not committed. The root `tsconfig.json` lists the packages (project references); the two browser halves (`client.ts`) have their own `tsconfig.client.json`, because DSH loads them as classic scripts, not modules. ```sh npm install # also links your local DSH host packages (scripts/link-host.mjs) npm run build # src/*.ts -> lib/*.js + lib/*.d.ts npm run typecheck # strict type check (tsc -b; writes lib/ too, references need it) node --test test/unit/*.test.mjs # pure catalog and registry tests (needs a build) node test/e2e.mjs # boots throwaway DSH instances; never touches your profile ``` Host packages (`@deepseek-ai/*`) are peers and are never installed from the registry (`.npmrc` sets `legacy-peer-deps`): a registry copy next to the plugin would shadow the DSH you actually run. `npm install` links them from `$DSH_APP` (default `~/.local/share/deepseek-harness/app`) instead. ## License Apache-2.0 — see [LICENSE](LICENSE). # @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-code-insight **Only JavaScript / TypeScript is supported** (`.js/.jsx/.mjs/.cjs` and `.ts/.tsx/.mts/.cts`) using `@babel/parser`. Python, Rust and Go regex parsers have been removed. Multi-language support requires a separately reviewed Tree-sitter implementation; this release does not claim it. ## Tools | Tool | Group / category | What it does | | --- | --- | --- | | `code_outline` | code / system | Top-level declarations, class methods, imports and exports; no function bodies in output. | | `code_symbols` | code / system | Search declaration names and file/line locations. | | `code_callgraph` | code / system | Legacy name: lists static module imports, **not function calls** or resolved cross-file semantics. | These are structural summaries, not type checking, complete symbol resolution or a substitute for reading the source before editing. Local parsing reads source bodies; only the output omits them. No fixed token-saving percentage is claimed. Unsupported file requests and malformed syntax fail explicitly. Directory scans ignore unsupported languages and symlinks, reject more than 50 supported files or depth over 12, and limit each regular file to 2 MB. Parse failures are reported, not silently turned into a misleading empty outline. Host file permissions apply; this pack is not a filesystem sandbox. ## Register and load Build the workspace with `npm install` / `npm run build`, using `DSH_APP` to link host peers (see root README). Add/link the package to the DSH profile's dependencies and bundles; `cordis.patch.yml` mounts the plugin. For published versions: ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-code-insight ``` Then `tools_load({targets:["pack:code-insight"]})` exposes the three tools through Tool Ultra. Config: `disable`, `maxDepth` (outline request range 1–10), `maxSymbols`. ## Validation `node --test test/unit/pack-code-insight.test.mjs` checks TS exports and methods, JSX/CommonJS/CTS handling, unsupported-language refusal, syntax failure, symbols and static imports. No cross-language or semantic-call-graph acceptance is implied.

External links and data URLs are refused. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-gc`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-gc) | Artifact and media garbage collection: date-partitioned storage management (`[YYYY-MM-DD]`), retention sweeps, and LRU capacity eviction. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-db`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-db) | In-memory OLAP analytics via embedded DuckDB: query CSV, Parquet, and JSON datasets directly via SQL without context inflation. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-office`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-office) | Office documents pack: Word (.docx) text extraction, Excel (.xlsx) read/write, and PDF document metadata inspection. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-devices`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-devices) | Device namespace: Swiftnest device tools under `/device/`, loadable as `device:current`, `device:all` or `device:`, with offline devices marked. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager-dsbot-entry`](packages/dsh-tool-manager-dsbot-entry) | Deprecated, no longer released. A "Tool manager" row in the ds-bot settings dialog that opens the panel. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager`](packages/dsh-tool-manager) | The old core name: re-exports `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core` so existing profiles keep working. | | [`@lvy-jsd/create-dsh-tool-ultra-plugin`](packages/create-dsh-tool-ultra-plugin) | Scaffold your own extension: `npm create @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-plugin@latest my-ext -- --type classifier`. | See [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md) for the design. ## Extending Every feature beyond the core is an ordinary plugin using the `toolCatalog` service, and the bundled `classifier-rules` package is written exactly as a third party would write it. Four extension points: | Point | For | |---|---| | `registerClassifier({ name, priority, group?, categorize? })` | placing tools into groups and groups into categories | | `annotate(match, { group?, category?, risk?, summary? })` | runtime metadata; `package.json` `dsh.toolCatalog` does the same without code | | `registerVisibilityFilter({ name, filter(agent, names) })` | narrowing what one agent may see — can only remove names | | `registerTargetResolver({ name, prefix, resolve })` | owning a target prefix, e.g. `cap:` | | `registerRiskGate` / `registerStateProvider` | confirming high-risk loads / keeping state across a restart | Hooks are plain events: `tool-catalog/before-load` (throw to veto), `after-load`, `before-unload`, `after-unload`, `before-rebuild`, `after-rebuild`, `state-changed`. Start from a generated package — it comes with a passing test: ```sh npm create @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-plugin@latest my-ext -- --type classifier cd my-ext && npm test ``` Two worked examples live in [`examples/`](examples), and the full interface list is in the core README and [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md) §11. ## Development Every package is written in TypeScript (`src/`) and compiled to `lib/` (JavaScript plus `.d.ts` type declarations); `lib/` is build output and not committed. # @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-db Database and analytical data queries for [Tool Ultra](https://github.com/lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra). Uses the official `@duckdb/node-api` binding for embedded SQL analytics over local CSV, Parquet and JSON files. Files are scanned by DuckDB, not read into a full JavaScript array. This is not a claim of zero-copy execution. ## Query lifetime Each `db_query` call runs in a fresh in-memory database. Tables, transactions and session settings do not persist across calls; use a single SQL call or query local files directly. `db_load_file` also releases its inspection databases before it returns. Results, connections and instances are explicitly released with the binding's `closeSync()` APIs in nested `finally` blocks, also on read/SQL failures. Cleanup errors are reported rather than ignored. Immediate dataset deletion after success and failure is covered by the Windows CI regression test. ## Large datasets and JSON values `maxRows` defaults to 500 (allowed range 1–10000). Queries stream into a bounded prefix: at most the requested row count plus lookahead and one native chunk is retained as JS rows, rather than fetching the entire result before truncating. The response reports when additional rows are omitted; it does not invent a total count. SQL sorts, joins and aggregations can still consume native memory or scan the complete dataset; the row cap is not a SQL execution or byte-memory quota. `db_load_file` returns schema plus five sample rows without copying the whole file into JS. Tests generate a >25 MB / 250,000-row CSV and check prefix reading, inspection, exact aggregate results and immediate deletion. The official JSON converter preserves BIGINT/HUGEINT and DECIMAL as strings, including nested values, rather than rounding them through JavaScript numbers. ## Tools | Tool | Group / category | What it does | | --- | --- | --- | | `db_query` | data / system | Execute SQL queries in-memory using DuckDB. Supports direct querying of Parquet/CSV files (e.g. `SELECT * FROM 'data.parquet' WHERE ...`). | | `db_load_file` | data / system | Describe and inspect local CSV, Parquet, or JSON datasets: returns schema metadata and the first 5 sample rows without dumping large datasets into the context window. |

Four extension points: | Point | For | |---|---| | `registerClassifier({ name, priority, group?, categorize? })` | placing tools into groups and groups into categories | | `annotate(match, { group?, category?, risk?, summary? })` | runtime metadata; `package.json` `dsh.toolCatalog` does the same without code | | `registerVisibilityFilter({ name, filter(agent, names) })` | narrowing what one agent may see — can only remove names | | `registerTargetResolver({ name, prefix, resolve })` | owning a target prefix, e.g. `cap:` | | `registerRiskGate` / `registerStateProvider` | confirming high-risk loads / keeping state across a restart | Hooks are plain events: `tool-catalog/before-load` (throw to veto), `after-load`, `before-unload`, `after-unload`, `before-rebuild`, `after-rebuild`, `state-changed`. Start from a generated package — it comes with a passing test: ```sh npm create @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-plugin@latest my-ext -- --type classifier cd my-ext && npm test ``` Two worked examples live in [`examples/`](examples), and the full interface list is in the core README and [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md) §11. ## Development Every package is written in TypeScript (`src/`) and compiled to `lib/` (JavaScript plus `.d.ts` type declarations); `lib/` is build output and not committed. The root `tsconfig.json` lists the packages (project references); the two browser halves (`client.ts`) have their own `tsconfig.client.json`, because DSH loads them as classic scripts, not modules. ```sh npm install # also links your local DSH host packages (scripts/link-host.mjs) npm run build # src/*.ts -> lib/*.js + lib/*.d.ts npm run typecheck # strict type check (tsc -b; writes lib/ too, references need it) node --test test/unit/*.test.mjs # pure catalog and registry tests (needs a build) node test/e2e.mjs # boots throwaway DSH instances; never touches your profile ``` Host packages (`@deepseek-ai/*`) are peers and are never installed from the registry (`.npmrc` sets `legacy-peer-deps`): a registry copy next to the plugin would shadow the DSH you actually run. `npm install` links them from `$DSH_APP` (default `~/.local/share/deepseek-harness/app`) instead. ## License Apache-2.0 — see [LICENSE](LICENSE). Releases before Tool Ultra (`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager*`) were MIT.

Repository rename to dsh-tool-ultra was verified by numeric repository ID. Exact npm lookup is 404; the nested TypeScript pack exports lib/index.js that is absent in the fixed source and relies on prepack tsc. Native DuckDB readOnly tools are identifiable, but publication/build mapping is incomplete. Prepack was only read, never run. No candidate code or lifecycle hooks were executed; runtime safety and compatibility are unproven.

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-essentials Everyday tools for [Tool Ultra](https://github.com/lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra). None of them need an API key. | Tool | Group / category | What it does | Data source | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `time_now` | time / system | Current time in any IANA zone | `Intl` (local) | | `time_convert` | time / system | Convert a time between zones | `Intl` (local) | | `date_diff` | time / system | Time between two dates | local | | `math_eval` | math / system | Exact math, statistics, matrices, units ("60 mph to km/h") | [mathjs](https://mathjs.org) (local) | | `weather_forecast` | weather / maps | Current weather and up to 16 days of forecast | [Open-Meteo](https://open-meteo.com) | | `geo_search` | places / maps | Place and address lookup, reverse geocoding | [Nominatim](https://nominatim.org) (OpenStreetMap) | | `wiki_search` | wikipedia / search | Search any Wikipedia language edition | Wikimedia REST | | `wiki_summary` | wikipedia / search | Lead section of one page | Wikimedia REST | Tool names do not collide with DSH's built-in `web_fetch` and `web_search`. ## Install The pack is a normal DSH plugin. With Tool Ultra installed, it shows up under `/system`, `/maps` and `/search` in `tools_ls`. ```yaml # cordis.patch.yml (shipped in this package) - insert: - id: tool-ultra-pack-essentials name: '@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-essentials' config: disable: [] # tool names to skip userAgent: 'dsh-tool-ultra (+https://github.com/lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra)' timeoutMs: 10000 wikiLang: en # default Wikipedia edition, e.g. zh ``` Nominatim's usage policy asks for at most one request per second and an identifying User-Agent. Set `userAgent` to something that names your deployment if you run it for many users. ## License Apache-2.0. Weather data © Open-Meteo (CC BY 4.0). Map data © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL). Wikipedia text is CC BY-SA.

Tool Ultra
On-demand tool loading for DeepSeek Harness — every tool as a directory, loaded only when an agent asks.

English · 中文

--- ## What It Is Tool Ultra is an All-in-One tool-plugin product for DeepSeek Harness, and an important component of [Swiftnest](https://github.com/lvy-jsd/swiftnest). Its goal is one coherent tool product across everyday tasks, web/MCP services, media and device capabilities. The small core and replaceable extension packages are its internal architecture; the product is more than a tool-directory browser. Tools are browsable as a directory (category → group → tool), searchable by intent and loaded on demand, keeping unneeded schemas out of the model's context. Savings depend on catalog size, discovery/load steps and provider caching: compare per-request schemas, total task tokens and task success separately. Broad capability does not mean every external service or upload is enabled by default. The current preview is distributed as source and modular packages; Swiftnest builds a pinned source commit. An AI can install and configure the required modules. The published-package quick-start syntax below applies when those package versions are available on npm; it is not a claim that the renamed 0.5.0 packages have already been published. > **Renamed.** This project was `dsh-tool-manager`. Version 0.5.0 renames every > package from `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager-` to `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-` > (the core is `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core`). Nothing else changes: the entry > tools, the `toolCatalog` service (now also provided as `toolUltra`), the hooks, > the config and the state directory `/tool-manager/` stay the same. > An existing profile can keep `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager`: from 0.5.0 it only > re-exports the new core. Older extension releases keep working with the new core. ## Quick start ```sh # 1. install the core plus the rule-based classifier (optional but recommended) dsh plugin --profile web add @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-rules # 2. restart DSH, then ask the agent: "what tools do you have?" # it answers with tools_ls("/") — a directory, not 200 tool schemas # 3. want the UI? add the panel, then open Settings → "Tool manager" dsh plugin --profile web add @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-panel ``` > **Install the scoped `@lvy-jsd/…` packages.** The unscoped `dsh-tool-manager` > on npm is a different project. Do not install both: each one narrows which > tools an agent can see, so together they hide tools from each other. On a fresh install every group is `uncategorized` until a classifier is installed — the tools are still browsable and loadable, only the categories are missing. # @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-image-creative Offline image editing via [sharp](https://sharp.pixelplumbing.com/) for Tool Ultra. This version has **no `image_generate` tool**, generation backend, ComfyUI adapter, background removal or external upload. ## Tools | Tool | Group / category | What it does | | --- | --- | --- | | `image_metadata` | image / media | Inspect dimensions, format, channels, color space and alpha. | | `image_edit` | image / media | Resize (cover may crop), rotate, flip/flop, grayscale and encode PNG/JPEG/WebP/AVIF. | Rotation precedes resizing; width/height describe the final resize box. Input images are limited to 40 million pixels and requested dimensions to 8192 per axis. Existing output files are never overwritten. Local paths follow the host's filesystem permissions; this pack is not a filesystem sandbox. Output defaults to date-partitioned `~/dsh-artifacts` or `artifactsDir`. ## Register and load Build this source workspace with `npm install` and `npm run build`, linking host peers through `DSH_APP` as described in the root README. Install/link this package into the DSH profile's dependencies and bundles; its `cordis.patch.yml` mounts the plugin. For published versions the equivalent command is: ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-image-creative ``` With Tool Ultra mounted, `tools_load({targets:["pack:image-creative"]})` exposes only these two tools. Registering the pack does not enable a generation service. ## Validation `node --test test/unit/pack-image-creative.test.mjs` creates real pixels, checks rotation/resize and JPEG/WebP encoding, rejects invalid inputs and overwrites, and verifies no generation schema is registered. Sharp versions match the existing media pack to avoid loading incompatible Windows native libraries.

Tool Ultra
On-demand tool loading for DeepSeek Harness — every tool as a directory, loaded only when an agent asks.

English · 中文

--- ## What It Is Tool Ultra is an All-in-One tool-plugin product for DeepSeek Harness, and an important component of [Swiftnest](https://github.com/lvy-jsd/swiftnest). Its goal is one coherent tool product across everyday tasks, web/MCP services, media and device capabilities. The small core and replaceable extension packages are its internal architecture; the product is more than a tool-directory browser. Tools are browsable as a directory (category → group → tool), searchable by intent and loaded on demand, keeping unneeded schemas out of the model's context. Savings depend on catalog size, discovery/load steps and provider caching: compare per-request schemas, total task tokens and task success separately. Broad capability does not mean every external service or upload is enabled by default. The current preview is distributed as source and modular packages; Swiftnest builds a pinned source commit. An AI can install and configure the required modules. The published-package quick-start syntax below applies when those package versions are available on npm; it is not a claim that the renamed 0.5.0 packages have already been published. > **Renamed.** This project was `dsh-tool-manager`. Version 0.5.0 renames every > package from `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager-` to `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-` > (the core is `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core`). Nothing else changes: the entry > tools, the `toolCatalog` service (now also provided as `toolUltra`), the hooks, > the config and the state directory `/tool-manager/` stay the same. > An existing profile can keep `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager`: from 0.5.0 it only > re-exports the new core. Older extension releases keep working with the new core. ## Quick start ```sh # 1. install the core plus the rule-based classifier (optional but recommended) dsh plugin --profile web add @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-rules # 2. restart DSH, then ask the agent: "what tools do you have?" # it answers with tools_ls("/") — a directory, not 200 tool schemas # 3. want the UI? add the panel, then open Settings → "Tool manager" dsh plugin --profile web add @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-panel ``` > **Install the scoped `@lvy-jsd/…` packages.** The unscoped `dsh-tool-manager` > on npm is a different project. Do not install both: each one narrows which > tools an agent can see, so together they hide tools from each other. On a fresh install every group is `uncategorized` until a classifier is installed — the tools are still browsable and loadable, only the categories are missing. See [Extending](#extending) to write your own classifier. `tools_load(["web"])` also accepts bare names: try registered `pack:` → `cap:` → `device:` namespaces, first non-empty match only, then normal directory lookup; explicit prefixes keep their behavior and plugin ownership. ## Packages | Package | What it does | |---|---| | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-core) | Core: directory, `tools_ls` / `tools_load` / `tools_unload`, per-agent allowlist, the `toolCatalog` extension service, plus intent retrieval + routing (`tools_find` / `tools_route` / `skills_find` / `skills_route`, BM25 with a Rust sidecar). Without extensions every group is `uncategorized`. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-rules`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-rules) | Places groups into categories from built-in rules and your config overrides. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-risk-gate`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-risk-gate) | Confirms loading high-risk tools through the DSH approval channel, with a per-session allowlist. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-persist`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-persist) | Keeps loaded tools across a DSH restart, one state file per session. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-panel`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-panel) | Web panel: browse the tree, see each live session's loaded tools and token cost, load/unload from the UI, edit the always-on and high-risk lists, edit one tool's metadata, exempt one session. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-llm`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-llm) | Places groups with a small model, one request per group, cached by a hash of the group and its tool descriptions. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-capability-bridge`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-capability-bridge) | Load a named bundle of tools in one call: `tools_load(["cap:android-debug"])`. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-attribution-scan`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-attribution-scan) | Group tools by the plugin package whose source defines them. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-essentials`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-essentials) | Native tool pack, no API keys: time zones and date math, a calculator with units (mathjs), weather (Open-Meteo), place search (Nominatim), Wikipedia. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-web`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-web) | Native tool pack: `web_read` turns a page into clean Markdown (Readability + turndown), `web_links` lists its links. Refuses private addresses by default. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-mcp`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-mcp) | MCP presets through DSH's MCP client: memory, sequential thinking, Context7, Playwright and filesystem start without keys; GitHub, SearXNG, Brave, Tavily, Firecrawl, Notion and AMap start once their key is set. `mcp_presets` shows the status. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-media`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-media) | Native tool pack, no API keys: images, music and video made from code. `html_render` designs an image in HTML/CSS (no browser) or turns its CSS animations into a GIF, `svg_render` turns an SVG drawing into PNG/JPEG/WebP, `chart_render` draws a Vega-Lite chart, `music_render` plays a score with real recorded instruments (SoundFont, mastered) and saves WAV and MIDI, `video_render` makes an MP4 from CSS-animated HTML, SVG or photo scenes with transitions, captions and a soundtrack (host ffmpeg), `audio_transcribe` turns speech into timestamped text with local SenseVoice / Whisper models, with who speaks when, emotions and sounds such as laughter, `video_understand` reads a video as a timestamped storyboard image plus its transcript. External links and data URLs are refused. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-gc`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-gc) | Artifact and media garbage collection: date-partitioned storage management (`[YYYY-MM-DD]`), retention sweeps, and LRU capacity eviction. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-db`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-db) | In-memory OLAP analytics via embedded DuckDB: query CSV, Parquet, and JSON datasets directly via SQL without context inflation. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-office`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-office) | Office documents pack: Word (.docx) text extraction, Excel (.xlsx) read/write, and PDF document metadata inspection. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-devices`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-devices) | Device namespace: Swiftnest device tools under `/device/`, loadable as `device:current`, `device:all` or `device:`, with offline devices marked. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager-dsbot-entry`](packages/dsh-tool-manager-dsbot-entry) | Deprecated, no longer released. A "Tool manager" row in the ds-bot settings dialog that opens the panel. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager`](packages/dsh-tool-manager) | The old core name: re-exports `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core` so existing profiles keep working. | | [`@lvy-jsd/create-dsh-tool-ultra-plugin`](packages/create-dsh-tool-ultra-plugin) | Scaffold your own extension: `npm create @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-plugin@latest my-ext -- --type classifier`. | See [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md) for the design. ## Extending Every feature beyond the core is an ordinary plugin using the `toolCatalog` service, and the bundled `classifier-rules` package is written exactly as a third party would write it. Four extension points: | Point | For | |---|---| | `registerClassifier({ name, priority, group?, categorize? })` | placing tools into groups and groups into categories | | `annotate(match, { group?, category?, risk?, summary? })` | runtime metadata; `package.json` `dsh.toolCatalog` does the same without code | | `registerVisibilityFilter({ name, filter(agent, names) })` | narrowing what one agent may see — can only remove names | | `registerTargetResolver({ name, prefix, resolve })` | owning a target prefix, e.g. `cap:` | | `registerRiskGate` / `registerStateProvider` | confirming high-risk loads / keeping state across a restart | Hooks are plain events: `tool-catalog/before-load` (throw to veto), `after-load`, `before-unload`, `after-unload`, `before-rebuild`, `after-rebuild`, `state-changed`. Start from a generated package — it comes with a passing test: ```sh npm create @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-plugin@latest my-ext -- --type classifier cd my-ext && npm test ``` Two worked examples live in [`examples/`](examples), and the full interface list is in the core README and [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md) §11. ## Development Every package is written in TypeScript (`src/`) and compiled to `lib/` (JavaScript plus `.d.ts` type declarations); `lib/` is build output and not committed. # @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-mcp Ready-made MCP servers for [Tool Ultra](https://github.com/lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra). The pack starts each preset through DSH's own MCP client (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client`), one connection per preset. A server's tools appear as `mcp____` and are filed under the preset's category, so they stay out of context until the model loads them with `tools_load`. Presets that need nothing start by default. Presets that need a key or a setting wait until it is present, either in the environment or under `presets..env`. The `mcp_presets` tool lists what is running and what is waiting, and says where to get each missing key. | Preset | Category | Starts | Source | Needs | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `memory` | memory | by default | `@modelcontextprotocol/server-memory` | nothing (`MEMORY_FILE_PATH` optional) | | `thinking` | automation | by default | `@modelcontextprotocol/server-sequential-thinking` | nothing | | `context7` | code | by default | `@upstash/context7-mcp` | nothing (`CONTEXT7_API_KEY` switches it to the hosted endpoint with higher limits) | | `playwright` | browser | by default | `@playwright/mcp`, headless and isolated | nothing, but downloads a browser on first use | | `filesystem` | system | when given roots | `@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem` | `presets.filesystem.roots` | | `github` | code | with a token | GitHub's hosted server `api.githubcopilot.com/mcp` | `GITHUB_TOKEN` | | `searxng` | search | with a URL | `mcp-searxng` | `SEARXNG_URL` | | `brave` | search | with a key | `@brave/brave-search-mcp-server` | `BRAVE_API_KEY` | | `tavily` | search | with a key | Tavily's hosted server | `TAVILY_API_KEY` | | `firecrawl` | browser | with a key | `firecrawl-mcp` | `FIRECRAWL_API_KEY` | | `notion` | collaboration | with a token | `@notionhq/notion-mcp-server` | `NOTION_TOKEN` | | `amap` | maps | with a key | `@amap/amap-maps-mcp-server` (高德地图) | `AMAP_MAPS_API_KEY` | All local presets are TypeScript servers started with `npx`, at pinned versions. GitHub and Tavily use their vendors' hosted HTTP endpoints, so there is no Go or Python on the host. Tools that write, delete or run code (GitHub writes, filesystem writes, Playwright `browser_evaluate`, Notion edits) are marked high risk, so loading them goes through the risk gate. ## Config ```yaml - insert: - id: tool-ultra-pack-mcp name: '@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-mcp' config: defaults: true # start keyless presets without listing them presets: filesystem: { roots: ['/home/me/work'] } github: { env: { GITHUB_TOKEN: !!js process.env.GITHUB_TOKEN } } playwright: { enabled: false } brave: { toolCallTimeoutMs: 30000 } ``` Per-preset options are `enabled`, `env`, `roots` (filesystem only), `args` (extra stdio arguments, playwright only) and `toolCallTimeoutMs`. The host must provide `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` (shipped DSH profiles do). If it is missing, the pack logs a warning, starts nothing, and `mcp_presets` shows why. ## License Apache-2.0. Every server keeps its own license. They are listed in `src/presets.ts`; check them before redistributing.

Tool Ultra
On-demand tool loading for DeepSeek Harness — every tool as a directory, loaded only when an agent asks.

English · 中文

--- ## What It Is Tool Ultra is an All-in-One tool-plugin product for DeepSeek Harness, and an important component of [Swiftnest](https://github.com/lvy-jsd/swiftnest). Its goal is one coherent tool product across everyday tasks, web/MCP services, media and device capabilities. The small core and replaceable extension packages are its internal architecture; the product is more than a tool-directory browser. Tools are browsable as a directory (category → group → tool), searchable by intent and loaded on demand, keeping unneeded schemas out of the model's context. Savings depend on catalog size, discovery/load steps and provider caching: compare per-request schemas, total task tokens and task success separately. Broad capability does not mean every external service or upload is enabled by default. The current preview is distributed as source and modular packages; Swiftnest builds a pinned source commit. An AI can install and configure the required modules. The published-package quick-start syntax below applies when those package versions are available on npm; it is not a claim that the renamed 0.5.0 packages have already been published. > **Renamed.** This project was `dsh-tool-manager`. Version 0.5.0 renames every > package from `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager-` to `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-` > (the core is `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core`). Nothing else changes: the entry > tools, the `toolCatalog` service (now also provided as `toolUltra`), the hooks, > the config and the state directory `/tool-manager/` stay the same. > An existing profile can keep `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager`: from 0.5.0 it only > re-exports the new core. Older extension releases keep working with the new core. ## Quick start ```sh # 1. install the core plus the rule-based classifier (optional but recommended) dsh plugin --profile web add @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-rules # 2. restart DSH, then ask the agent: "what tools do you have?" # it answers with tools_ls("/") — a directory, not 200 tool schemas # 3. want the UI? add the panel, then open Settings → "Tool manager" dsh plugin --profile web add @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-panel ``` > **Install the scoped `@lvy-jsd/…` packages.** The unscoped `dsh-tool-manager` > on npm is a different project. Do not install both: each one narrows which > tools an agent can see, so together they hide tools from each other. On a fresh install every group is `uncategorized` until a classifier is installed — the tools are still browsable and loadable, only the categories are missing. See [Extending](#extending) to write your own classifier. `tools_load(["web"])` also accepts bare names: try registered `pack:` → `cap:` → `device:` namespaces, first non-empty match only, then normal directory lookup; explicit prefixes keep their behavior and plugin ownership. ## Packages | Package | What it does | |---|---| | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-core) | Core: directory, `tools_ls` / `tools_load` / `tools_unload`, per-agent allowlist, the `toolCatalog` extension service, plus intent retrieval + routing (`tools_find` / `tools_route` / `skills_find` / `skills_route`, BM25 with a Rust sidecar). Without extensions every group is `uncategorized`. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-rules`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-rules) | Places groups into categories from built-in rules and your config overrides. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-risk-gate`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-risk-gate) | Confirms loading high-risk tools through the DSH approval channel, with a per-session allowlist. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-persist`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-persist) | Keeps loaded tools across a DSH restart, one state file per session. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-panel`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-panel) | Web panel: browse the tree, see each live session's loaded tools and token cost, load/unload from the UI, edit the always-on and high-risk lists, edit one tool's metadata, exempt one session. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-llm`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-llm) | Places groups with a small model, one request per group, cached by a hash of the group and its tool descriptions. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-capability-bridge`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-capability-bridge) | Load a named bundle of tools in one call: `tools_load(["cap:android-debug"])`. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-attribution-scan`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-attribution-scan) | Group tools by the plugin package whose source defines them. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-essentials`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-essentials) | Native tool pack, no API keys: time zones and date math, a calculator with units (mathjs), weather (Open-Meteo), place search (Nominatim), Wikipedia. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-web`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-web) | Native tool pack: `web_read` turns a page into clean Markdown (Readability + turndown), `web_links` lists its links. Refuses private addresses by default. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-mcp`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-mcp) | MCP presets through DSH's MCP client: memory, sequential thinking, Context7, Playwright and filesystem start without keys; GitHub, SearXNG, Brave, Tavily, Firecrawl, Notion and AMap start once their key is set. `mcp_presets` shows the status. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-media`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-media) | Native tool pack, no API keys: images, music and video made from code. `html_render` designs an image in HTML/CSS (no browser) or turns its CSS animations into a GIF, `svg_render` turns an SVG drawing into PNG/JPEG/WebP, `chart_render` draws a Vega-Lite chart, `music_render` plays a score with real recorded instruments (SoundFont, mastered) and saves WAV and MIDI, `video_render` makes an MP4 from CSS-animated HTML, SVG or photo scenes with transitions, captions and a soundtrack (host ffmpeg), `audio_transcribe` turns speech into timestamped text with local SenseVoice / Whisper models, with who speaks when, emotions and sounds such as laughter, `video_understand` reads a video as a timestamped storyboard image plus its transcript. External links and data URLs are refused. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-gc`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-gc) | Artifact and media garbage collection: date-partitioned storage management (`[YYYY-MM-DD]`), retention sweeps, and LRU capacity eviction. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-db`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-db) | In-memory OLAP analytics via embedded DuckDB: query CSV, Parquet, and JSON datasets directly via SQL without context inflation. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-office`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-office) | Office documents pack: Word (.docx) text extraction, Excel (.xlsx) read/write, and PDF document metadata inspection. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-devices`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-devices) | Device namespace: Swiftnest device tools under `/device/`, loadable as `device:current`, `device:all` or `device:`, with offline devices marked. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager-dsbot-entry`](packages/dsh-tool-manager-dsbot-entry) | Deprecated, no longer released. A "Tool manager" row in the ds-bot settings dialog that opens the panel. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager`](packages/dsh-tool-manager) | The old core name: re-exports `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core` so existing profiles keep working. | | [`@lvy-jsd/create-dsh-tool-ultra-plugin`](packages/create-dsh-tool-ultra-plugin) | Scaffold your own extension: `npm create @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-plugin@latest my-ext -- --type classifier`. | See [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md) for the design. ## Extending Every feature beyond the core is an ordinary plugin using the `toolCatalog` service, and the bundled `classifier-rules` package is written exactly as a third party would write it. Four extension points: | Point | For | |---|---| | `registerClassifier({ name, priority, group?, categorize? })` | placing tools into groups and groups into categories | | `annotate(match, { group?, category?, risk?, summary? })` | runtime metadata; `package.json` `dsh.toolCatalog` does the same without code | | `registerVisibilityFilter({ name, filter(agent, names) })` | narrowing what one agent may see — can only remove names | | `registerTargetResolver({ name, prefix, resolve })` | owning a target prefix, e.g. `cap:` | | `registerRiskGate` / `registerStateProvider` | confirming high-risk loads / keeping state across a restart | Hooks are plain events: `tool-catalog/before-load` (throw to veto), `after-load`, `before-unload`, `after-unload`, `before-rebuild`, `after-rebuild`, `state-changed`. Start from a generated package — it comes with a passing test: ```sh npm create @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-plugin@latest my-ext -- --type classifier cd my-ext && npm test ``` Two worked examples live in [`examples/`](examples), and the full interface list is in the core README and [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md) §11. ## Development Every package is written in TypeScript (`src/`) and compiled to `lib/` (JavaScript plus `.d.ts` type declarations); `lib/` is build output and not committed. The root `tsconfig.json` lists the packages (project references); the two browser halves (`client.ts`) have their own `tsconfig.client.json`, because DSH loads them as classic scripts, not modules. ```sh npm install # also links your local DSH host packages (scripts/link-host.mjs) npm run build # src/*.ts -> lib/*.js + lib/*.d.ts npm run typecheck # strict type check (tsc -b; writes lib/ too, references need it) node --test test/unit/*.test.mjs # pure catalog and registry tests (needs a build) node test/e2e.mjs # boots throwaway DSH instances; never touches your profile ``` Host packages (`@deepseek-ai/*`) are peers and are never installed from the registry (`.npmrc` sets `legacy-peer-deps`): a registry copy next to the plugin would shadow the DSH you actually run. `npm install` links them from `$DSH_APP` (default `~/.local/share/deepseek-harness/app`) instead. ## License Apache-2.0 — see [LICENSE](LICENSE). Releases before Tool Ultra (`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager*`) were MIT.

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-media Images, music and video made from code, and speech-to-text, for [Tool Ultra](https://github.com/lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra). The model writes an HTML/CSS page, an SVG drawing, a chart spec, a short score or a list of scenes, and this pack renders it on the DSH host. Recordings and videos use local processing unless you opt in with `geminiUploads: true` and configure a Gemini key. Local processing needs no API key; speech models and a SoundFont download once on first use. | Tool | Group / category | What it does | | --- | --- | --- | | `html_render` | image / media | Design an image in HTML and CSS (poster, social card, slide, infographic, certificate) and save it as PNG, JPEG or WebP, or save its CSS animations as an animated GIF or WebP (`seconds`). Flexbox, grid, gradients, gradient text, shadows, filters, blend modes; Chinese and emoji fonts from the host. | | `svg_render` | image / media | Render an SVG document (poster, greeting card, icon, diagram, infographic) to PNG, JPEG or WebP. `width` scales it sharply; `name` is a file name hint. | | `chart_render` | image / media | Draw a [Vega-Lite](https://vega.github.io/vega-lite/) chart (bar, line, pie, scatter, area, heatmap, ...) with inline data and save it as an image. A single-view chart without a size gets 480×300. | | `music_render` | audio / media | Compose a piece from notes for up to 16 of 37 instruments plus a drum kit, and save a WAV played with real recorded instruments (General MIDI SoundFont, stereo, reverb, mastered to −14 LUFS) and the MIDI file. | | `video_render` | video / media | Make an MP4 (H.264 + AAC) from scenes: HTML pages animated with CSS, still SVG drawings, or photos with a slow camera move. Transitions (fade, slide, wipe, circle, cut), captions or an `.srt`, and a soundtrack from `music_render`. Needs ffmpeg on the host. | | `audio_transcribe` | audio / media | Turn speech into timestamped text with speakers, tone and meaningful sounds. Saves SRT subtitles and reports local file facts. Local processing or optional Gemini. Needs ffmpeg and ffprobe. | | `video_understand` | video / media | Read file facts, save a storyboard of 4-16 frames following scene changes, and transcribe speech. Optional Gemini adds scenes, motion and screen text. Needs ffmpeg and ffprobe. | Load the pack with `tools_load(["pack:media"])`. Each call returns the saved file's path, size and pixel dimensions. ### HTML designs `html_render` draws the page with [Takumi](https://github.com/kane50613/takumi) (Rust, MIT OR Apache-2.0), a layout and paint engine for HTML and CSS that needs no browser: no Chromium download, no scripts, nothing fetched. It supports flexbox and grid, gradients (including `background-clip: text`), box and text shadows, `filter`, blend modes, `border-radius`, transforms and CSS `@keyframes`. ```json { "width": 1080, "height": 1350, "scale": 2, "name": "poster", "html": "

你好 👋

" } ``` A still shows the design after its animations finish. With `seconds` (0.5-10), the first seconds of the animations become an animated GIF (default) or WebP at 20 frames per second. `width` and `height` are CSS pixels (default 1080 wide, as tall as the content); `scale` 2 or 3 draws them sharper. Pictures are inline `data:image/...` or `.png`/`.jpg`/`.webp`/`.gif` files from the output folder by name (a chart from `chart_render`, a photo) or by absolute path inside `inputDirs`. Fonts come from the host through fontconfig (`fc-match`): Chinese sans and serif (regular and bold), monospace and colour emoji, plus any `fontFiles`. `lang` (default `zh-CN`) picks regional glyphs. Rotations interpolate as matrices, so a full spin needs keyframes under 180° apart. ### Note notation Each track is one line of `:` tokens played in order: `C4:1 E4:0.5 G4:1/2 R:1 [C4,E4,G4]:2`. `C4` is middle C, `#` is sharp, `b` is flat, `R` is a rest and `[..]` is a chord. Drum tracks use `K` (kick), `S` (snare) and `H` (hi-hat). Up to 16 tracks play together; `tempo` is in beats per minute. ```json { "tempo": 120, "tracks": [ { "instrument": "piano", "notes": "C4:1 C4:1 G4:1 G4:1 A4:1 A4:1 G4:2" }, { "instrument": "drums", "notes": "K:1 H:1 S:1 H:1 K:1 H:1 S:1 H:1" } ] } ``` ### Video ```json { "width": 1080, "height": 1920, "audio": "bgm-20261103T080000Z.wav", "captionStyle": "pop", "scenes": [ { "html": "

Title

", "seconds": 3, "transition": "circle" }, { "image": "trip.jpg", "motion": "zoom-in", "seconds": 4 }, { "svg": "", "seconds": 3 } ], "captions": [ { "start": 0.5, "end": 2.5, "text": "一句话做视频" } ] } ``` Every frame is drawn by the pack and streamed as raw pixels into the host's `ffmpeg`, which encodes H.264 and adds the soundtrack: - **Scenes.** An `html` scene is a page the size of the video, drawn with the same engine as `html_render`; its CSS animations start when the scene appears, so entrances, kinetic type and growing bar charts play out. An `image` scene shows a photo full-frame with a slow camera move (`zoom-in`, `zoom-out`, `pan-left`, `pan-right`, `none`). An `svg` scene is a still drawing, letterboxed. - **Transitions.** `fade` (default), `slide-left`, `slide-up`, `wipe`, `circle` or `cut`, eased, up to 0.6 s, set per scene or for the whole video. A transition straddles the boundary, so the video is exactly as long as its scenes. `fade` also fades the video in from and out to black. - **Captions.** A `captions` list, or `subtitles`: an `.srt` file such as the one `audio_transcribe` saves. `subtitle` style is small and at the bottom; `pop` is big, bold and bounces in, short-video style. Caption text is escaped, never markup. - `fps` 24, 30 (default) or 60. A 1280×720 video takes about one to two times its length to render on a 4-core CPU. ffmpeg runs as a separate program with an argument list, no shell, and a time limit (`ffmpegTimeoutMs`; set `ffmpegPath` if it is not on `PATH`). ### Speech to text With the local engine, `audio_transcribe` decodes the file with ffmpeg (16 kHz mono, at most `maxTranscribeSeconds`) and recognizes it with [sherpa-onnx](https://github.com/k2-fsa/sherpa-onnx) (Apache-2.0) on the CPU, so it does not compete with a local LLM for the GPU. Local processing never uploads your audio. - **Who speaks when.** Speaker diarization (pyannote segmentation 3.0, MIT, plus a 3D-Speaker ERes2Net voiceprint, Apache-2.0) splits the recording into turns, labelled Speaker 1, 2, … when more than one person talks. `speakers: false` skips it and cuts the audio by voice activity (Silero VAD, MIT) instead, which is several times faster. - **What is said.** [SenseVoice Small](https://github.com/FunAudioLLM/SenseVoice) (code MIT; weights under the FunASR model license, which asks for attribution) reads Chinese, Cantonese, English, Japanese and Korean with punctuation, and also hears how the speaker sounds (happy, sad, angry, …) and sounds such as laughter, applause, coughing or music. About 0.15× real time on 4 cores. - **Other languages.** A `language` SenseVoice does not read (for example `fr`) goes to Whisper large-v3-turbo (MIT, about 540 MB); `speechModel: whisper-turbo` uses Whisper for everything. The models (SenseVoice about 155 MB, the speaker models about 45 MB) download once from the sherpa-onnx releases on GitHub (`modelMirror`) into `modelCacheDir`, are checked against their SHA-256 and unpacked in JavaScript, so the server needs no tar or bzip2. The model gets the timestamped transcript (up to 20 000 characters) and the full text is saved as an `.srt` file. ### Video understanding `video_understand` reads the file's facts with `ffprobe`, then has ffmpeg find the cuts (its scene-change score on a small copy of each frame, which takes well under a second per minute of video). The frames follow the edit: the strongest cuts split the video into shots, each shot gets a frame from its middle, and long shots get more. The reply lists when the scene changes, and the frames go four to a row on one JPEG storyboard, each with its time. It then transcribes the sound track the same way as `audio_transcribe` (skip it with `transcript: false`). The reply names the saved storyboard, so the agent can look at it with its own image-reading tool; with a text-only model, the facts and the transcript still describe the video. An audio-only file gets the facts and the transcript. The file is a name from the output folder or an absolute path inside one of `inputDirs` (for example where uploads land). Paths are checked after resolving links. ### Gemini **Privacy / 隐私：Gemini uploads the entire input file to Google. 默认关闭上传；只有显式设置 `geminiUploads: true` 并配置密钥后才会上传。** Uploads are optional and default to `false`. A key shared with Swiftnest vision does not enable media uploads. With uploads off, the tools do not read the key or make Gemini requests. `engine: "auto"` quietly uses local processing; `engine: "gemini"` also runs locally and adds `Gemini uploads are off (set geminiUploads: true)` (or its Chinese translation). `engine: "local"` keeps the file on this server even when uploads are enabled. Both `audio_transcribe` and `video_understand` accept `engine: "auto" | "local" | "gemini"`. With `geminiUploads: true`, the default, `auto`, uses Gemini when a key resolves and local processing otherwise. Key sources are checked in order: `geminiApiKey`, then `geminiKeyFile` (default `~/.config/swiftnest/gemini.key`, with surrounding whitespace removed), then `GEMINI_API_KEY`. A missing or empty key file allows the environment fallback. An unreadable key file causes local fallback. Keep keys out of version control; prefer the private key file or environment to a shared config. To opt in, create a key in [Google AI Studio](https://aistudio.google.com/api-keys), save it in the key file, set `geminiUploads: true` in the pack config, and call either tool normally. You can override `geminiModel`. The default is the stable `gemini-3.8-flash`: the [models page](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/models) recommends 3.8 Flash for new projects, and its [model details](https://aistudio.google.com/docs/models/gemini-3.8-flash) list “Stable: `gemini-3.8-flash`”. Gemini describes video scenes, screen text, actions and motion with timestamps in Markdown. Audio uses [structured JSON output](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/structured-output) (`generationConfig.responseMimeType: application/json` and `responseJsonSchema`) for segments with `start`/`end` in seconds, a numeric `speaker`, `text` and optional `tone`. The pack checks these segments and builds timestamped text and SRT subtitles with the same formatters as the local engine. `language`, `speakers: false` (audio) and `transcript: false` (video) guide the request. Both engines retain local ffprobe facts, and video always saves the local storyboard. Gemini receives the **whole file**, including video audio when `transcript: false`; the local `maxTranscribeSeconds` limit does not trim uploads. The client uses the REST Files API, waits for processing, then calls `generateContent`. Uploads are capped at 2 GB. Each phase has its own time budget: upload gets two minutes plus the transfer time at a modest 1 Mbps (125,000 bytes/second), processing gets ten minutes, and generation gets five minutes. For example, 500 MiB has about 72 minutes to upload, without consuming the processing or generation budgets. No extra timeout configuration is needed. Deletion is attempted afterwards, including on failure, with its own five-second limit. If deletion fails, Google's [Files API retention](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/files#delete-uploaded) applies. API errors, quota limits, unsupported files and timeouts run the local pipeline and add one short reason line at the top. With uploads enabled and `engine: "gemini"` but no key, that line is `no Gemini key configured (set geminiApiKey or ~/.config/swiftnest/gemini.key)`. Every successful Gemini reply includes `analysed by Gemini (file uploaded to Google)`. Keys are sent only in the `x-goog-api-key` header and are filtered from replies and errors. The integration uses global `fetch`, with no SDK dependency. ### Music `music_render` writes the score as MIDI (each track on its own channel with an instrument, a place in the stereo field and some reverb) and plays it with [spessasynth_core](https://github.com/spessasus/spessasynth_core) (Apache-2.0), a SoundFont synthesizer in plain TypeScript. The default SoundFont is FluidR3 Mono GM (MIT, about 24 MB as `.sf3`), downloaded once from `soundfontUrl` into `modelCacheDir` and checked against its SHA-256; set `soundfont` to use a local `.sf2`/`.sf3` instead. The mix is then mastered: gain to −14 LUFS integrated loudness (ITU-R BS.1770, what streaming services aim for) and a look-ahead limiter at −1 dBFS. If the SoundFont cannot load, a small built-in synthesizer plays the piece and the reply says why. Instruments: piano, harpsichord, vibraphone, marimba, organ, accordion, guitar, bass, violin, cello, pizzicato, harp, timpani, strings, choir, trumpet, trombone, horn, brass, sax, oboe, clarinet, flute, chip, pad, sitar, koto and more (the tool lists all 37), plus `drums`: K kick, S snare, P clap, H closed and O open hi-hat, C crash, Y ride, T/M/L toms. `[K,C]:1` hits two at once. ### Libraries Rendering images uses [sharp](https://sharp.pixelplumbing.com/) (Apache-2.0, librsvg for SVG) and [Vega](https://vega.github.io/vega/) / Vega-Lite / vega-interpreter (BSD-3-Clause). ## Safety - **HTML allowlist.** `

# @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-office Office document reading and manipulation for [Tool Ultra](https://github.com/lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra). Pure JavaScript/TypeScript document parsing and generation: Word (.docx), Excel (.xlsx), and PDF metadata inspection. ## Tools | Tool | Group / category | What it does | | --- | --- | --- | | `office_doc_read` | office / system | Extract text content and structure from Word documents (.docx) as Markdown/plain text. | | `office_sheet_read` | office / system | Read rows and sheet data from an Excel spreadsheet (.xlsx). | | `office_sheet_write` | office / system | Create a new Excel spreadsheet (.xlsx) with column headers and row data. | | `office_pdf_info` | office / system | Read metadata, title, author, and page count from a PDF document. |

Tool Ultra
On-demand tool loading for DeepSeek Harness — every tool as a directory, loaded only when an agent asks.

English · 中文

--- ## What It Is Tool Ultra is an All-in-One tool-plugin product for DeepSeek Harness, and an important component of [Swiftnest](https://github.com/lvy-jsd/swiftnest). Its goal is one coherent tool product across everyday tasks, web/MCP services, media and device capabilities. The small core and replaceable extension packages are its internal architecture; the product is more than a tool-directory browser. Tools are browsable as a directory (category → group → tool), searchable by intent and loaded on demand, keeping unneeded schemas out of the model's context. Savings depend on catalog size, discovery/load steps and provider caching: compare per-request schemas, total task tokens and task success separately. Broad capability does not mean every external service or upload is enabled by default. The current preview is distributed as source and modular packages; Swiftnest builds a pinned source commit. An AI can install and configure the required modules. The published-package quick-start syntax below applies when those package versions are available on npm; it is not a claim that the renamed 0.5.0 packages have already been published. > **Renamed.** This project was `dsh-tool-manager`. Version 0.5.0 renames every > package from `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager-` to `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-` > (the core is `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core`). Nothing else changes: the entry > tools, the `toolCatalog` service (now also provided as `toolUltra`), the hooks, > the config and the state directory `/tool-manager/` stay the same. > An existing profile can keep `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager`: from 0.5.0 it only > re-exports the new core. Older extension releases keep working with the new core. ## Quick start ```sh # 1. install the core plus the rule-based classifier (optional but recommended) dsh plugin --profile web add @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-rules # 2. restart DSH, then ask the agent: "what tools do you have?" # it answers with tools_ls("/") — a directory, not 200 tool schemas # 3. want the UI? add the panel, then open Settings → "Tool manager" dsh plugin --profile web add @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-panel ``` > **Install the scoped `@lvy-jsd/…` packages.** The unscoped `dsh-tool-manager` > on npm is a different project. Do not install both: each one narrows which > tools an agent can see, so together they hide tools from each other. On a fresh install every group is `uncategorized` until a classifier is installed — the tools are still browsable and loadable, only the categories are missing. See [Extending](#extending) to write your own classifier. `tools_load(["web"])` also accepts bare names: try registered `pack:` → `cap:` → `device:` namespaces, first non-empty match only, then normal directory lookup; explicit prefixes keep their behavior and plugin ownership. ## Packages | Package | What it does | |---|---| | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-core) | Core: directory, `tools_ls` / `tools_load` / `tools_unload`, per-agent allowlist, the `toolCatalog` extension service, plus intent retrieval + routing (`tools_find` / `tools_route` / `skills_find` / `skills_route`, BM25 with a Rust sidecar). Without extensions every group is `uncategorized`. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-rules`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-rules) | Places groups into categories from built-in rules and your config overrides. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-risk-gate`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-risk-gate) | Confirms loading high-risk tools through the DSH approval channel, with a per-session allowlist. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-persist`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-persist) | Keeps loaded tools across a DSH restart, one state file per session. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-panel`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-panel) | Web panel: browse the tree, see each live session's loaded tools and token cost, load/unload from the UI, edit the always-on and high-risk lists, edit one tool's metadata, exempt one session. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-llm`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-llm) | Places groups with a small model, one request per group, cached by a hash of the group and its tool descriptions. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-capability-bridge`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-capability-bridge) | Load a named bundle of tools in one call: `tools_load(["cap:android-debug"])`. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-attribution-scan`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-attribution-scan) | Group tools by the plugin package whose source defines them. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-essentials`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-essentials) | Native tool pack, no API keys: time zones and date math, a calculator with units (mathjs), weather (Open-Meteo), place search (Nominatim), Wikipedia. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-web`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-web) | Native tool pack: `web_read` turns a page into clean Markdown (Readability + turndown), `web_links` lists its links. Refuses private addresses by default. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-mcp`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-mcp) | MCP presets through DSH's MCP client: memory, sequential thinking, Context7, Playwright and filesystem start without keys; GitHub, SearXNG, Brave, Tavily, Firecrawl, Notion and AMap start once their key is set. `mcp_presets` shows the status. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-media`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-media) | Native tool pack, no API keys: images, music and video made from code. `html_render` designs an image in HTML/CSS (no browser) or turns its CSS animations into a GIF, `svg_render` turns an SVG drawing into PNG/JPEG/WebP, `chart_render` draws a Vega-Lite chart, `music_render` plays a score with real recorded instruments (SoundFont, mastered) and saves WAV and MIDI, `video_render` makes an MP4 from CSS-animated HTML, SVG or photo scenes with transitions, captions and a soundtrack (host ffmpeg), `audio_transcribe` turns speech into timestamped text with local SenseVoice / Whisper models, with who speaks when, emotions and sounds such as laughter, `video_understand` reads a video as a timestamped storyboard image plus its transcript. External links and data URLs are refused. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-gc`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-gc) | Artifact and media garbage collection: date-partitioned storage management (`[YYYY-MM-DD]`), retention sweeps, and LRU capacity eviction. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-db`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-db) | In-memory OLAP analytics via embedded DuckDB: query CSV, Parquet, and JSON datasets directly via SQL without context inflation. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-office`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-office) | Office documents pack: Word (.docx) text extraction, Excel (.xlsx) read/write, and PDF document metadata inspection. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-devices`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-devices) | Device namespace: Swiftnest device tools under `/device/`, loadable as `device:current`, `device:all` or `device:`, with offline devices marked. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager-dsbot-entry`](packages/dsh-tool-manager-dsbot-entry) | Deprecated, no longer released. A "Tool manager" row in the ds-bot settings dialog that opens the panel. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager`](packages/dsh-tool-manager) | The old core name: re-exports `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core` so existing profiles keep working. | | [`@lvy-jsd/create-dsh-tool-ultra-plugin`](packages/create-dsh-tool-ultra-plugin) | Scaffold your own extension: `npm create @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-plugin@latest my-ext -- --type classifier`. | See [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md) for the design. ## Extending Every feature beyond the core is an ordinary plugin using the `toolCatalog` service, and the bundled `classifier-rules` package is written exactly as a third party would write it. Four extension points: | Point | For | |---|---| | `registerClassifier({ name, priority, group?, categorize? })` | placing tools into groups and groups into categories | | `annotate(match, { group?, category?, risk?, summary? })` | runtime metadata; `package.json` `dsh.toolCatalog` does the same without code | | `registerVisibilityFilter({ name, filter(agent, names) })` | narrowing what one agent may see — can only remove names | | `registerTargetResolver({ name, prefix, resolve })` | owning a target prefix, e.g. `cap:` | | `registerRiskGate` / `registerStateProvider` | confirming high-risk loads / keeping state across a restart | Hooks are plain events: `tool-catalog/before-load` (throw to veto), `after-load`, `before-unload`, `after-unload`, `before-rebuild`, `after-rebuild`, `state-changed`. Start from a generated package — it comes with a passing test: ```sh npm create @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-plugin@latest my-ext -- --type classifier cd my-ext && npm test ``` Two worked examples live in [`examples/`](examples), and the full interface list is in the core README and [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md) §11. ## Development Every package is written in TypeScript (`src/`) and compiled to `lib/` (JavaScript plus `.d.ts` type declarations); `lib/` is build output and not committed. The root `tsconfig.json` lists the packages (project references); the two browser halves (`client.ts`) have their own `tsconfig.client.json`, because DSH loads them as classic scripts, not modules. ```sh npm install # also links your local DSH host packages (scripts/link-host.mjs) npm run build # src/*.ts -> lib/*.js + lib/*.d.ts npm run typecheck # strict type check (tsc -b; writes lib/ too, references need it) node --test test/unit/*.test.mjs # pure catalog and registry tests (needs a build) node test/e2e.mjs # boots throwaway DSH instances; never touches your profile ``` Host packages (`@deepseek-ai/*`) are peers and are never installed from the registry (`.npmrc` sets `legacy-peer-deps`): a registry copy next to the plugin would shadow the DSH you actually run. `npm install` links them from `$DSH_APP` (default `~/.local/share/deepseek-harness/app`) instead. ## License Apache-2.0 — see [LICENSE](LICENSE). Releases before Tool Ultra (`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager*`) were MIT.
