evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-web Web-reading tools for [Tool Ultra](https://github.com/lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra). No API keys. | Tool | Group / category | What it does | | --- | --- | --- | | `web_read` | web / search | Fetch a page and return the main article as Markdown, with title, author, date and absolute links. Plain text and JSON pass through. `offset` and `max_chars` page through long documents; `full_page` converts the whole body. | | `web_links` | web / search | List a page's links, optionally filtered by a word or limited to the same site. | Extraction uses [Mozilla Readability](https://github.com/mozilla/readability) (Apache-2.0) on a [linkedom](https://github.com/WebReflection/linkedom) DOM (ISC), and [turndown](https://github.com/mixmark-io/turndown) (MIT) for Markdown. Everything is TypeScript/JavaScript, with no headless browser. For pages that need JavaScript to render, use a browser pack (Playwright MCP). The names do not collide with DSH's built-in `web_fetch` and `web_search`. Those stay available for raw fetches and search. ## Safety The tools refuse loopback, private, link-local and CGNAT addresses, so a model cannot reach services on the DSH host or its LAN (for example `169.254.169.254` or `192.168.x.x`). The check runs on the resolved IP and again on every redirect hop. Set `allowPrivate: true` only if you trust every agent that can load these tools. Response bodies are capped at `maxBytes`. ## Config See [`cordis.patch.yml`](cordis.patch.yml): `disable`, `userAgent`, `timeoutMs`, `maxBytes`, `maxChars`, `allowPrivate`. ## License Apache-2.0.

Tool Ultra
On-demand tool loading for DeepSeek Harness — every tool as a directory, loaded only when an agent asks.

English · 中文

--- ## What It Is Tool Ultra is an All-in-One tool-plugin product for DeepSeek Harness, and an important component of [Swiftnest](https://github.com/lvy-jsd/swiftnest). Its goal is one coherent tool product across everyday tasks, web/MCP services, media and device capabilities. The small core and replaceable extension packages are its internal architecture; the product is more than a tool-directory browser. Tools are browsable as a directory (category → group → tool), searchable by intent and loaded on demand, keeping unneeded schemas out of the model's context. Savings depend on catalog size, discovery/load steps and provider caching: compare per-request schemas, total task tokens and task success separately. Broad capability does not mean every external service or upload is enabled by default. The current preview is distributed as source and modular packages; Swiftnest builds a pinned source commit. An AI can install and configure the required modules. The published-package quick-start syntax below applies when those package versions are available on npm; it is not a claim that the renamed 0.5.0 packages have already been published. > **Renamed.** This project was `dsh-tool-manager`. Version 0.5.0 renames every > package from `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager-` to `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-` > (the core is `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core`). Nothing else changes: the entry > tools, the `toolCatalog` service (now also provided as `toolUltra`), the hooks, > the config and the state directory `/tool-manager/` stay the same. > An existing profile can keep `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager`: from 0.5.0 it only > re-exports the new core. Older extension releases keep working with the new core. ## Quick start ```sh # 1. install the core plus the rule-based classifier (optional but recommended) dsh plugin --profile web add @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-rules # 2. restart DSH, then ask the agent: "what tools do you have?" # it answers with tools_ls("/") — a directory, not 200 tool schemas # 3. want the UI? add the panel, then open Settings → "Tool manager" dsh plugin --profile web add @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-panel ``` > **Install the scoped `@lvy-jsd/…` packages.** The unscoped `dsh-tool-manager` > on npm is a different project. Do not install both: each one narrows which > tools an agent can see, so together they hide tools from each other. On a fresh install every group is `uncategorized` until a classifier is installed — the tools are still browsable and loadable, only the categories are missing. See [Extending](#extending) to write your own classifier. `tools_load(["web"])` also accepts bare names: try registered `pack:` → `cap:` → `device:` namespaces, first non-empty match only, then normal directory lookup; explicit prefixes keep their behavior and plugin ownership. ## Packages | Package | What it does | |---|---| | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-core) | Core: directory, `tools_ls` / `tools_load` / `tools_unload`, per-agent allowlist, the `toolCatalog` extension service, plus intent retrieval + routing (`tools_find` / `tools_route` / `skills_find` / `skills_route`, BM25 with a Rust sidecar). Without extensions every group is `uncategorized`. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-rules`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-rules) | Places groups into categories from built-in rules and your config overrides. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-risk-gate`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-risk-gate) | Confirms loading high-risk tools through the DSH approval channel, with a per-session allowlist. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-persist`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-persist) | Keeps loaded tools across a DSH restart, one state file per session. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-panel`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-panel) | Web panel: browse the tree, see each live session's loaded tools and token cost, load/unload from the UI, edit the always-on and high-risk lists, edit one tool's metadata, exempt one session. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-llm`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-llm) | Places groups with a small model, one request per group, cached by a hash of the group and its tool descriptions. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-capability-bridge`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-capability-bridge) | Load a named bundle of tools in one call: `tools_load(["cap:android-debug"])`. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-attribution-scan`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-attribution-scan) | Group tools by the plugin package whose source defines them. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-essentials`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-essentials) | Native tool pack, no API keys: time zones and date math, a calculator with units (mathjs), weather (Open-Meteo), place search (Nominatim), Wikipedia. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-web`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-web) | Native tool pack: `web_read` turns a page into clean Markdown (Readability + turndown), `web_links` lists its links. Refuses private addresses by default. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-mcp`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-mcp) | MCP presets through DSH's MCP client: memory, sequential thinking, Context7, Playwright and filesystem start without keys; GitHub, SearXNG, Brave, Tavily, Firecrawl, Notion and AMap start once their key is set. `mcp_presets` shows the status. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-media`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-media) | Native tool pack, no API keys: images, music and video made from code. `html_render` designs an image in HTML/CSS (no browser) or turns its CSS animations into a GIF, `svg_render` turns an SVG drawing into PNG/JPEG/WebP, `chart_render` draws a Vega-Lite chart, `music_render` plays a score with real recorded instruments (SoundFont, mastered) and saves WAV and MIDI, `video_render` makes an MP4 from CSS-animated HTML, SVG or photo scenes with transitions, captions and a soundtrack (host ffmpeg), `audio_transcribe` turns speech into timestamped text with local SenseVoice / Whisper models, with who speaks when, emotions and sounds such as laughter, `video_understand` reads a video as a timestamped storyboard image plus its transcript. External links and data URLs are refused. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-gc`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-gc) | Artifact and media garbage collection: date-partitioned storage management (`[YYYY-MM-DD]`), retention sweeps, and LRU capacity eviction. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-db`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-db) | In-memory OLAP analytics via embedded DuckDB: query CSV, Parquet, and JSON datasets directly via SQL without context inflation. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-office`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-office) | Office documents pack: Word (.docx) text extraction, Excel (.xlsx) read/write, and PDF document metadata inspection. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-devices`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-devices) | Device namespace: Swiftnest device tools under `/device/`, loadable as `device:current`, `device:all` or `device:`, with offline devices marked. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager-dsbot-entry`](packages/dsh-tool-manager-dsbot-entry) | Deprecated, no longer released. A "Tool manager" row in the ds-bot settings dialog that opens the panel. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager`](packages/dsh-tool-manager) | The old core name: re-exports `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core` so existing profiles keep working. | | [`@lvy-jsd/create-dsh-tool-ultra-plugin`](packages/create-dsh-tool-ultra-plugin) | Scaffold your own extension: `npm create @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-plugin@latest my-ext -- --type classifier`. | See [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md) for the design. ## Extending Every feature beyond the core is an ordinary plugin using the `toolCatalog` service, and the bundled `classifier-rules` package is written exactly as a third party would write it. Four extension points: | Point | For | |---|---| | `registerClassifier({ name, priority, group?, categorize? })` | placing tools into groups and groups into categories | | `annotate(match, { group?, category?, risk?, summary? })` | runtime metadata; `package.json` `dsh.toolCatalog` does the same without code | | `registerVisibilityFilter({ name, filter(agent, names) })` | narrowing what one agent may see — can only remove names | | `registerTargetResolver({ name, prefix, resolve })` | owning a target prefix, e.g. `cap:` | | `registerRiskGate` / `registerStateProvider` | confirming high-risk loads / keeping state across a restart | Hooks are plain events: `tool-catalog/before-load` (throw to veto), `after-load`, `before-unload`, `after-unload`, `before-rebuild`, `after-rebuild`, `state-changed`. Start from a generated package — it comes with a passing test: ```sh npm create @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-plugin@latest my-ext -- --type classifier cd my-ext && npm test ``` Two worked examples live in [`examples/`](examples), and the full interface list is in the core README and [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md) §11. ## Development Every package is written in TypeScript (`src/`) and compiled to `lib/` (JavaScript plus `.d.ts` type declarations); `lib/` is build output and not committed. The root `tsconfig.json` lists the packages (project references); the two browser halves (`client.ts`) have their own `tsconfig.client.json`, because DSH loads them as classic scripts, not modules. ```sh npm install # also links your local DSH host packages (scripts/link-host.mjs) npm run build # src/*.ts -> lib/*.js + lib/*.d.ts npm run typecheck # strict type check (tsc -b; writes lib/ too, references need it) node --test test/unit/*.test.mjs # pure catalog and registry tests (needs a build) node test/e2e.mjs # boots throwaway DSH instances; never touches your profile ``` Host packages (`@deepseek-ai/*`) are peers and are never installed from the registry (`.npmrc` sets `legacy-peer-deps`): a registry copy next to the plugin would shadow the DSH you actually run. `npm install` links them from `$DSH_APP` (default `~/.local/share/deepseek-harness/app`) instead. ## License Apache-2.0 — see [LICENSE](LICENSE). Releases before Tool Ultra (`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager*`) were MIT.

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-panel Web panel for [`dsh-tool-ultra-core`](../dsh-tool-ultra-core): browse the tool directory, see what each live session has loaded and what it costs, and load or unload from the UI. Optional — the core works without it. When the deployment has no web server (headless), the plugin mounts nothing and stays harmless. ## What you get | View | Shows | Actions | |---|---|---| | **Directory** | the same category → group → tool tree the model browses, with per-node tool counts and schema tokens, plus each tool's summary and high-risk mark | click to drill down; `load` on any node; search across the whole tree from the search box; **Metadata** on a tool opens its metadata editor | | **Sessions** | every live agent (subagents marked with their parent), its loaded groups and tools, how many tools are visible (`exempt` for a route listed in `exemptProviders`, which is never narrowed), and the **schema tokens actually sent** for it | `load` / `unload` per agent; **exempt this session** writes a per-session entry to the exemption file | | **Configuration** | the effective always-on list, config additions, and the high-risk list, plus every registered extension point (classifiers with priorities, visibility filters, risk gates, state providers, categories) and the exemption file in force | edit the always-on and high-risk lists; add/remove tools; saves to `settings.json` | | **Metadata** | one tool's three layers — what the package or a classifier declares, what the panel edited, and what the model actually receives — with its group, category, risk and summary | edit and save (writes `metadata.json`), or revert to the declaration | | **Tidy** | the groups still in `uncategorized`, the categories the model may choose from, and which model is in force | **ask the model** for a placement per group, then apply the rows you confirm; writes `metadata.json` | Editing is limited to metadata the core exposes: categories, groups, summaries and the risk mark. The JSON schema sent to the model (`description`, `parameters`) has no public interception point in DSH, so the panel does not touch it. Tidy never runs on its own. A placement is durable, so a wrong answer is work to undo rather than something that clears itself: the model only proposes, every row is unticked-able, and nothing is written until **Apply**. The model comes from this plugin's `model` config, else from the host's default selection (`agentDefaultModel`); with neither, the button explains why it is disabled instead of failing. Answers naming a group that does not exist, or a category that is not in the catalog, are shown as rejected rather than dropped silently. Exemptions move to a file once you toggle one from the panel: see the core package's README for the precedence between `exempt.json` and the configured `exemptProviders`. Loading from the panel goes through the **same path as `tools_load`**, so `tool-catalog/before-load` hooks and vetoes apply. The risk gate's approval prompt does not: it guards the model's `tools_load` call, and a click in the panel is itself the user's consent. Without any risk gate installed, high-risk loads are still refused. ## Install ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-rules @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-panel ``` Then restart DSH (or let live reload pick it up). Open **Settings**: a **Tool manager** section (工具管理 in Chinese) appears in the settings sidebar. The panel follows the DSH interface language (English and Chinese, English by default; category names and descriptions are translated) and the active theme, light or dark, because it is styled only with the host's `--dsw-alias-*` theme variables. ```yaml - id: tool-manager-panel name: '@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-panel' config: enabled: true # false disables the routes (the settings section then reports the service offline) ``` ## How it is put together Two halves: - **Server half** (`src/index.ts`) mounts two same-origin routes under a loopback + same-origin trust fence (the same shape `dsh-mcp-connector` uses): | Route | Purpose | |---|---| | `POST /tool-manager/api` | JSON-RPC with a method whitelist (`tree`, `sessions`, `load`, `unload`, `config`, `updateConfig`, `reloadConfig`, `setExemptSession`, `reloadExempt`, `toolMeta`, `updateToolMeta`, `clearToolMeta`, `extensions`, `search`, `toolNames`) | | `GET /tool-manager/events` | SSE: catalog rebuilt, per-session state changed, configuration saved, metadata edited | - **Browser half** (`src/client.ts`) is a small `window.__ModuleLoader__.load({...})` registration, compiled by `tsc` into a classic script (`lib/client.js`) — no bundler. It registers one `settings.section` slot and renders the panel natively with React (no iframe). Copy lives in two dictionaries registered with the host `locale` service; styles use only `--dsw-alias-*` variables, so any DSH theme applies. To add a language, add a dictionary next to `en` and `zh` in `src/client.ts` and register it under the same namespace (`tool-manager.panel`). ## Writing your own panel Every method reads from the `toolCatalog` service, so a different UI needs no core changes: ```js ctx.inject(['toolCatalog'], (c) => { const tree = c.toolCatalog.get() // catalog for an agent (or the union) const rows = c.toolCatalog.agents() // live agents with parents const state = c.toolCatalog.stateOf(agent) // { loaded, groups, … } (Sets) const tokens = c.toolCatalog.wireTokens(agent) // schema tokens really sent const hits = c.toolCatalog.find('adb') // structured cross-tree search await c.toolCatalog.load(agent, ['/device/adb']) // same path as tools_load }) ``` ## License Apache-2.0 — see [LICENSE](LICENSE). Releases before Tool Ultra (`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager*`) were MIT.

Tool Ultra
On-demand tool loading for DeepSeek Harness — every tool as a directory, loaded only when an agent asks.

English · 中文

--- ## What It Is Tool Ultra is an All-in-One tool-plugin product for DeepSeek Harness, and an important component of [Swiftnest](https://github.com/lvy-jsd/swiftnest). Its goal is one coherent tool product across everyday tasks, web/MCP services, media and device capabilities. The small core and replaceable extension packages are its internal architecture; the product is more than a tool-directory browser. Tools are browsable as a directory (category → group → tool), searchable by intent and loaded on demand, keeping unneeded schemas out of the model's context. Savings depend on catalog size, discovery/load steps and provider caching: compare per-request schemas, total task tokens and task success separately. Broad capability does not mean every external service or upload is enabled by default. The current preview is distributed as source and modular packages; Swiftnest builds a pinned source commit. An AI can install and configure the required modules. The published-package quick-start syntax below applies when those package versions are available on npm; it is not a claim that the renamed 0.5.0 packages have already been published. > **Renamed.** This project was `dsh-tool-manager`. Version 0.5.0 renames every > package from `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager-` to `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-` > (the core is `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core`). Nothing else changes: the entry > tools, the `toolCatalog` service (now also provided as `toolUltra`), the hooks, > the config and the state directory `/tool-manager/` stay the same. > An existing profile can keep `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager`: from 0.5.0 it only > re-exports the new core. Older extension releases keep working with the new core. ## Quick start ```sh # 1. install the core plus the rule-based classifier (optional but recommended) dsh plugin --profile web add @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-rules # 2. restart DSH, then ask the agent: "what tools do you have?" # it answers with tools_ls("/") — a directory, not 200 tool schemas # 3. want the UI? add the panel, then open Settings → "Tool manager" dsh plugin --profile web add @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-panel ``` > **Install the scoped `@lvy-jsd/…` packages.** The unscoped `dsh-tool-manager` > on npm is a different project. Do not install both: each one narrows which > tools an agent can see, so together they hide tools from each other. On a fresh install every group is `uncategorized` until a classifier is installed — the tools are still browsable and loadable, only the categories are missing. See [Extending](#extending) to write your own classifier. `tools_load(["web"])` also accepts bare names: try registered `pack:` → `cap:` → `device:` namespaces, first non-empty match only, then normal directory lookup; explicit prefixes keep their behavior and plugin ownership. ## Packages | Package | What it does | |---|---| | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-core) | Core: directory, `tools_ls` / `tools_load` / `tools_unload`, per-agent allowlist, the `toolCatalog` extension service, plus intent retrieval + routing (`tools_find` / `tools_route` / `skills_find` / `skills_route`, BM25 with a Rust sidecar). Without extensions every group is `uncategorized`. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-rules`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-rules) | Places groups into categories from built-in rules and your config overrides. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-risk-gate`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-risk-gate) | Confirms loading high-risk tools through the DSH approval channel, with a per-session allowlist. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-persist`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-persist) | Keeps loaded tools across a DSH restart, one state file per session. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-panel`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-panel) | Web panel: browse the tree, see each live session's loaded tools and token cost, load/unload from the UI, edit the always-on and high-risk lists, edit one tool's metadata, exempt one session. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-llm`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-llm) | Places groups with a small model, one request per group, cached by a hash of the group and its tool descriptions. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-capability-bridge`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-capability-bridge) | Load a named bundle of tools in one call: `tools_load(["cap:android-debug"])`. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-attribution-scan`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-attribution-scan) | Group tools by the plugin package whose source defines them. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-essentials`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-essentials) | Native tool pack, no API keys: time zones and date math, a calculator with units (mathjs), weather (Open-Meteo), place search (Nominatim), Wikipedia. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-web`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-web) | Native tool pack: `web_read` turns a page into clean Markdown (Readability + turndown), `web_links` lists its links. Refuses private addresses by default. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-mcp`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-mcp) | MCP presets through DSH's MCP client: memory, sequential thinking, Context7, Playwright and filesystem start without keys; GitHub, SearXNG, Brave, Tavily, Firecrawl, Notion and AMap start once their key is set. `mcp_presets` shows the status. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-media`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-media) | Native tool pack, no API keys: images, music and video made from code. `html_render` designs an image in HTML/CSS (no browser) or turns its CSS animations into a GIF, `svg_render` turns an SVG drawing into PNG/JPEG/WebP, `chart_render` draws a Vega-Lite chart, `music_render` plays a score with real recorded instruments (SoundFont, mastered) and saves WAV and MIDI, `video_render` makes an MP4 from CSS-animated HTML, SVG or photo scenes with transitions, captions and a soundtrack (host ffmpeg), `audio_transcribe` turns speech into timestamped text with local SenseVoice / Whisper models, with who speaks when, emotions and sounds such as laughter, `video_understand` reads a video as a timestamped storyboard image plus its transcript. External links and data URLs are refused. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-gc`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-gc) | Artifact and media garbage collection: date-partitioned storage management (`[YYYY-MM-DD]`), retention sweeps, and LRU capacity eviction. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-db`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-db) | In-memory OLAP analytics via embedded DuckDB: query CSV, Parquet, and JSON datasets directly via SQL without context inflation. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-office`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-office) | Office documents pack: Word (.docx) text extraction, Excel (.xlsx) read/write, and PDF document metadata inspection. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-devices`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-devices) | Device namespace: Swiftnest device tools under `/device/`, loadable as `device:current`, `device:all` or `device:`, with offline devices marked. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager-dsbot-entry`](packages/dsh-tool-manager-dsbot-entry) | Deprecated, no longer released. A "Tool manager" row in the ds-bot settings dialog that opens the panel. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager`](packages/dsh-tool-manager) | The old core name: re-exports `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core` so existing profiles keep working. | | [`@lvy-jsd/create-dsh-tool-ultra-plugin`](packages/create-dsh-tool-ultra-plugin) | Scaffold your own extension: `npm create @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-plugin@latest my-ext -- --type classifier`. | See [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md) for the design. ## Extending Every feature beyond the core is an ordinary plugin using the `toolCatalog` service, and the bundled `classifier-rules` package is written exactly as a third party would write it. Four extension points: | Point | For | |---|---| | `registerClassifier({ name, priority, group?, categorize? })` | placing tools into groups and groups into categories | | `annotate(match, { group?, category?, risk?, summary? })` | runtime metadata; `package.json` `dsh.toolCatalog` does the same without code | | `registerVisibilityFilter({ name, filter(agent, names) })` | narrowing what one agent may see — can only remove names | | `registerTargetResolver({ name, prefix, resolve })` | owning a target prefix, e.g. `cap:` | | `registerRiskGate` / `registerStateProvider` | confirming high-risk loads / keeping state across a restart | Hooks are plain events: `tool-catalog/before-load` (throw to veto), `after-load`, `before-unload`, `after-unload`, `before-rebuild`, `after-rebuild`, `state-changed`. Start from a generated package — it comes with a passing test: ```sh npm create @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-plugin@latest my-ext -- --type classifier cd my-ext && npm test ``` Two worked examples live in [`examples/`](examples), and the full interface list is in the core README and [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md) §11. ## Development Every package is written in TypeScript (`src/`) and compiled to `lib/` (JavaScript plus `.d.ts` type declarations); `lib/` is build output and not committed. The root `tsconfig.json` lists the packages (project references); the two browser halves (`client.ts`) have their own `tsconfig.client.json`, because DSH loads them as classic scripts, not modules. ```sh npm install # also links your local DSH host packages (scripts/link-host.mjs) npm run build # src/*.ts -> lib/*.js + lib/*.d.ts npm run typecheck # strict type check (tsc -b; writes lib/ too, references need it) node --test test/unit/*.test.mjs # pure catalog and registry tests (needs a build) node test/e2e.mjs # boots throwaway DSH instances; never touches your profile ``` Host packages (`@deepseek-ai/*`) are peers and are never installed from the registry (`.npmrc` sets `legacy-peer-deps`): a registry copy next to the plugin would shadow the DSH you actually run. `npm install` links them from `$DSH_APP` (default `~/.local/share/deepseek-harness/app`) instead. ## License Apache-2.0 — see [LICENSE](LICENSE). Releases before Tool Ultra (`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager*`) were MIT.

# @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-persist Keep loaded tools across a DSH restart for [`dsh-tool-ultra-core`](../dsh-tool-ultra-core). Without it, loaded state lives in memory only. Restart DSH mid-task and the model has to walk the directory again. This plugin registers a **state provider** on the `toolCatalog` service: one small JSON file per session, written on every load/unload, read back when the session is adopted again (resume or fork). ## Configuration ```yaml - id: tool-manager-persist name: '@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-persist' config: enabled: true # false disables the plugin dir: ~/.config/deepseek-harness/tool-manager/sessions # default write: true # false = restore only ``` `dir` defaults to `/tool-manager/sessions`. Files are named after the session id, so a session restores exactly its own state. A session with nothing loaded gets no file; unloading everything removes it. ## What is stored ```json { "loaded": ["mcp__amap__maps_weather"], "groups": ["adb"], "excluded": [], "handoffGroups": [], "handoffTools": [] } ``` Groups are stored by name, not by their current tool list, so a group that gains tools later (an MCP server reconnecting) restores with them included. ## Writing your own store The provider interface is the extension point; a plugin that keeps state in a database or in the session log instead of files registers the same shape: ```js ctx.inject(['toolCatalog'], (c) => { c.effect(() => c.toolCatalog.registerStateProvider({ name: 'my-store', load: (agent) => readFromMyStore(agent.id), // serialized state or null save: (agent, state) => writeToMyStore(agent.id, state), })) }) ``` Providers are consulted in registration order; the first one that returns a state wins, and every provider receives each save. Restoring is authoritative: it replaces what the agent would otherwise start from (pinned tools plus the parent's handoff). ## License Apache-2.0 — see [LICENSE](LICENSE). Releases before Tool Ultra (`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager*`) were MIT.

Tool Ultra
On-demand tool loading for DeepSeek Harness — every tool as a directory, loaded only when an agent asks.

English · 中文

--- ## What It Is Tool Ultra is an All-in-One tool-plugin product for DeepSeek Harness, and an important component of [Swiftnest](https://github.com/lvy-jsd/swiftnest). Its goal is one coherent tool product across everyday tasks, web/MCP services, media and device capabilities. The small core and replaceable extension packages are its internal architecture; the product is more than a tool-directory browser. Tools are browsable as a directory (category → group → tool), searchable by intent and loaded on demand, keeping unneeded schemas out of the model's context. Savings depend on catalog size, discovery/load steps and provider caching: compare per-request schemas, total task tokens and task success separately. Broad capability does not mean every external service or upload is enabled by default. The current preview is distributed as source and modular packages; Swiftnest builds a pinned source commit. An AI can install and configure the required modules. The published-package quick-start syntax below applies when those package versions are available on npm; it is not a claim that the renamed 0.5.0 packages have already been published. > **Renamed.** This project was `dsh-tool-manager`. Version 0.5.0 renames every > package from `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager-` to `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-` > (the core is `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core`). Nothing else changes: the entry > tools, the `toolCatalog` service (now also provided as `toolUltra`), the hooks, > the config and the state directory `/tool-manager/` stay the same. > An existing profile can keep `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager`: from 0.5.0 it only > re-exports the new core. Older extension releases keep working with the new core. ## Quick start ```sh # 1. install the core plus the rule-based classifier (optional but recommended) dsh plugin --profile web add @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-rules # 2. restart DSH, then ask the agent: "what tools do you have?" # it answers with tools_ls("/") — a directory, not 200 tool schemas # 3. want the UI? add the panel, then open Settings → "Tool manager" dsh plugin --profile web add @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-panel ``` > **Install the scoped `@lvy-jsd/…` packages.** The unscoped `dsh-tool-manager` > on npm is a different project. Do not install both: each one narrows which > tools an agent can see, so together they hide tools from each other. On a fresh install every group is `uncategorized` until a classifier is installed — the tools are still browsable and loadable, only the categories are missing. See [Extending](#extending) to write your own classifier. `tools_load(["web"])` also accepts bare names: try registered `pack:` → `cap:` → `device:` namespaces, first non-empty match only, then normal directory lookup; explicit prefixes keep their behavior and plugin ownership. ## Packages | Package | What it does | |---|---| | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-core) | Core: directory, `tools_ls` / `tools_load` / `tools_unload`, per-agent allowlist, the `toolCatalog` extension service, plus intent retrieval + routing (`tools_find` / `tools_route` / `skills_find` / `skills_route`, BM25 with a Rust sidecar). Without extensions every group is `uncategorized`. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-rules`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-rules) | Places groups into categories from built-in rules and your config overrides. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-risk-gate`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-risk-gate) | Confirms loading high-risk tools through the DSH approval channel, with a per-session allowlist. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-persist`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-persist) | Keeps loaded tools across a DSH restart, one state file per session. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-panel`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-panel) | Web panel: browse the tree, see each live session's loaded tools and token cost, load/unload from the UI, edit the always-on and high-risk lists, edit one tool's metadata, exempt one session. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-llm`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-llm) | Places groups with a small model, one request per group, cached by a hash of the group and its tool descriptions. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-capability-bridge`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-capability-bridge) | Load a named bundle of tools in one call: `tools_load(["cap:android-debug"])`. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-attribution-scan`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-attribution-scan) | Group tools by the plugin package whose source defines them. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-essentials`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-essentials) | Native tool pack, no API keys: time zones and date math, a calculator with units (mathjs), weather (Open-Meteo), place search (Nominatim), Wikipedia. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-web`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-web) | Native tool pack: `web_read` turns a page into clean Markdown (Readability + turndown), `web_links` lists its links. Refuses private addresses by default. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-mcp`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-mcp) | MCP presets through DSH's MCP client: memory, sequential thinking, Context7, Playwright and filesystem start without keys; GitHub, SearXNG, Brave, Tavily, Firecrawl, Notion and AMap start once their key is set. `mcp_presets` shows the status. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-media`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-media) | Native tool pack, no API keys: images, music and video made from code. `html_render` designs an image in HTML/CSS (no browser) or turns its CSS animations into a GIF, `svg_render` turns an SVG drawing into PNG/JPEG/WebP, `chart_render` draws a Vega-Lite chart, `music_render` plays a score with real recorded instruments (SoundFont, mastered) and saves WAV and MIDI, `video_render` makes an MP4 from CSS-animated HTML, SVG or photo scenes with transitions, captions and a soundtrack (host ffmpeg), `audio_transcribe` turns speech into timestamped text with local SenseVoice / Whisper models, with who speaks when, emotions and sounds such as laughter, `video_understand` reads a video as a timestamped storyboard image plus its transcript. External links and data URLs are refused. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-gc`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-gc) | Artifact and media garbage collection: date-partitioned storage management (`[YYYY-MM-DD]`), retention sweeps, and LRU capacity eviction. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-db`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-db) | In-memory OLAP analytics via embedded DuckDB: query CSV, Parquet, and JSON datasets directly via SQL without context inflation. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-office`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-office) | Office documents pack: Word (.docx) text extraction, Excel (.xlsx) read/write, and PDF document metadata inspection. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-devices`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-devices) | Device namespace: Swiftnest device tools under `/device/`, loadable as `device:current`, `device:all` or `device:`, with offline devices marked. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager-dsbot-entry`](packages/dsh-tool-manager-dsbot-entry) | Deprecated, no longer released. A "Tool manager" row in the ds-bot settings dialog that opens the panel. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager`](packages/dsh-tool-manager) | The old core name: re-exports `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core` so existing profiles keep working. | | [`@lvy-jsd/create-dsh-tool-ultra-plugin`](packages/create-dsh-tool-ultra-plugin) | Scaffold your own extension: `npm create @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-plugin@latest my-ext -- --type classifier`. | See [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md) for the design. ## Extending Every feature beyond the core is an ordinary plugin using the `toolCatalog` service, and the bundled `classifier-rules` package is written exactly as a third party would write it. Four extension points: | Point | For | |---|---| | `registerClassifier({ name, priority, group?, categorize? })` | placing tools into groups and groups into categories | | `annotate(match, { group?, category?, risk?, summary? })` | runtime metadata; `package.json` `dsh.toolCatalog` does the same without code | | `registerVisibilityFilter({ name, filter(agent, names) })` | narrowing what one agent may see — can only remove names | | `registerTargetResolver({ name, prefix, resolve })` | owning a target prefix, e.g. `cap:` | | `registerRiskGate` / `registerStateProvider` | confirming high-risk loads / keeping state across a restart | Hooks are plain events: `tool-catalog/before-load` (throw to veto), `after-load`, `before-unload`, `after-unload`, `before-rebuild`, `after-rebuild`, `state-changed`. Start from a generated package — it comes with a passing test: ```sh npm create @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-plugin@latest my-ext -- --type classifier cd my-ext && npm test ``` Two worked examples live in [`examples/`](examples), and the full interface list is in the core README and [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md) §11. ## Development Every package is written in TypeScript (`src/`) and compiled to `lib/` (JavaScript plus `.d.ts` type declarations); `lib/` is build output and not committed. The root `tsconfig.json` lists the packages (project references); the two browser halves (`client.ts`) have their own `tsconfig.client.json`, because DSH loads them as classic scripts, not modules. ```sh npm install # also links your local DSH host packages (scripts/link-host.mjs) npm run build # src/*.ts -> lib/*.js + lib/*.d.ts npm run typecheck # strict type check (tsc -b; writes lib/ too, references need it) node --test test/unit/*.test.mjs # pure catalog and registry tests (needs a build) node test/e2e.mjs # boots throwaway DSH instances; never touches your profile ``` Host packages (`@deepseek-ai/*`) are peers and are never installed from the registry (`.npmrc` sets `legacy-peer-deps`): a registry copy next to the plugin would shadow the DSH you actually run. `npm install` links them from `$DSH_APP` (default `~/.local/share/deepseek-harness/app`) instead. ## License Apache-2.0 — see [LICENSE](LICENSE). Releases before Tool Ultra (`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager*`) were MIT.

# @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-risk-gate Confirm loading high-risk tools for [`dsh-tool-ultra-core`](../dsh-tool-ultra-core). Loading a tool only makes it visible; it runs nothing. That is why ordinary loads need no confirmation. A few tools are different — merging a pull request, deleting a file — and those are confirmed **at load time**, so the model cannot quietly arm one and call it a step later. ## What it does - registers a **risk gate** on `toolCatalog` (this is what tells the core a gate exists — without one, high-risk loads are refused outright); - listens on `tools/pre-execute`: when a `tools_load` would load at least one high-risk tool, it returns `{ kind: 'ask' }`; - DSH routes that to its approval channel. A session with no channel (headless, a bot without approvals) is **denied automatically** by the host — the safe default; - a per-session allowlist lets a known unattended session skip the prompt. High-risk tools are only ever loaded one at a time. Loading a whole group skips them and tells the model to load them individually, so each confirmation is tied to exactly one dangerous tool. ## Which tools count as high-risk Two sources, either is enough: 1. **Declared in the catalog** — a plugin's `package.json` `dsh.toolCatalog` entry with `"risk": "high"`, or a runtime `annotate()` call; 2. **Listed here** — `DEFAULT_HIGH_RISK` (GitHub's `merge_pull_request`, `delete_file`, `delete_branch`, `create_or_update_file`, `push_files`, `delete_repository`) plus your `highRisk` config. Names in the list (and in `allow`) are matched by their short name too, so `merge_pull_request` also covers the MCP tool `mcp__github__merge_pull_request`. The list is also annotated into the catalog (`risk: 'high'`), so the core treats these tools as high risk everywhere: a group load skips them, and a direct call of a hidden one is refused with a `tools_load` instruction instead of being auto-loaded. Unloading the plugin removes the annotation. Set `defaultHighRisk: false` to use only your own list and catalog declarations. ## Configuration ```yaml - id: tool-manager-risk-gate name: '@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-risk-gate' config: enabled: true highRisk: [my_dangerous_tool] defaultHighRisk: true allow: # An unattended session that must load these without a prompt. sess_abc123: [merge_pull_request] sess_def456: true # every high-risk tool in this session ``` `allow` keys are session ids. Use `true` or `"*"` for all high-risk tools in that session, or a list of tool names. Without an entry, every high-risk load asks — and is denied when the session has no approval channel. ## Writing your own gate The gate is an extension point; anything that confirms a load works: ```js ctx.inject(['toolCatalog'], (c) => { c.effect(() => c.toolCatalog.registerRiskGate({ name: 'my-policy' })) }) ``` Registering a gate is what re-enables high-risk loading; the confirmation itself can come from any `tools/pre-execute` listener that returns `{ kind: 'ask' }` (or `{ kind: 'deny' }` to refuse). ## License Apache-2.0 — see [LICENSE](LICENSE). Releases before Tool Ultra (`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager*`) were MIT.

Tool Ultra
On-demand tool loading for DeepSeek Harness — every tool as a directory, loaded only when an agent asks.

English · 中文

--- ## What It Is Tool Ultra is an All-in-One tool-plugin product for DeepSeek Harness, and an important component of [Swiftnest](https://github.com/lvy-jsd/swiftnest). Its goal is one coherent tool product across everyday tasks, web/MCP services, media and device capabilities. The small core and replaceable extension packages are its internal architecture; the product is more than a tool-directory browser. Tools are browsable as a directory (category → group → tool), searchable by intent and loaded on demand, keeping unneeded schemas out of the model's context. Savings depend on catalog size, discovery/load steps and provider caching: compare per-request schemas, total task tokens and task success separately. Broad capability does not mean every external service or upload is enabled by default. The current preview is distributed as source and modular packages; Swiftnest builds a pinned source commit. An AI can install and configure the required modules. The published-package quick-start syntax below applies when those package versions are available on npm; it is not a claim that the renamed 0.5.0 packages have already been published. > **Renamed.** This project was `dsh-tool-manager`. Version 0.5.0 renames every > package from `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager-` to `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-` > (the core is `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core`). Nothing else changes: the entry > tools, the `toolCatalog` service (now also provided as `toolUltra`), the hooks, > the config and the state directory `/tool-manager/` stay the same. > An existing profile can keep `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager`: from 0.5.0 it only > re-exports the new core. Older extension releases keep working with the new core. ## Quick start ```sh # 1. install the core plus the rule-based classifier (optional but recommended) dsh plugin --profile web add @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-rules # 2. restart DSH, then ask the agent: "what tools do you have?" # it answers with tools_ls("/") — a directory, not 200 tool schemas # 3. want the UI? add the panel, then open Settings → "Tool manager" dsh plugin --profile web add @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-panel ``` > **Install the scoped `@lvy-jsd/…` packages.** The unscoped `dsh-tool-manager` > on npm is a different project. Do not install both: each one narrows which > tools an agent can see, so together they hide tools from each other. On a fresh install every group is `uncategorized` until a classifier is installed — the tools are still browsable and loadable, only the categories are missing. See [Extending](#extending) to write your own classifier. `tools_load(["web"])` also accepts bare names: try registered `pack:` → `cap:` → `device:` namespaces, first non-empty match only, then normal directory lookup; explicit prefixes keep their behavior and plugin ownership. ## Packages | Package | What it does | |---|---| | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-core) | Core: directory, `tools_ls` / `tools_load` / `tools_unload`, per-agent allowlist, the `toolCatalog` extension service, plus intent retrieval + routing (`tools_find` / `tools_route` / `skills_find` / `skills_route`, BM25 with a Rust sidecar). Without extensions every group is `uncategorized`. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-rules`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-rules) | Places groups into categories from built-in rules and your config overrides. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-risk-gate`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-risk-gate) | Confirms loading high-risk tools through the DSH approval channel, with a per-session allowlist. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-persist`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-persist) | Keeps loaded tools across a DSH restart, one state file per session. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-panel`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-panel) | Web panel: browse the tree, see each live session's loaded tools and token cost, load/unload from the UI, edit the always-on and high-risk lists, edit one tool's metadata, exempt one session. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-llm`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-llm) | Places groups with a small model, one request per group, cached by a hash of the group and its tool descriptions. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-capability-bridge`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-capability-bridge) | Load a named bundle of tools in one call: `tools_load(["cap:android-debug"])`. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-attribution-scan`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-attribution-scan) | Group tools by the plugin package whose source defines them. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-essentials`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-essentials) | Native tool pack, no API keys: time zones and date math, a calculator with units (mathjs), weather (Open-Meteo), place search (Nominatim), Wikipedia. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-web`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-web) | Native tool pack: `web_read` turns a page into clean Markdown (Readability + turndown), `web_links` lists its links. Refuses private addresses by default. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-mcp`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-mcp) | MCP presets through DSH's MCP client: memory, sequential thinking, Context7, Playwright and filesystem start without keys; GitHub, SearXNG, Brave, Tavily, Firecrawl, Notion and AMap start once their key is set. `mcp_presets` shows the status. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-media`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-media) | Native tool pack, no API keys: images, music and video made from code. `html_render` designs an image in HTML/CSS (no browser) or turns its CSS animations into a GIF, `svg_render` turns an SVG drawing into PNG/JPEG/WebP, `chart_render` draws a Vega-Lite chart, `music_render` plays a score with real recorded instruments (SoundFont, mastered) and saves WAV and MIDI, `video_render` makes an MP4 from CSS-animated HTML, SVG or photo scenes with transitions, captions and a soundtrack (host ffmpeg), `audio_transcribe` turns speech into timestamped text with local SenseVoice / Whisper models, with who speaks when, emotions and sounds such as laughter, `video_understand` reads a video as a timestamped storyboard image plus its transcript. External links and data URLs are refused. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-gc`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-gc) | Artifact and media garbage collection: date-partitioned storage management (`[YYYY-MM-DD]`), retention sweeps, and LRU capacity eviction. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-db`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-db) | In-memory OLAP analytics via embedded DuckDB: query CSV, Parquet, and JSON datasets directly via SQL without context inflation. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-office`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-office) | Office documents pack: Word (.docx) text extraction, Excel (.xlsx) read/write, and PDF document metadata inspection. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-devices`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-devices) | Device namespace: Swiftnest device tools under `/device/`, loadable as `device:current`, `device:all` or `device:`, with offline devices marked. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager-dsbot-entry`](packages/dsh-tool-manager-dsbot-entry) | Deprecated, no longer released. A "Tool manager" row in the ds-bot settings dialog that opens the panel. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager`](packages/dsh-tool-manager) | The old core name: re-exports `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core` so existing profiles keep working. | | [`@lvy-jsd/create-dsh-tool-ultra-plugin`](packages/create-dsh-tool-ultra-plugin) | Scaffold your own extension: `npm create @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-plugin@latest my-ext -- --type classifier`. | See [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md) for the design. ## Extending Every feature beyond the core is an ordinary plugin using the `toolCatalog` service, and the bundled `classifier-rules` package is written exactly as a third party would write it. Four extension points: | Point | For | |---|---| | `registerClassifier({ name, priority, group?, categorize? })` | placing tools into groups and groups into categories | | `annotate(match, { group?, category?, risk?, summary? })` | runtime metadata; `package.json` `dsh.toolCatalog` does the same without code | | `registerVisibilityFilter({ name, filter(agent, names) })` | narrowing what one agent may see — can only remove names | | `registerTargetResolver({ name, prefix, resolve })` | owning a target prefix, e.g. `cap:` | | `registerRiskGate` / `registerStateProvider` | confirming high-risk loads / keeping state across a restart | Hooks are plain events: `tool-catalog/before-load` (throw to veto), `after-load`, `before-unload`, `after-unload`, `before-rebuild`, `after-rebuild`, `state-changed`. Start from a generated package — it comes with a passing test: ```sh npm create @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-plugin@latest my-ext -- --type classifier cd my-ext && npm test ``` Two worked examples live in [`examples/`](examples), and the full interface list is in the core README and [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md) §11. ## Development Every package is written in TypeScript (`src/`) and compiled to `lib/` (JavaScript plus `.d.ts` type declarations); `lib/` is build output and not committed. The root `tsconfig.json` lists the packages (project references); the two browser halves (`client.ts`) have their own `tsconfig.client.json`, because DSH loads them as classic scripts, not modules. ```sh npm install # also links your local DSH host packages (scripts/link-host.mjs) npm run build # src/*.ts -> lib/*.js + lib/*.d.ts npm run typecheck # strict type check (tsc -b; writes lib/ too, references need it) node --test test/unit/*.test.mjs # pure catalog and registry tests (needs a build) node test/e2e.mjs # boots throwaway DSH instances; never touches your profile ``` Host packages (`@deepseek-ai/*`) are peers and are never installed from the registry (`.npmrc` sets `legacy-peer-deps`): a registry copy next to the plugin would shadow the DSH you actually run. `npm install` links them from `$DSH_APP` (default `~/.local/share/deepseek-harness/app`) instead. ## License Apache-2.0 — see [LICENSE](LICENSE). Releases before Tool Ultra (`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager*`) were MIT.

Tool Ultra
On-demand tool loading for DeepSeek Harness — every tool as a directory, loaded only when an agent asks.

English · 中文

--- ## What It Is Tool Ultra is an All-in-One tool-plugin product for DeepSeek Harness, and an important component of [Swiftnest](https://github.com/lvy-jsd/swiftnest). Its goal is one coherent tool product across everyday tasks, web/MCP services, media and device capabilities. The small core and replaceable extension packages are its internal architecture; the product is more than a tool-directory browser. Tools are browsable as a directory (category → group → tool), searchable by intent and loaded on demand, keeping unneeded schemas out of the model's context. Savings depend on catalog size, discovery/load steps and provider caching: compare per-request schemas, total task tokens and task success separately. Broad capability does not mean every external service or upload is enabled by default. The current preview is distributed as source and modular packages; Swiftnest builds a pinned source commit. An AI can install and configure the required modules. The published-package quick-start syntax below applies when those package versions are available on npm; it is not a claim that the renamed 0.5.0 packages have already been published. > **Renamed.** This project was `dsh-tool-manager`. Version 0.5.0 renames every > package from `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager-` to `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-` > (the core is `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core`). Nothing else changes: the entry > tools, the `toolCatalog` service (now also provided as `toolUltra`), the hooks, > the config and the state directory `/tool-manager/` stay the same. > An existing profile can keep `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager`: from 0.5.0 it only > re-exports the new core. Older extension releases keep working with the new core. ## Quick start ```sh # 1. install the core plus the rule-based classifier (optional but recommended) dsh plugin --profile web add @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-rules # 2. restart DSH, then ask the agent: "what tools do you have?" # it answers with tools_ls("/") — a directory, not 200 tool schemas # 3. want the UI? add the panel, then open Settings → "Tool manager" dsh plugin --profile web add @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-panel ``` > **Install the scoped `@lvy-jsd/…` packages.** The unscoped `dsh-tool-manager` > on npm is a different project. Do not install both: each one narrows which > tools an agent can see, so together they hide tools from each other. On a fresh install every group is `uncategorized` until a classifier is installed — the tools are still browsable and loadable, only the categories are missing. See [Extending](#extending) to write your own classifier. `tools_load(["web"])` also accepts bare names: try registered `pack:` → `cap:` → `device:` namespaces, first non-empty match only, then normal directory lookup; explicit prefixes keep their behavior and plugin ownership. ## Packages | Package | What it does | |---|---| | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-core) | Core: directory, `tools_ls` / `tools_load` / `tools_unload`, per-agent allowlist, the `toolCatalog` extension service, plus intent retrieval + routing (`tools_find` / `tools_route` / `skills_find` / `skills_route`, BM25 with a Rust sidecar). Without extensions every group is `uncategorized`. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-rules`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-rules) | Places groups into categories from built-in rules and your config overrides. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-risk-gate`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-risk-gate) | Confirms loading high-risk tools through the DSH approval channel, with a per-session allowlist. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-persist`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-persist) | Keeps loaded tools across a DSH restart, one state file per session. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-panel`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-panel) | Web panel: browse the tree, see each live session's loaded tools and token cost, load/unload from the UI, edit the always-on and high-risk lists, edit one tool's metadata, exempt one session. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-llm`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-classifier-llm) | Places groups with a small model, one request per group, cached by a hash of the group and its tool descriptions. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-capability-bridge`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-capability-bridge) | Load a named bundle of tools in one call: `tools_load(["cap:android-debug"])`. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-attribution-scan`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-attribution-scan) | Group tools by the plugin package whose source defines them. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-essentials`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-essentials) | Native tool pack, no API keys: time zones and date math, a calculator with units (mathjs), weather (Open-Meteo), place search (Nominatim), Wikipedia. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-web`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-web) | Native tool pack: `web_read` turns a page into clean Markdown (Readability + turndown), `web_links` lists its links. Refuses private addresses by default. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-mcp`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-mcp) | MCP presets through DSH's MCP client: memory, sequential thinking, Context7, Playwright and filesystem start without keys; GitHub, SearXNG, Brave, Tavily, Firecrawl, Notion and AMap start once their key is set. `mcp_presets` shows the status. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-media`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-media) | Native tool pack, no API keys: images, music and video made from code. `html_render` designs an image in HTML/CSS (no browser) or turns its CSS animations into a GIF, `svg_render` turns an SVG drawing into PNG/JPEG/WebP, `chart_render` draws a Vega-Lite chart, `music_render` plays a score with real recorded instruments (SoundFont, mastered) and saves WAV and MIDI, `video_render` makes an MP4 from CSS-animated HTML, SVG or photo scenes with transitions, captions and a soundtrack (host ffmpeg), `audio_transcribe` turns speech into timestamped text with local SenseVoice / Whisper models, with who speaks when, emotions and sounds such as laughter, `video_understand` reads a video as a timestamped storyboard image plus its transcript. External links and data URLs are refused. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-gc`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-gc) | Artifact and media garbage collection: date-partitioned storage management (`[YYYY-MM-DD]`), retention sweeps, and LRU capacity eviction. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-db`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-db) | In-memory OLAP analytics via embedded DuckDB: query CSV, Parquet, and JSON datasets directly via SQL without context inflation. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-office`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-office) | Office documents pack: Word (.docx) text extraction, Excel (.xlsx) read/write, and PDF document metadata inspection. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-devices`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-devices) | Device namespace: Swiftnest device tools under `/device/`, loadable as `device:current`, `device:all` or `device:`, with offline devices marked. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager-dsbot-entry`](packages/dsh-tool-manager-dsbot-entry) | Deprecated, no longer released. A "Tool manager" row in the ds-bot settings dialog that opens the panel. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager`](packages/dsh-tool-manager) | The old core name: re-exports `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core` so existing profiles keep working. | | [`@lvy-jsd/create-dsh-tool-ultra-plugin`](packages/create-dsh-tool-ultra-plugin) | Scaffold your own extension: `npm create @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-plugin@latest my-ext -- --type classifier`. | See [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md) for the design. ## Extending Every feature beyond the core is an ordinary plugin using the `toolCatalog` service, and the bundled `classifier-rules` package is written exactly as a third party would write it. Four extension points: | Point | For | |---|---| | `registerClassifier({ name, priority, group?, categorize? })` | placing tools into groups and groups into categories | | `annotate(match, { group?, category?, risk?, summary? })` | runtime metadata; `package.json` `dsh.toolCatalog` does the same without code | | `registerVisibilityFilter({ name, filter(agent, names) })` | narrowing what one agent may see — can only remove names | | `registerTargetResolver({ name, prefix, resolve })` | owning a target prefix, e.g. `cap:` | | `registerRiskGate` / `registerStateProvider` | confirming high-risk loads / keeping state across a restart | Hooks are plain events: `tool-catalog/before-load` (throw to veto), `after-load`, `before-unload`, `after-unload`, `before-rebuild`, `after-rebuild`, `state-changed`. Start from a generated package — it comes with a passing test: ```sh npm create @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-plugin@latest my-ext -- --type classifier cd my-ext && npm test ``` Two worked examples live in [`examples/`](examples), and the full interface list is in the core README and [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md) §11. ## Development Every package is written in TypeScript (`src/`) and compiled to `lib/` (JavaScript plus `.d.ts` type declarations); `lib/` is build output and not committed. The root `tsconfig.json` lists the packages (project references); the two browser halves (`client.ts`) have their own `tsconfig.client.json`, because DSH loads them as classic scripts, not modules. ```sh npm install # also links your local DSH host packages (scripts/link-host.mjs) npm run build # src/*.ts -> lib/*.js + lib/*.d.ts npm run typecheck # strict type check (tsc -b; writes lib/ too, references need it) node --test test/unit/*.test.mjs # pure catalog and registry tests (needs a build) node test/e2e.mjs # boots throwaway DSH instances; never touches your profile ``` Host packages (`@deepseek-ai/*`) are peers and are never installed from the registry (`.npmrc` sets `legacy-peer-deps`): a registry copy next to the plugin would shadow the DSH you actually run. `npm install` links them from `$DSH_APP` (default `~/.local/share/deepseek-harness/app`) instead. ## License Apache-2.0 — see [LICENSE](LICENSE). Releases before Tool Ultra (`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager*`) were MIT.

Refuses private addresses by default. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-mcp`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-mcp) | MCP presets through DSH's MCP client: memory, sequential thinking, Context7, Playwright and filesystem start without keys; GitHub, SearXNG, Brave, Tavily, Firecrawl, Notion and AMap start once their key is set. `mcp_presets` shows the status. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-media`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-media) | Native tool pack, no API keys: images, music and video made from code. `html_render` designs an image in HTML/CSS (no browser) or turns its CSS animations into a GIF, `svg_render` turns an SVG drawing into PNG/JPEG/WebP, `chart_render` draws a Vega-Lite chart, `music_render` plays a score with real recorded instruments (SoundFont, mastered) and saves WAV and MIDI, `video_render` makes an MP4 from CSS-animated HTML, SVG or photo scenes with transitions, captions and a soundtrack (host ffmpeg), `audio_transcribe` turns speech into timestamped text with local SenseVoice / Whisper models, with who speaks when, emotions and sounds such as laughter, `video_understand` reads a video as a timestamped storyboard image plus its transcript. External links and data URLs are refused. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-gc`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-gc) | Artifact and media garbage collection: date-partitioned storage management (`[YYYY-MM-DD]`), retention sweeps, and LRU capacity eviction. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-db`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-db) | In-memory OLAP analytics via embedded DuckDB: query CSV, Parquet, and JSON datasets directly via SQL without context inflation. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-office`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-pack-office) | Office documents pack: Word (.docx) text extraction, Excel (.xlsx) read/write, and PDF document metadata inspection. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-devices`](packages/dsh-tool-ultra-devices) | Device namespace: Swiftnest device tools under `/device/`, loadable as `device:current`, `device:all` or `device:`, with offline devices marked. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager-dsbot-entry`](packages/dsh-tool-manager-dsbot-entry) | Deprecated, no longer released. A "Tool manager" row in the ds-bot settings dialog that opens the panel. | | [`@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-manager`](packages/dsh-tool-manager) | The old core name: re-exports `@lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-core` so existing profiles keep working. | | [`@lvy-jsd/create-dsh-tool-ultra-plugin`](packages/create-dsh-tool-ultra-plugin) | Scaffold your own extension: `npm create @lvy-jsd/dsh-tool-ultra-plugin@latest my-ext -- --type classifier`. | See [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md) for the design. ## Extending Every feature beyond the core is an ordinary plugin using the `toolCatalog` service, and the bundled `classifier-rules` package is written exactly as a third party would write it. Broad capability does not mean every external service or upload is enabled by default. The current preview is distributed as source and modular packages; Swiftnest builds a pinned source commit. An AI can install and configure the required modules. evidence.readmeExcerpt: # Message metrics A DeepSeek Harness plugin that puts a gauge action under every assistant reply. Opening it shows that reply's performance dashboard: ![The performance dashboard opened above an assistant reply](docs/panel.png) | Reading | Source | | --- | --- | | Model | the request's provider/model route | | Prompt | every prompt token the request took in (uncached + cached + cache write) | | Cached | cache-read tokens and their exact share of the prompt | | Uncached | prompt tokens the model actually computed | | Output | completion tokens, with the reasoning share when reported | | First token | `step/start` → first streamed delta | | Prefill | prompt tokens / first-token time (includes cache restore) | | Uncached compute | cache misses plus cache writes / first-token time | | Decode | output tokens / decode time | | Total | `step/start` → final assistant message | The panel describes **one assistant reply**. The usage pill beside it (`用量 … tok`) aggregates the whole turn across every step, so the two numbers answer different questions: this panel is the request that produced the closing answer, the pill is every request in the turn. When almost the whole prompt is served from a provider cache, the Uncached row is small and the prefill rate is the cache-inclusive ingestion rate; the Uncached compute row is that small share over the same first-token window, so it stays low even though the request returned quickly. Read Decode for model generation speed. Everything is derived from the durable message the Session already records (provider usage plus the step and chunk timestamps), so the dashboard works for every provider, local or cloud, and adds no request of its own. The readings come from two conversation targets and are merged field by field: - the **Chat** target supplies the settled message and its token buckets; - the **Trajectory** target supplies the durable first-token time (it folds the packed stream records back into a timestamp) and the provider/model route, which the Chat target does not carry. An assembly without the Trajectory view still shows the token rows; timing and the model row then fall back to the Chat target and may read `—`. The trigger matches the shipped assistant action strip (28px IconActions, 15–17px gauge glyph, tertiary label colour). The panel reuses the stat-dialog skin: menu surface, `--dsw-elevation-prominent`, the 12px detail grid, and viewport-clamped placement above the trigger. ## Install Add it to your DSH profile as a linked dependency and select the `@local/dsh-message-metrics` bundle: ```json "@local/dsh-message-metrics": "link:/absolute/path/to/dsh-message-metrics" ``` The bundle name is `@local/dsh-message-metrics`; after the next load the gauge appears in every assistant message's action row. Or install with the CLI: ```bash dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:LXD-8/dsh-message-metrics ``` ## Usage Click the gauge under a reply. The headline shows decode throughput; the rows below list the model, token buckets, first-token latency, prefill and decode throughput, and total request time. Escape or an outside click closes it. ## License MIT

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# AgentPilot for DSH 在 DeepSeek Harness（DSH）中连接 AgentPilot，从手机、平板或 Web 查看 DSH 会话、继续对话、回复提问和审批请求。Agent 仍在安装 DSH 的工作设备上运行；远程使用时，这台设备需要保持开机、联网，并让 DSH 与 Connector 正常运行。 插件随 **DSH Desktop** 提供，也可从 **npm** 安装到兼容的独立 DSH 环境。两种安装方式选其一；使用 DSH Desktop 时无需重复安装 npm 包。 ## 可以做什么 - 在其他设备上查看 DSH 会话与运行进度，发送消息或继续已有会话。 - 根据 DSH 和当前会话的能力选择模型、权限与 Agent 模式，发送文字、图片或普通文件，回复输入请求与单次操作审批。 - 使用自己的服务实例；在插件中查看连接状态、管理本机 Connector 和桥接日志。 - 如果 AgentPilot Desktop 正在运行，转到该应用完成连接；否则可以直接在插件中登录并连接本机设备。AgentPilot Desktop 和 DSH Desktop 是两个不同的应用。 ## 在 DSH Desktop 中启用 DSH Desktop 已集成此插件，**不需要另行下载或执行 npm 安装命令**。在 DSH Desktop 的“插件”页面找到“远程控制”并启用，然后从左侧边栏“设置”上方打开“远程控制”。部分 Desktop 版本的开关位于“桌面设置”的“手机连接”区域；请以当前应用显示的入口为准。 ![DSH Desktop 中的 AgentPilot 连接面板，显示账号和 Connector 运行状态](docs/images/remote-control-desktop.webp) 首次使用时输入自己部署的服务端地址，然后在浏览器中完成登录和授权。若这份部署通过插件配置 `apiBaseUrl` 固定了默认服务地址，插件会额外显示「登录 AgentPilot Cloud」入口；未配置时只保留自建入口。按照页面引导添加 Agent，并按需连接手机。若插件检测到 AgentPilot Desktop 正在运行，会引导你到该应用继续设置，避免两个应用同时管理同一台工作设备的连接。 插件随 DSH Desktop 一同打包和更新；请通过 Desktop 的发布渠道升级，不要对内置插件叠加独立 npm 安装。 ## 从 npm 安装到独立 DSH 如果使用独立安装的 DSH，可以通过官方插件命令从 npm 安装。先确认目标 Profile 的名称，以及当前 npm 包声明的 DSH 依赖是否与你的环境相容。下面以 `desktop` Profile 为例： ```bash dsh plugin --profile desktop add @agent-pilot/dsh-bridge-next ``` 安装完成后重启对应的 DSH 实例，从左侧边栏打开“远程控制”，按提示登录并连接。若你的 Profile 不是 `desktop`，请替换命令中的 Profile 名称。 安装命令不锁定插件版本，会获取 npm 当前的默认发布版本。插件包与 DSH 的兼容范围请以所安装版本的 `peerDependencies` 为准；较新的 DSH 不代表旧插件包自动兼容。当前仓库源码声明支持 DSH `0.2.0-rc.1` 及之后的 0.2.x 版本（peer 范围 `>=0.2.0-rc.1 <0.3.0-0`），开发与测试基线为 `0.2.0-rc.2`。DSH 在安装和启动插件时都会按这个范围检查，不满足时拒绝安装或跳过加载；DSH Desktop 使用与自身版本配套的内置构建，不能简单等同于 npm 上的包。需要固定可复现的部署时，再在包名后添加经过验证的版本号。 ## 确认 DSH 已接入 完成连接后，在 AgentPilot 的设备页面可以看到设备在线，以及 DSH 运行时的状态。下图展示了 DSH 正在运行的设备；如果状态未出现或显示断开，先检查工作设备上的 DSH 和 Connector。 ![AgentPilot 设备页面显示设备在线，DSH Agent Runtime 正在运行](docs/images/dsh-runtime-connected.webp) ## 使用条件与数据范围 - 远程连接需要 AgentPilot 账号和可访问的服务端。自托管时输入后端地址；手机扫码时，手机也需要能够访问该服务。 - 会话、时间线和附件等数据会按所用功能经过或保存在 AgentPilot Server；自托管时由你部署的服务处理。模型账号与费用遵循所用模型服务的规则。 - 账号与设备凭据保存在本机插件数据目录，不放入页面跳转 URL。设备凭据失效或设备被删除时，插件会提示重新连接或创建，不会静默注册新设备。 - 如果 DSH 原生历史读取失败，对应会话的历史可能无法同步；其他会话仍可工作。在“桥接日志”中查看原因，修复原生历史后重试。插件不会自行修改 DSH 会话文件。 ## 开发与进一步阅读 本仓库源码和 npm 已发布包可能处于不同版本。源码构建、链接安装、headless 检查、配置和实现细节见[技术说明](https://github.com/lxfebd/AgentPilot/blob/main/dsh-bridge-next/TECHNICAL.md)。 [开发计划](https://github.com/lxfebd/AgentPilot/blob/main/dsh-bridge-next/DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md) · [Onboarding 方案](https://github.com/lxfebd/AgentPilot/blob/main/dsh-bridge-next/ONBOARDING_PLAN.md) · [验证记录](https://github.com/lxfebd/AgentPilot/blob/main/dsh-bridge-next/VERIFICATION.md)

AgentPilot：跨设备的开源 Agent 工作台
连接工作设备，在桌面、手机和 Web 管理 AI Agent。

开源 · 多种 Agent · 会话与工作区 · 自托管

下载客户端 · 部署并打开 Web · English

**AgentPilot** 是跨设备的开源 Agent 工作台。连接运行 **Codex、Claude Code 或 DeepSeek Harness** 的工作设备，在桌面、手机和 Web 查看会话、回复请求、管理文件与终端。Agent 在连接的工作设备上执行任务。 ## 下载与入口 在工作设备上安装桌面客户端，再通过手机、平板或 Web 访问。Linux 和无图形界面的服务器可使用 Connector CLI 接入。各客户端连接你自己部署的服务实例。 | 平台 | 获取客户端 | | --- | --- | | **macOS** | [GitHub Releases · Universal DMG](https://github.com/lxfebd/AgentPilot/releases) | | **Windows** | [GitHub Releases · x64 安装包](https://github.com/lxfebd/AgentPilot/releases) | | **Android** | [GitHub Releases · APK](https://github.com/lxfebd/AgentPilot/releases) | | **iOS / iPadOS** | [App Store](https://apps.apple.com/cn/app/agent-pilot) · [TestFlight](https://testflight.apple.com/join/AgentPilot) | | **Web** | 部署自己的服务后打开对应地址（见[自托管快速开始](#自托管快速开始)） | | **Linux / headless** | [运行 Connector CLI](connector/README.md) | > 正式发布后，上面的安装包链接会指向对应 Release；当前 `main` 是开发主线，源码中的新修复不一定已进入安装包。
平台要求、安装包与更新说明 - macOS：Apple Silicon / Intel 通用，已签名、公证；需要 macOS 12 及以上。 - Windows：x64 桌面工作台，含本机 Connector；当前安装包未做代码签名。 - Android：Android 8.0 及以上。 - iOS / iPadOS：在 App Store 下载安装；也可以通过 TestFlight 安装测试版，以邀请页显示的可用状态为准。 - Linux / headless：运行 Connector 接入工作设备，通过其他客户端操作。 各端 PATCH 版本独立发布，数据库 schema revision 单独编号。
## Agent 与工作区管理 | 你想做的事 | 在 AgentPilot 中 | | --- | --- | | **管理项目与会话** | 在设备、项目和会话之间切换，通过时间线（Timeline）查看运行进度。 | | **审批操作与回复请求** | 响应工具审批和输入请求；按 Runtime 能力打断或继续任务。 | | **查看文件与使用终端** | 浏览与预览文件、上传下载附件，打开远程 shell 和交互式终端。 | | **配置 Agent** | 配置 Codex、Claude Code、DSH 与 Pi（ACP）；根据对应 Runtime 支持的能力选择模型、权限与操作。 | | **计划模式与计划审阅** | 用 `/plan` 让 Agent 先给出可评审的计划，同意后再执行；计划版本与执行状态显示在会话时间线里。 | | **附件与流式传输** | 发送图片与附件，大文件边下边用；被拒绝的附件会说明原因，不会静默失败。 | Runtime 是工作设备上运行和连接 Agent 的组件。模型账号和调用费用遵循所使用 Agent 的规则。各 Runtime 的能力存在差异，具体操作以客户端显示为准。[DSH 接入说明 →](dsh-bridge-next/README.md) ## 桌面、移动端与 Web 用手机查看进展、回复 Agent，在平板上打开工作区，回到电脑后继续处理。同一服务、同一账号下，自己的设备和会话可以从不同客户端访问。 **手机负责控制，工作设备负责执行。** 远程使用时，工作设备需要保持开机、联网，并让 Connector 与对应 Runtime 正常运行。 ## 首次使用 1. **登录服务。** 安装客户端或打开 Web，填写你的服务地址并登录。 2. **连接工作设备。** Desktop 集成本机 Connector；服务器与无图形环境使用 [Connector CLI](connector/README.md)。 3. **准备 Agent 和项目。** 在工作设备上配置 Runtime、账号与工作目录，创建或打开会话。 4. **从其他设备访问。** 在手机、平板或另一台电脑登录同一服务和账号，访问自己的设备与任务。 ## 执行位置与自托管 Agent 使用 Connector 所在机器的工作区与权限。服务部署在你自己的服务器上，客户端填入该地址即可。 ```mermaid flowchart LR Clients["桌面 · 手机 · Web"] <-->|"访问与控制"| Server["AgentPilot Server"] Server <-->|"Connector RPC"| Connector["工作设备上的 Connector"] Connector <--> Agents["Codex · Claude Code · DSH"] Connector <--> Workspace["工作区 · 文件 · 终端"] ``` 会话内容、Timeline 和上传附件等数据会按功能经过或存储在 Server。自托管时，这些服务端数据由你部署的实例处理。 ### 使用 Docker 部署 克隆仓库后，在根目录运行以下命令，先替换示例密码和密钥： ```bash POSTGRES_PASSWORD=replace-with-a-strong-password \ AGENT_SERVER_SECRET=replace-with-a-long-random-secret \ docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.postgres.yml up --build ``` 打开 `http://127.0.0.1:5174`，从 Server 日志取得 setup token，完成首位管理员设置。Compose 包含 PostgreSQL、Redis、迁移任务以及托管 Web 的 Server。 [完整部署步骤](docker/README.md) · [Server 文档](server/README.md) ## 开发与贡献 开发环境使用 **Python 3.12+ / uv / Node.js 22 / Corepack + Yarn**。 | 想了解什么 | 从这里开始 | | --- | --- | | Agent 接入与本机执行 | [Connector](connector/README.md) | | Web 与桌面客户端 | [Web 源码](web-next/) · [Desktop Workbench](desktop-workbench/README.md) | | 原生移动客户端 | [Android](android/README.md) · [iOS 源码](ios/) | | DSH 集成 | [DSH Bridge Next](dsh-bridge-next/README.md) | 欢迎通过 [Issues](https://github.com/lxfebd/AgentPilot/issues) 反馈问题，或通过 [Pull Requests](https://github.com/lxfebd/AgentPilot/pulls) 参与改进。报告问题时，请附上客户端版本、系统、Runtime 类型和复现步骤，并移除日志中的凭据。 ## 交流与反馈 欢迎通过 [Issues](https://github.com/lxfebd/AgentPilot/issues) 反馈问题、通过 [Pull Requests](https://github.com/lxfebd/AgentPilot/pulls) 参与改进。如果项目对你有用，欢迎在 [GitHub](https://github.com/lxfebd/AgentPilot) 点个 Star。 ## 开源许可 MIT。本项目的品牌、下载入口与社区以本项目仓库为准。 > **致谢**：AgentPilot 基于 [Agents Anywhere](https://github.com/anywhere-labs/Agents-Anywhere)（MIT License）二次开发并更名。感谢原作者的开源工作。
