--- description: "The shared dsh core: model access, tools, durable sessions, and safety defaults for every dsh --profile surface, for users composing or customizing a profile." kind: "package-bundle" --- # @deepseek-ai/dsh-base English | [中文](README.zh.md) ## Summary Every base-backed `dsh --profile` surface runs on `dsh-base`, so those surfaces share a model connection, the full tool set, durable session history, and workspace safety defaults. The shipped `sdk-minimal` profile deliberately uses a complete standalone tree instead. You rarely touch this bundle directly — shipped base-backed profiles already include it, and a custom base-backed profile names it first. When you need different defaults, change your profile patch or add a later bundle; this package is not a library you import. ## Table of Contents - [Use this package](#use-this-package) - [Understand the implementation](#understand-the-implementation) - [Further Exploration](#further-exploration) - [Model Experience](#model-experience) - [Known Limitations and Deferred Work](#known-limitations-and-deferred-work) - [Dev Note](#dev-note) ----- ## Use this package You get the dsh core automatically: the shipped `web`, `headless`, `sdk`, and `acp` profiles already include it, and a custom profile names it as its first bundle. After that, everything works with no further configuration. ### A minimal custom profile To build a profile on the shared core, create a profile with a `package.json` that names `@deepseek-ai/dsh-base` first: ```json { "name": "my-profile", "private": true, "dsh": { "profile": { "bundles": ["@deepseek-ai/dsh-base"] } } } ``` Run `dsh --profile my-profile "your task"` and you get a working agent with model access, tools, persistence, and the default permission policy. The shipped `web`, `headless`, `sdk`, and `acp` profiles are created for you on first use. To add more bundles, run `dsh plugin --profile add `; in-box bundles resolve from the dsh installation. The profile contract is documented in the [app-boot profile section](../../boot/app-boot/README.md). ### What you get Out of the box, every profile built on this core provides: a DeepSeek model connection (the provider and model are configurable, and you can enable extra providers from your settings), the full tool set — file editing, shell commands, web search, public HTTP(S) fetch, subagents, task and goal tracking — durable sessions that survive restarts, and the default permission policy that confines file writes to your workspace and asks before risky actions. Web fetch runs without per-call approval; its provider rejects non-public destinations. Feedback stays in the Session log. [OTel session upload](../../session/session-telemetry-otel/README.md) defaults to `FEEDBACK_ONLY` for all users, including `deepseek-official`: new text feedback, message ratings, edits, and withdrawals release the complete canonical prefix through that event, including context. Later records wait for the next explicit feedback; sending an authorized batch needs no further interaction or model call. `DISABLED` prevents OTel capture. The opt-in [DeepSeek session-log contributor](../../session/session-log-deepseek/README.md) remains a separate request path. Default file editing uses `read`, `write`, and `edit`. The `str_replace_editor` tool remains available as an explicit opt-in. To add it to a base-backed profile, put this entry in the profile, home, or invocation patch: ```yaml - insert: - id: tool-str-replace-editor name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-str-replace-editor' config: maxOutputChars: 16000 ``` ### Shell tools per platform On macOS and Linux you get the bash shell tools; on Windows you get the PowerShell twins instead, so exactly one shell stack is available per machine. The safety behavior is identical on every platform. A Windows host that prefers the unconfined PowerShell executor can switch the shell rows in its profile patch — the switch must disable both PowerShell rows and re-enable both bash rows, otherwise the profile fails to load. ### Changing the defaults To change what a profile built on this core provides — a different default model, a stricter permission mode, extra or fewer tools — edit your profile's `cordis.patch.yml` or add a later bundle. Each patch entry replaces the target's whole configuration, so restate every setting you want to keep. Keep the sandboxed filesystem provider as the single file-write path: adding the plain filesystem provider on top of it makes the profile fail to load. ----- ## Understand the implementation
Implementation internals — click to expand The bundle is a static patch document: one `insert` list applied over the empty profile root. It mounts no service, emits no events, and holds no mutable state; each inserted row's package owns that row's behavior and invariants. ### Composition mechanics A patch replaces the targeted row's whole `config` rather than merging into it. Later bundle layers and the user's profile `cordis.patch.yml` override rows by id, with the last write winning per row. Rows whose value differs by mode do not live here: each mode bundle restates its complete configuration, keeping any single row down to one bundle layer plus the user's. The full row set and its rationale are documented inline in [`cordis.patch.yml`](cordis.patch.yml); the [generated composition graph](../../../apps/cli/composition.md) renders it. ### Platform gating The patch gates the two shell stacks by platform on its own rows: `bash-sandbox` and `tool-bash` carry `disabled: !!js process.platform === 'win32'`, and their twins `pwsh-sandbox` and `tool-pwsh` mount on win32 only with the inverted expression. The permission surface stays identical to POSIX: the sandbox policy executes the same file-effect policy through the Windows ACL restricted-token runner (`dsh-sandbox-local` → `@deepseek-ai/dsh-sandbox-windows-acl`), and `fs-sandbox` keeps fencing `ctx.fs` writes — mounting `dsh-fs-local` alongside it would double-register `ctx.fs` and fail the load. ### Source map | File | Role | |---|---| | [`cordis.patch.yml`](cordis.patch.yml) | The bundle substance: the base plugin rows, with per-row rationale as inline comments | | [`src/index.ts`](src/index.ts) | Package entry; carries no runtime API | | — | No runtime invariant companion is published; the package is a static patch-list carrier (a YAML document of loader rows owned by other packages); it mounts no service, emits no events, and owns no mutable relation to check. Each inserted row's own package carries that row's invariants. | | [`tests/base.spec.ts`](tests/base.spec.ts) | Manifest declaration and platform-gating checks | ### Invariant ownership No invariant companion is published because the package is a static patch-list carrier: each inserted row's package owns that row's invariants, and the bundle owns no mutable relation to check.
----- ## Further Exploration Read these pages when you want to go deeper into profiles, the surfaces built on this core, or the exact composition. - [app-boot profile section](../../boot/app-boot/README.md) — how profiles are resolved, layered, and customized. - [Bundle package map](../README.md) — the surfaces built on this core. - [Generated composition graph](../../../apps/cli/composition.md) — the exact plugin set each shipped profile uses. - [Profile plugin bundles note](../../../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-08-05-profile-plugin-bundles.md) — the profile and bundle composition design. - [Codex and Claude Code provider bundles](../../subagent/README.md) — optional provider bundles you can install on top. ----- ## Model Experience Indirectly, through each inserted row's package, which owns that row's model-facing behavior. #### KV Cache effect The bundle itself adds no request prefix; each inserted row's package owns any cache effect. ## Known Limitations and Deferred Work These limits tell you when the core needs extra care or where an override must go. They are current package constraints, not a general comparison or a task backlog. - **Overrides replace whole settings blocks** — a patch entry replaces the target's entire configuration, so your override must restate every setting you want to keep; nothing merges automatically. - **Per-surface settings belong to the surface's bundle** — a default that differs between the web GUI and headless mode lives in that surface's bundle, not in the shared core. - **Windows temp grants are private per-session subdirectories** — `workspace-write` confines writes to the workspace plus the session's own temp subdirectory (`\dsh-`, TMP/TEMP rewritten for confined children); `read-only` grants nothing. See `@deepseek-ai/dsh-sandbox-windows-acl`. - **Adding the plain filesystem provider on top of the sandboxed one fails the profile** — the two register the same service, so the profile refuses to load; use one or the other. ### Dev Note

--- description: "One-shot task mode for dsh: run a single task from the command line and get the final answer printed, for users scripting or automating dsh." kind: "package-bundle" --- # @deepseek-ai/dsh-headless English | [中文](README.zh.md) ## Summary `dsh-headless` runs one dsh task from the command line and prints the final answer, then exits — no GUI, no server, no browser. Type `dsh --profile headless "run the tests"` and the agent works through the task with the same model, tools, and safety defaults as every other surface. It is ideal for scripts, CI, and one-off jobs: the process opens no ports and leaves nothing running behind. The exit code tells you the outcome — 0 when the task completed, 1 when it aborted or errored. The main boundary: one task per invocation, with no interactive follow-up. ## Table of Contents - [Use this package](#use-this-package) - [Understand the implementation](#understand-the-implementation) - [Further Exploration](#further-exploration) - [Model Experience](#model-experience) - [Known Limitations and Deferred Work](#known-limitations-and-deferred-work) - [Dev Note](#dev-note) ----- ## Use this package Run one task, get the final answer, and exit. The task is the command line itself, so the whole invocation is the smallest working example. ### Running a one-shot task ```sh dsh --profile headless "run the tests" ``` The agent works through the task, streams each non-empty provider reasoning delta to stderr under a `dsh: reasoning:` heading, then prints the final answer on stdout and exits. Consecutive reasoning deltas stay in one section, and the runner closes that section before later output when the provider supplied no trailing newline. A successful run without reasoning keeps stderr empty; a failure exits 1 and prints `dsh: : ` to stderr. A missing or blank task is rejected before anything runs. The task text is supplied through the single `task` setting: | Field | Default | Meaning | |---|---|---| | `task` | required | The task text for the single run | The generated [configuration catalog](../../../docs/config-catalog.md#deepseek-aidsh-headless) is the exhaustive source for every accepted field and its JSDoc. ### When to use it Use headless for scripted or automated dsh runs — CI steps, batch jobs, quick answers from a terminal. Avoid it when you need a multi-turn interactive session or a GUI; the browser surface ([dsh-web-app](../web-app/README.md)) serves that. The process stays alive only for the run, opens no listening port, and exits on its own, so it fits pipelines that wait on the process. ### Help and task errors `dsh --profile headless --help` prints the command's help text and exits without running anything. A missing or whitespace-only task is a usage error: nothing runs and the process exits 1. ----- ## Understand the implementation
Implementation internals — click to expand The runner is a direct driver over the core API carrier: it creates one fresh Agent through the registry and folds the owned durable event interval into one process-level outcome. ### Run flow The runner awaits the complete application (`ctx.get('loader')?.await()`) so the composed tools and adapters are not half-mounted, reads the shared [`agentDefaultModel`](../../core/agent-default-model/README.md) selection, creates one fresh persisted Agent with that provider and model, and submits the task as an ordinary user message. It streams that Agent's non-empty reasoning deltas to stderr, waits for quiescence, then flushes the Session and folds the owned interval (`firstSeq` onward) into the last non-empty `assistant/message` text and final `turn/end` reason. It writes the final text to stdout and requests exit. ### Patch surface over base The patch rides over `dsh-base`: it inherits the projection cache, sets the coding persona prefix and separate cwd suffix on the base `system-prompt` row, keeps the same temporary process-wide PTC mode opt-in (`DSH_TOOLS_MODE`) as the Web surface, disables the shared HMR row, inserts PTC mode's worker as a core execution capability, and mounts the startup provider and the runner. The cache checkpoints each persisted one-shot session for later consumers; its durability barrier flushes each covered log prefix before publishing the cache row and may split otherwise coalesced JSONL runs. The startup provider ([`src/startup.ts`](src/startup.ts)) injects `ctx.cmdlineArgs` ([`dsh-cmdline`](../../boot/cmdline/README.md)), reads the positional argument, prints the app's `--help`, and provides `headlessStartup`; the runner injects that service and reads its task from lazy config. ### Exit mapping A completed final `turn/end` exits 0; any other outcome — aborted, error, or no turn in the owned interval — exits 1. An `error` reason also writes `dsh: : ` to stderr. A direct driver failure (for example, Agent creation) writes `dsh: ` to stderr and exits 1. ### Source map | File | Role | |---|---| | [`src/index.ts`](src/index.ts) | The `headless-runner` plugin: run flow, output contract, exit mapping | | [`src/startup.ts`](src/startup.ts) | The `headless-startup` provider: task positional and `--help` | | [`cordis.patch.yml`](cordis.patch.yml) | The one-shot patch over `dsh-base` | | — | No runtime invariant companion is published; the runner's observable contract (provider reasoning on stderr, final text on stdout, exit code by turn-end reason) is process-level and owned by the launcher e2e; it registers nothing and holds no mutable relation to audit inside the tree. | | [`tests/headless.spec.ts`](tests/headless.spec.ts) | Run flow, aggregation, flush, and exit mapping | | [`tests/startup.spec.ts`](tests/startup.spec.ts) | Command-line parsing over a real Loader tree | ### Invariant ownership No invariant companion is published because the runner's observable contract (final text on stdout, exit code by turn-end reason) is process-level and owned by the launcher e2e; the plugin registers nothing and holds no mutable relation to audit inside the tree.
----- ## Further Exploration Read these pages when you want to go deeper into the shared core, the sibling GUI, or the command-line handoff. - [Bundle package map](../README.md) — the surfaces built on the same core. - [dsh-base](../base/README.md) — the shared core headless runs on. - [dsh-web-app](../web-app/README.md) — the interactive browser sibling for multi-turn work. - [dsh-cmdline](../../boot/cmdline/README.md) — how the launcher hands the command line to the app. - [Generated configuration catalog](../../../docs/config-catalog.md#deepseek-aidsh-headless) — every accepted config field and its source declaration. ----- ## Model Experience None, as the runner submits the task as an ordinary user message and the composed base and headless rows own the prompts and tools. #### KV Cache effect The runner adds nothing to the request prefix; it only drives one user message through the composed tree. ## Known Limitations and Deferred Work These limits tell you when headless does not fit and what it needs from the `dsh` launcher. They are current package constraints, not a general CLI comparison or a task backlog. - **One task per run** — after the task is answered the process exits; there is no interactive follow-up, so split multi-step work into separate runs. - **Runs through the `dsh` launcher** — starting the headless profile another way fails at startup, because only the launcher can request the process exit. - **No pre-token heartbeat** — stderr stays silent until the provider emits a non-empty reasoning delta; a delayed first token exposes no earlier progress signal. - **Reasoning enters stderr logs** — redirection and supervisors may retain substantially more and potentially sensitive model output; route stderr to a controlled sink when needed. - **Only reasoning and the final answer are printed** — a run without an assistant message prints an empty stdout line and exits 1; intermediate tool output is not printed. ### Dev Note

--- description: "The npm-installable DeepSeek Harness Plus profile composition and explicit official-source materializer." kind: "package-bundle" --- # @sparkelf/dsh-plus English | [中文](README.zh.md) ## Summary This distribution composes official `@deepseek-ai/dsh-base` and `@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app` with selected Office, MinerU, mobile, market, GenUI, and Supervisor packages, four in-repository Plus capability packages, and twelve independent patch packages. It owns only ordered composition, minimum compatibility metadata, dependency closure, explicit materialization, and the credential-free deployment lock; capability behavior and patch payloads stay in their owning packages. ## Table of Contents - [Use this package](#use-this-package) - [Model Experience](#model-experience) - [Known Limitations and Deferred Work](#known-limitations-and-deferred-work) - [Dev Note](#dev-note) ----- ## Use this package Install and materialize Plus without Desktop or the tray: ```bash dsh plugin --profile plus add @sparkelf/dsh-plus dsh plugin --profile plus exec dsh-plus apply --dsh-root /path/to/official-dsh dsh --profile plus ``` The explicit rc24 apply step requires official revision `fb2c4b9e698e30edb738bca4cf0618587db7d203`, applies every pending source payload, configures exact npm patches, removes retired Plus-owned entries, and writes `.dsh-plus/patchset.lock.json` with mode `0600`. Patched official source workspaces always replace clean CLI packages in the profile scope. The profile resolves SQL Workbench 0.5.0, Workbench Vault 0.1.1, SSH Manager 0.7.0, API Client 0.5.0, Supervisor 0.1.4, GenUI 0.9.9, dshmarket 1.45.1, OfficeCLI 0.1.1, MinerU 0.1.1, and Mobile Bridge 0.2.11 from npm. Version conflicts, source mismatches, missing bundles, and runtime closure drift stop promotion. Official DSH supplies Sidebar navigation, file and text preview, Session search, generic file upload, durable attachment cards, read-only model paths, onboarding, Workspace selection, Session export, and Turn folding. Plus configures the official SQLite Session query provider to open on first search with a durable derived index at `$DSH_HOME/storages/session-query.sqlite`; canonical compressed JSONL remains the history source. Plus adds an OfficeCLI tool for original DOCX/XLSX/PPTX production and a MinerU PDF tool that consumes the official uploaded-file path without a prompt hook. It replaces mixed English `Session` wording in the Simplified-Chinese export UI, places the desktop Session-log action immediately before Trajectory search while retaining its Header position on phones, and keeps composer permission and model popovers inside the center column with 12px horizontal clearance. `@changfenhuang/dsh-genui@0.9.9` now contains the previously patched streaming EChart behavior. The registry-pinned Supervisor manages the materialized runtime and restores Sessions interrupted by its own restart. DataOps and MinerU mount only when their endpoint environment variables exist. Agent Teams remains excluded because official shipped profiles disable those private experimental packages. Plus explicitly selects `browserAuthentication: disabled`: its Web URL is clean and opens without a process-token exchange or browser cookie, while Connection still applies the official Host/Origin trust fence. Every process that can reach an accepted authority can therefore use the complete Host API, including Shell, files, and Sessions. The official `web` profile keeps the upstream `required` default; only the Plus composition opts out. ----- ## Model Experience ### Profile composition #### What the model sees Nothing directly. `@sparkelf/dsh-plus` registers no tool, prompt section, model-facing Session event, or provider content; each selected capability owns its own model-visible behavior. #### Token effect Zero by itself. Token use comes only from the capability and official packages selected by the profile. #### KV Cache effect Independent by itself. The profile changes a request prefix only when one of its selected packages contributes or removes model-visible content. ## Known Limitations and Deferred Work - **Exact source target**: source payloads apply only to the recorded official revision; another source tree fails loudly, and the distribution provides no accepted-fork or fuzzy-apply fallback. ### Dev Note
Working context for maintainers, click to expand This Dev Note is working context for maintainers; shipped behavior, limits, and rationale live in the sections above, the package code, and the linked Agent Note. - The [distribution Agent Note](../../../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-08-29-ranged-plus-patchset-distribution.md) owns package forms, inventory, materialization, and deletion rules; `src/apply.ts` and `cordis.patch.yml` own the executable profile behavior. - No runtime invariant companion is published because profile and patchset validity is checked before materialization and the bundle owns no independent runtime observation.
# DeepSeek Harness English | [中文](README.zh.md) DeepSeek Harness (`dsh`) is an open-source agent harness developed by [DeepSeek AI](https://deepseek.com). It is built on an **everything-is-a-plugin** architecture and powered by [Cordis](https://github.com/cordiverse/cordis), whose design is described in [_A Programming Paradigm for Spatiotemporal Composability_](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25512). Documentation: [https://deepseek-harness.github.io/deepseek-harness/](https://deepseek-harness.github.io/deepseek-harness/) ## Developer preview DeepSeek Harness is in _developer preview_ and iterating rapidly. **THERE WILL BE COMPATIBILITY-BREAKING CHANGES.** Review the [safety notice](SAFETY.md) before running the project. ## Run ### Run from `npm` Install `Node.js`, then run: ```sh npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web ``` The command starts the Web UI at `http://127.0.0.1:3080` by default and opens it in the default browser for a local launch. An SSH launch only prints the host URL because the SSH client or editor owns the local forwarded address. Pass `--no-open` to run the server without opening a browser. For agents, follow [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md). ## License [MIT](LICENSE) Third-party dependencies and their licenses are disclosed in [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).

--- description: "SDK stdio application profile for users and maintainers launching a JSON-RPC harness runtime." kind: "package-bundle" --- # `@deepseek-ai/dsh-sdk-app` English | [中文](README.zh.md) ## Summary The SDK stdio application as a `dsh` profile bundle over [`dsh-base`](../base/README.md). SDK protocol `shutdown`, SIGINT, and SIGTERM retain their owning server or launcher paths; disposal drains the root profile tree and persistence. Stdout is reserved for newline-delimited JSON-RPC frames. The bundle disables model-generated session titles because the SDK exposes no title surface; deterministic fallback titles remain durable without an auxiliary model request. The inherited projection cache checkpoints SDK-created sessions for later consumers; its durability barrier flushes each covered log prefix before publishing the cache row and may split otherwise coalesced JSONL runs. Provider/model and workspace cwd arrive through the SDK initialization request; the base profile owns adapters, tools, persistence, policy, settings, and credentials. The SDK uses the base `read`, `write`, and `edit` defaults. To add `str_replace_editor`, use the explicit insertion patch in the [base configuration guide](../base/README.md#use-this-package). --- description: "Standalone single-tool SDK profile for users who need a minimal cross-platform coding agent without the shared base bundle." kind: "package-bundle" --- # `@deepseek-ai/dsh-sdk-minimal` English | [中文](README.zh.md) ## Summary Use `dsh --profile sdk-minimal` when an SDK client needs a small, explicit coding-agent runtime. The profile advertises only a platform-selected persistent shell, persists sessions as uncompressed JSONL, and selects the model from the SDK initialization request. It supplies a complete Cordis tree and deliberately excludes `dsh-base`, Web, settings, managed credentials, telemetry, compaction, filesystem tools, workspace instructions, skills, jobs, and subagents. Its danger-full-access policy lets the shell modify any path available to the process, so use it only with an isolated workspace. ## Table of Contents - [Use this package](#use-this-package) - [Understand the implementation](#understand-the-implementation) - [Further Exploration](#further-exploration) - [Model Experience](#model-experience) - [Known Limitations and Deferred Work](#known-limitations-and-deferred-work) - [Dev Note](#dev-note) ----- ## Use this package Launch the profile directly or select it from the Python SDK. Supply an explicit `DSH_HOME`, use a disposable workspace, and provide the model credential through `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`. ```sh export DSH_HOME=/absolute/path/to/example-dsh-home dsh --profile sdk-minimal ``` `DSH_CONTEXT_WINDOW` sets the fallback capacity for a model absent from the adapter's advisory catalog. `DSH_SYSTEM_PROMPT` replaces the default persona. The SDK initialization request is the sole model selection and overrides environment defaults. Use `dsh plugin --profile sdk-minimal` to manage persistent external dependencies. Profile, home, and ordered `--patch` files can replace rows or insert bundles above the complete default tree. The shipped template applies patches only at startup. The profile mounts exactly one persistent shell stack: Bash on Linux and macOS, or PowerShell on Windows. Both stacks use a 300-second timeout and one owner-scoped terminal; the other platform's rows remain disabled. ----- ## Understand the implementation
Implementation internals — click to expand The bundle's single insert is the complete application tree: SDK stdio startup and JSON-RPC serving, one environment-configured DeepSeek adapter, the explicit agent core, local subprocess execution, a platform-selected persistent shell PTY, and uncompressed JSONL persistence under `$DSH_HOME/sessions`. It does not inherit another bundle, so every extra row is an explicit profile change. ### Source map | File | Role | |---|---| | [`cordis.patch.yml`](cordis.patch.yml) | Complete standalone profile tree and its environment-backed defaults | | [`src/index.ts`](src/index.ts) | Bundle package entry | | — | No runtime invariant companion is published; the package is a static patch-list carrier whose inserted rows own their runtime relationships and invariant companions. | | [`tests/sdk-minimal.spec.ts`](tests/sdk-minimal.spec.ts) | Exact composition, profile-name, and platform-selection checks |
----- ## Further Exploration - [Python SDK example](../../../python/sdk/examples/README.md) — launches this profile from Python against an explicit Harness home. - [SDK application bundle](../sdk-app/README.md) — the JSON-RPC application layer reused by full and minimal SDK profiles. - [Base bundle](../base/README.md) — the full product foundation that this profile deliberately omits. ----- ## Model Experience ### Minimal coding-agent composition #### What the model sees The system prompt is `DSH_SYSTEM_PROMPT` or `You are a helpful software engineer assistant.`. The only advertised tool is owner-scoped persistent `bash` on Linux/macOS or `pwsh` on Windows; runtime context, filesystem tools, workspace instructions, skills, jobs controls, compaction, and Harness identity are absent. #### Token effect One stable persona plus one tool schema. Tool results and ordinary conversation history grow with the session. #### KV Cache effect Stable for a fixed persona, platform, provider, model, and bundle patch stack. Profile changes take effect on the next process. ## Known Limitations and Deferred Work - **The composition intentionally omits shared product services** — select `dsh --profile sdk` when settings, managed credentials, policy presets, telemetry, Web tools, or the full default tool roster are required. - **User patches can expand the tree and corrupt stdout** — profile customization is trusted application composition; a plugin that writes ordinary text to stdout can break JSON-RPC framing. ### Dev Note
Working context for maintainers — click to expand None.

--- description: "The browser GUI for dsh: interactive chat, model and settings management, and session history, for users running the dsh web surface." kind: "package-bundle" --- # @deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app English | [中文](README.zh.md) ## Summary Run `dsh --profile web` to open an interactive browser GUI with chat, model and settings management, and session history. It uses the same model access, tools, and safety defaults as other dsh surfaces. Startup prints an authenticated URL and normally opens it in the default browser; SSH sessions and `--no-open` leave the URL for manual opening. You can change the port and allow extra hosts, but cannot bind all network interfaces. Choose this package for interactive browser work; use `dsh-headless` for one-shot command-line tasks. ## Table of Contents - [Use this package](#use-this-package) - [Understand the implementation](#understand-the-implementation) - [Further Exploration](#further-exploration) - [Model Experience](#model-experience) - [Known Limitations and Deferred Work](#known-limitations-and-deferred-work) - [Dev Note](#dev-note) ----- ## Use this package Start the GUI, open your browser, and start talking to the agent. The flags fine-tune the invocation. ### Starting the Web GUI ```sh dsh --profile web dsh --profile web --no-open --port 8080 ``` After startup you see a `dsh web:` line whose root URL carries a fresh process token. Unless `--no-open` or an SSH session suppresses it, the default browser opens that URL, receives a signed cookie, and redirects to the clean root page. You know it worked when the page loads and you can chat with the agent. Two failures to expect: if the frontend is not built, startup stops with a build hint (`pnpm run build` in a checkout); if the browser cannot be opened, a credential-free diagnostic prints to stderr while the server keeps running — open the printed startup URL yourself. ### Configuration Most users never set these; the command-line flags feed the four settings below — `--host`, `--port`, and `--trusted-host` come from the invocation, and `--no-open` turns the browser handoff off for that invocation: | Field | Default | Meaning | |---|---|---| | `openBrowser` | `true` | Open the default browser after startup; SSH launches suppress it | | `printUrl` | `true` | Print the `dsh web:` URL line at startup | | `surfaceContext` | `true` | Give the agent GUI-orientation context and expose `DSH_WEB_URL` to its shell commands | | `trustedHosts` | `[]` | Extra hosts allowed to reach the GUI from the network | The generated [configuration catalog](../../../docs/config-catalog.md#deepseek-aidsh-web-app) is the exhaustive source for every accepted field and its JSDoc. ### LAN access and trusted hosts By default the GUI accepts connections from this machine only. A deployment that binds all network interfaces also allows browsers from the LAN, and the printed URL then includes a LAN address; `--trusted-host` adds extra hosts in either case. Host and Origin checks control reachability, while the token exchange authenticates every Host API method and WebSocket stream. The LAN addresses are sampled once at startup, so a network change later is not picked up — restart the GUI to re-advertise. ### Running over SSH When you launch `dsh --profile web` over SSH, the URL line still prints but the browser is not opened for you: the SSH client or editor owns the local forwarding address. Open the forwarded URL on your machine yourself; the printed URL names the remote host's loopback endpoint. ### Per-session agent setup Each browser session composes its own agent from the shipped presets (the `standard` preset by default), instead of sharing one process-wide tool set. You can change the default preset or add your own presets under `$DSH_HOME/.agent-presets`. ----- ## Understand the implementation
Implementation internals — click to expand The bundle is one patch plus one runtime glue plugin. The storage stack and projection cache come from `dsh-base`; the web overlay's workspace and message-feedback rows consume that shared `storageDomain` service. The patch restates the surface-specific values the base deliberately omits, inserts the web-only host rows and browser roster, then moves the agent plane behind presets. The glue plugin owns dist serving, trust sampling, prompt sections, the bash variable, and the readiness announcements. ### Patch semantics A patch replaces the targeted row's whole `config`, so each web row restates every key it owns: the persona prefix and suffix templates, the `DSH_TOOLS_MODE` PTC mode opt-in, and the `session-query-sqlite` values on the base rows, then `insert` adds the web host rows, transport, and browser roster. The per-agent tool rows the base mounts process-wide are disabled here and the preset roster takes over; the reasoning for each host-plane versus preset-plane decision is inline in the patch. ### Readiness The URL line and browser handoff are readiness signals: supervisors RPC as soon as they observe the line, and a browser requests the page as soon as it opens, so both run only after the Loader tree settles and Connection authentication is available — or immediately in a hand-built tree without a Loader. A tree disposed mid-boot announces nothing. ### LAN trust sampling `resolveLanTrust` samples the network once at boot: a loopback bind (`127.0.0.1`) derives no LAN addresses, while an all-interfaces bind adds every non-internal IPv4 literal. The derived literals plus the explicit `--trusted-host` authorities form the `/api` browser-trust fence, and the printed LAN URL always matches that fence. ### Source map | File | Role | |---|---| | [`src/index.ts`](src/index.ts) | The `web-app` glue plugin: dist resolution, LAN trust sampling, prompt sections, bash variable, URL line, browser handoff | | [`src/startup.ts`](src/startup.ts) | The `web-startup` provider: `--host`, `--port`, `--trusted-host`, `--no-open`, `--help` | | [`cordis.patch.yml`](cordis.patch.yml) | The web patch: restated base values, web host rows, browser roster, agent plane behind presets | | — | No runtime invariant companion is published; every contribution (frontend-static child plugin, prompt section, bashEnv registration) is registry-disposed with the fiber, and each owning registry's package carries that relation's invariant; the package holds no mutable state of its own to audit. | | [`tests/web-app.spec.ts`](tests/web-app.spec.ts) | Dist resolution, fallback seat, prompt sections, readiness | | [`tests/startup.spec.ts`](tests/startup.spec.ts) | Command-line parsing over a real Loader tree | | [`tests/trusted-hosts.spec.ts`](tests/trusted-hosts.spec.ts) | LAN-trust sampling | | [`tests/browser-open.spec.ts`](tests/browser-open.spec.ts) | Default-browser handoff after the page is reachable | ### Invariant ownership No invariant companion is published because every contribution — the frontend-static child plugin, the prompt sections, and the bash variable registration — is registry-disposed with the fiber, and each owning registry package carries that relation's invariant.
----- ## Further Exploration Read these pages when you want to go deeper into the shared core, the browser reload pipeline, or the built frontend. - [Bundle package map](../README.md) — the surfaces built on the same core. - [dsh-base](../base/README.md) — the shared core the GUI runs on. - [dsh-client-hmr](../../client/hmr/README.md) — how client-plugin changes reload during development. - [frontend-static](../../host/frontend-static/README.md) — how the built frontend is served. - [Generated configuration catalog](../../../docs/config-catalog.md#deepseek-aidsh-web-app) — every accepted config field and its source declaration. ----- ## Model Experience ### Harness-source and Web-surface context #### What the model sees When `surfaceContext` is true, the `harness:source` section identifies the on-disk Harness implementation without claiming it is the working directory, and the `app:web-surface` global section (first-party order 10100, after reusable instructions) orients the model to the GUI: the canonical local URL, the "this page" referent, the update contract (the reload receiver is always on; no-refresh reloads additionally need the `pnpm run dev:web` watcher), and the instruction not to start replacement servers. `DSH_WEB_URL` additionally appears in the managed bash environment with its description, resolved per invocation from the live server. When it is false, neither section nor the variable is registered. #### Token effect One source line and one prompt paragraph per session plus two managed-environment variable lines; constant per process. #### KV Cache effect Source and Web sections follow first-party reusable instructions. Different checkout paths or local ports leave that preceding prefix unchanged when tools and configuration match; provider cache reuse is not guaranteed. ## Known Limitations and Deferred Work These limits tell you what to expect in unusual setups — a source checkout, SSH sessions, or strict networks. They are current package constraints, not a general browser comparison or a task backlog. - **The frontend must be built** — a source checkout needs `pnpm run build` first; startup stops with a build hint when the dist is missing, and there is no source-serving fallback. - **LAN addresses are sampled once at startup** — interface changes after boot are not re-advertised; the printed LAN URL always matches what was sampled. - **Only the handoff start is observable** — the GUI reports that the browser was asked to open, not that it actually opened; a later browser exit is never reported, and the printed URL is your manual fallback. - **SSH sessions keep the URL but skip the browser handoff** — the printed URL names the remote host's loopback endpoint; the SSH client or editor must expose and open the local forwarded address. - **`BROWSER` overrides only come from the environment** — a discovered `.env` cannot set `BROWSER`; only an inherited value can choose the executable for the automatic handoff. - **Binding all network interfaces is not supported** — `--host 0.0.0.0` is rejected at startup for safety; use the default loopback host. ### Dev Note

# DeepSeek Harness English | [中文](README.zh.md) DeepSeek Harness (`dsh`) is an open-source agent harness developed by [DeepSeek AI](https://deepseek.com). It is built on an **everything-is-a-plugin** architecture and powered by [Cordis](https://github.com/cordiverse/cordis), whose design is described in [_A Programming Paradigm for Spatiotemporal Composability_](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25512). Documentation: [https://deepseek-harness.github.io/deepseek-harness/](https://deepseek-harness.github.io/deepseek-harness/) ## Developer preview DeepSeek Harness is in _developer preview_ and iterating rapidly. **THERE WILL BE COMPATIBILITY-BREAKING CHANGES.** Review the [safety notice](SAFETY.md) before running the project. ## Run ### Run from `npm` Install `Node.js`, then run: ```sh npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web ``` The command starts the Web UI at `http://127.0.0.1:3080` by default and opens it in the default browser for a local launch. An SSH launch only prints the host URL because the SSH client or editor owns the local forwarded address. Pass `--no-open` to run the server without opening a browser. See [Web UI guide](docs/user/guide/index.md). ### Run from source To run from a repository checkout: ```sh git clone https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness.git cd deepseek-harness pnpm install pnpm run build pnpm dsh web ``` `pnpm run build` prepares the repository artifacts. `pnpm dsh web` uses those built artifacts without rebuilding. ## Community and support - Submit feedback or bug reports through [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions). - Add the [`dsh-plugin`](https://github.com/topics/dsh-plugin) topic to your plugin repository for discoverability. - Join DeepSeek Harness Discord community. ## Contributing See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). ## Development Start with the [development guide](docs/development.md) and [architecture documentation](docs/architecture.md). For agents, follow [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md). ## License [MIT](LICENSE) Third-party dependencies and their licenses are disclosed in [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).

evidence.readmeExcerpt: # 寰镜股票看板 MarketLens（@suifei/dsh-market-lens） A股 / 港股 / 美股的**只读**看盘·盯盘股票看板 DSH Web 插件——Web 面板形态覆盖 PC 与移动端的延迟股市行情，摸鱼友好，**不接任何交易端能力**。 - 数据性质：公开免费接口的**延迟行情**，非 Level-2，UI 常驻标注。 - 市场：A 股（沪/深/北）、港股、美股；指数、个股（板块视图在后续版本）。 - 不做：下单、撤单、持仓盈亏、量化执行、任何写操作（连配置写回都没有）。 ## 截图 | 三列首页 · 暗色 | 证券大厅（灯阵总屏 · 紧凑档） | 三列首页 · 亮色 | |---|---|---| | | | | 首页 = 指数条 / 自选列表（代码主视觉 + 微型趋势线 + 涨跌胶囊 + 市场状态条）/ K 线（MA、量副图、框选放大）/ 详情卡 + 提醒 + 财报 + 资讯四段右栏。大厅 = UCDOS 血统点阵字库驱动的交易所总屏，**灯珠 3×3 像素、灯距 3.5 像素（0.5 像素灯缝）**，格点（灯珠阵）是布局本体、分辨率 = 格数 × 灯距，版式随格数在**完整五区 / 紧凑版式**两态间取档（现场图见 `docs/`，命名 `marketlens-<日期时间>-<场景>.png`）。 ## 架构 ``` 浏览器（DSH Web GUI） Node（DSH Host） ┌─────────────────────────┐ 同源 HTTP ┌──────────────────────────┐ │ client.js React 面板 │ ───────────→ │ index.js │ │ · sidebar.panellist 图标 │ /market-lens│ · /market-lens/* routes │ │ · main keyed 主面板 │ /* │ · market_search/quotes/ │ │ · Canvas 自绘 K 线（零 CDN）│ │ kline 三个只读工具 │ │ · localStorage 自选/偏好 │ │ lib/service.js │ └─────────────────────────┘ │ 归一化 · TTL 缓存 · 在途去重 │ UI 永不直连外部行情接口 │ 多源降级（按市场分链） │ │ sources/{eastmoney, │ │ tencent,yahoo}.js │ └──────────────────────────┘ ``` **行情抓取只发生在宿主侧。** UI 与模型工具共用同一个 `createMarketService`，一个操作、两个调用方。 ## 符号规范 内部规范格式（与腾讯公开接口词表一致）： | 市场 | 规范 | 接受输入 | |---|---|---| | 沪/深/北 | `sh600519` `sz000001` `bj830799` | `600519`、`SH600519`、`sh.600519`（裸 6 位按代码段推断：`5/6/9`→sh，`0/3/1`→sz，`4/8`→bj） | | 港股 | `hk00700`（5 位）、指数别名 `hkHSI` `hkHSTECH` | `700`、`00700`、`HK00700` | | 美股 | `usAAPL`、指数别名 `usDJI` `usIXIC` `usINX` | `AAPL`、`us.aapl`、`US.AAPL` | 搜索支持代码、中文名、拼音全拼与**拼音首字母**（`gzmt` → 贵州茅台）：拼音匹配委托给上游 suggest 接口（smartbox / 东方财富），宿主侧只做归一化、合并与去重。 ## 多源降级 | 市场 | 主源 | 备源 | |---|---|---| | A 股（含北交所）/ 指数 | 东方财富 | 腾讯 | | 港股 | 东方财富 | 腾讯 | | 美股 / 美指数 | Yahoo chart | 腾讯（美股 K 线自动解析 `.OQ/.N` 后缀码） | - 东方财富 TLS 在部分网络被重置：适配器带 **https 失败→http 重试**（仅公开只读 GET）。 - 单源失败自动切换；全链失败时 quotes 返回 `failed[]`（UI 显示「数据暂不可用」），有缓存旧值时以 `stale: true` 供出延迟值而非假数据。 ## 面板接口（同源，宿主实现） | Route | 参数 | 返回 | |---|---|---| | `GET /market-lens/meta` | — | `{ pollIntervalMs, defaultWatchlist, indexBar, limits, disclaimer }` | | `GET /market-lens/quotes` | `symbols`（逗号分隔，≤200） | `{ quotes: QuoteRow[], failed: [{symbol, reason}] }` | | `GET /market-lens/kline` | `symbol, period=day|week|month, count=20–320` | `{ symbol, period, adjust, bars: Bar[], source }` | | `GET /market-lens/search` | `q`（1–50）, `limit≤30` | `{ items: [{symbol, name, market, kind}] }` | | `GET /market-lens/news` | `q?`（关键词，可空）, `limit≤30` | `{ items: [{title, url, time, source}], source }` | | `GET /market-lens/posts` | `symbol`（必填）, `name?`（新闻关键词） | `{ symbol, notice[], posts[{title,url,time,comments,reads}], news[], source }` — 公告(A股)/股吧评论(A·港)/个股新闻三源并行，单源失败置空，全空 502 | | `GET /market-lens/updates` | `symbols`（逗号列表） | `{ items: [{symbol, notice[], latest, count, unsupported?}] }` — 自选行的**未读公告气泡**数据源（仅公告源，轻量批查） | | `GET /market-lens/financials` | `symbol` | A 股：`{ rows: [{report, revenue, revenueYoY, netProfit, netProfitYoY, eps, bps}] }`；港/美：`{ unsupported: true }` | | `GET /market-lens/alerts` | `since`（事件游标） | `{ alerts, events, cursor }`；`POST` 新建规则或 `{action:'dismiss'}` 清未读；`DELETE ?id=` 删规则 | `QuoteRow = { symbol, name, price, prevClose, open, high, low, change, changePct, volume(股), amount(元), turnoverRate, pe, volRatio, amplitude, pb, marketCap, floatMarketCap, currency?, updatedAt, source, stale? }`。字段可得性因市场与源而异：**缺失为 `null`，UI 显示 `—`，绝不补 0**。K 线前复权固定在宿主侧，UI 与工具都不暴露复权参数。 路由带同源护栏：`Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site` 或 Origin/Referer 与 Host 不一致一律 403；全部 `cache-control: no-store`。 ## 模型工具（只读） | 工具 | 参数 | 说明 | |---|---|---| | `market_search` | `query(1–50)`, `limit?≤30` | 代码/名称/拼音检索 | | `market_quotes` | `symbols: string[]`（≤200） | 批量报价，含 `source` 与 `stale` 标注 | | `market_kline` | `symbol`, `period: day|week|month`, `count: 20–320` | 前复权 K 线 | 工具描述内写明「只读行情、不涉及交易」；上限同时写在参数描述与宿主校验（越界报 `BAD_INPUT`）。没有 `market_order` 之类的写工具。 ## 可靠性实现点 - 轮询：`setTimeout` 链式调度，上一次完成后才排下一次；`document.hidden` 暂停，回前台立即刷新（面板卸载即整链拆除）。 - 收回：样式、监听、AbortController、定时器全部挂在 `ctx.effect` / 组件 cleanup。 - 指数条与自选行按 key 原地更新文本，不重建列表 DOM，滚动位置与手动顺序不被轮询重置。 - K 线：Canvas 自绘；PC 滚轮缩放 + 拖拽平移 + hover tooltip；移动端双指缩放、单指平移、长按出 tooltip（不依赖 hover）。 - 搜索带序号防竞态，慢的旧响应不覆盖新输入。 ## 配置（`cordis.patch.yml` 行内 `config`） `pollIntervalMs 5000 · quoteTtlMs 5000 · klineTtlMs 60000 · searchTtlMs 300000 · newsTtlMs 60000 · finTtlMs 21600000 · upstreamTimeoutMs 6000 · maxQuoteSymbols ≤200 · maxKlineCount ≤320 · routePath /market-lens · diagLevel errors` ## 诊断日志（自监控闭环，**全局开关**） **`diagLevel` 是日志总开关**：`off` 完全静音（不落盘、客户端连 POST 都不发）；`errors`（**发布默认**）只保留崩溃/失败行（`panel.crash`、`*.fail`、`route.status`、`route.reject`），日常事件零写盘；`full` 记录一切——开发调试期用。仓库自带的 `cordis.patch.yml` 行内写了 `config: { diagLevel: full }`（开发机现状），**发布前删掉或改回 `errors`** 即可回到静音默认；普通使用者不配置天然是 `errors`。 面板把关键事件（挂载、每类请求成败、渲染崩溃）批量 POST 到 `/market-lens/diag`，宿主连同护栏拒绝与非常规状态码一起写入 JSONL 日志（客户端与服务端各有一道同级过滤，`full` 之外不产生流水）： - 位置：`~/.dsh/market-lens/marketlens-diag-.jsonl`（`diagLogDir` / `diagLogMaxBytes` 可在插件配置改，按天分文件、超限轮转为 `.1`）。 - 回读：`GET /market-lens/diag?tail=50` 返回 `{file, rows}`；面板红条本身也带原因。 ## 自选行（对齐 Apple「股市」层级） 每行 = **代码大字主视觉 + 灰色名称** + **22 日微型趋势线**（SVG，面积渐变 + 端点强调，红涨绿跌跟随当前配色系；悬停显示 5 日累计涨幅）+ 右侧现价粗体（方向色）与**红/绿实底白字涨跌胶囊**（副行小字涨幅%与成交额）。选中行以 inset 圆环描边浮出；行距靠留白分层，不铺卡框，**一句话建议**（强势拉升/稳步走高/窄幅盘整/快速下降/加速下挫）作为名称下第三行方向着色小字。列表底部常驻**市场状态条**：集合竞价 / 交易中 / 午间休市 / 已收盘 + 日期（按北京时间 A 股时段，30s 自刷新）。趋势线宿主侧走 K 线缓存（5 分钟窗口），过滤、排序、置顶切换均不重复请求。筛选与周期按钮为**灰底分段胶囊**（选中提亮加粗、无描边）；资讯标题粗体，时间用**相对显示**（当日钟点，更早 "N周前"）。 ## K 线交互与配色 拖拽框选放大 · 滚轮以光标为锚缩放 · **右键拖动平移时间轴** · 双击回全览；**点击 K 线**在图下方展开当日详情条（开高低收、涨跌、涨幅、振幅、量），再点一次取消。悬停十字光标带主题化价签/日期签与左上角 OHLC/MA 图例；最新价虚线 + 轴上价签常驻。 配色五系可切换（工具栏「配色」）：红涨绿跌（**空心阳线**，默认）、绿涨红跌、蓝涨橙跌、紫涨金跌、青涨玫跌；选择持久化在 `ml.prefs.v1`，全部颜色走 CSS 变量并跟随宿主明暗主题。 ## 横向滚动规范 界面默认不出现横向滚动条。确需横向内容的区域（指数条、财报横表）统一用 `HScroll`：滚动条**悬停/聚焦才现身**（细圆角、跟随主题），两侧**渐隐边缘**提示还有内容（可滚状态实时更新），触屏 `pan-x` 原生拖动、`overscroll-behavior` 防串滚，`tabIndex` 支持键盘横滚。纵向滚动条全局统一为透明轨道 + 悬停显色的细圆角样式。 ## 看盘模式（0.7） - **三列分割条**：列表/K线/详情两缝可拖（260–460 / 280–560 px 限位），宽度写入 `ml.prefs.v1.cols`，窄模式隐藏分割条。 - **证券大厅**（标题右侧的金色按钮，点阵图标 + 悬停像素提示条）：**真·灯矩阵屏**——**灯距 3.5px（灯珠 3×3 像素、灯缝 0.5px）**，文字不走字体渲染，用 **UCDOS 血统的点阵字库**（HZK16 汉字 16×16 + ASC16 半角 8×16，8178 字，388KB，`/market-lens/lampfont` 供给，`assets/lamp.bin` 随包）：**一个字模点 = 一颗灯珠**，零抗锯齿零模糊。工具栏可切**两档点阵**：标准 16×16 / 紧凑 8×8（2×2 OR 折叠），并有**灯珠倍率弹出菜单**：1/4×、1/3×、1/2×、1×、2×、3×、4× 七档直选（放大档整格等比放大，4× 灯珠 12×12px，按容器宽度自动封顶——4× 需 ≥3080px 视口否则降档；缩小档灯珠下限 1px、灯距下限 1px，格数暴涨退细点总屏），高倍档墙格数变少时逐档减列（≥960 格五区 → ≥440 格四列 → ≥353 格三列 → 更窄两列，隐代码并缩短页脚）。内容画进离屏内存页（点阵直写）采样成**带间缝的圆形灯珠**网格，additive 柔光晕两遍烘焙；**版式照交易所总屏五区**：**标题+时钟条**（琥珀色，HH:MM 实时）/ **左指数面板**（指数名+最新/最高/最低/涨幅 2×2 数值群+近 60 日金色走势缎带+首末日期轴）/ **中行情主表**（红列头：名称 代码 前收 最高 最低 现价 涨幅 成交额，整行按涨跌着色，轮播行蓝带+金色箭头）/ **右双子屏**（涨幅榜压着跌幅榜）/ **底部汇总条**（支数/涨/跌/平+总成交额）；轮播高亮行下方展开灯格 K 线带。布局为**格点本体**：墙几何按灯珠格数计数（`格数 = floor(容器/灯距)`，分辨率是格数×灯距的乘积，1:1 逐灯铺满、不重采样、右缘死区小于一个灯距），列距基准 960 格（= 1920 屏 @2px 经典格）——**≥960 格（容器 ≥3360px）出五区全屏总屏**，窄于它自动退**紧凑版式**（名称/代码/现价/涨幅/成交额核心列，≥440 格的紧凑墙再加回前收盘列 + 指数并入院行，点阵字尺寸不随墙缩放，等比压缩列距必撞字故减列而非缩字）；标准档列距按半角字宽一次排定（7 位价格 + 六档数值列全部右对齐钉轨，相邻列 ≥12 设计像素气口），**永不裁剪**；canvas 与 CSS 像素 1:1，不叠 devicePixelRatio，浏览器零重采样故灯珠不闪烁，**行数不足时行距自动等化顶满屏幕**（游戏 fit 式）——窗口小是画面整体缩小，不是重算；大厅高度定死视口减头部（不靠内容撑高），空余边框也是灭灯灯珠，缩放瞬间不闪白。主循环 **~9fps** 双 blit（背景层+场景层各预烘一次）+ 扫描带 + 随机灯珠明暗抖；4 秒一行、整页轮完**逐灯熄灭/点亮清屏翻页**；K 线批量预取翻页零请求；悬停停屏锁行，点行只选中该股（**停留大屏不跳转**）；退出大厅用标题右侧金色按钮。ArkPixel webfont 仍服务 DOM 侧，灯墙与它无关。 - **个股资讯区**：原"快讯"卡升级为三 Tab——**快讯**（全市场）/**公告**（东财公告，A 股）/**评论**（股吧热帖，A·港股，带回复数），公告与评论跟随当前选中股票，走 `/market-lens/posts` 聚合路由（三源并行、单源失败置空）。 - **当日详情条增强**：点选 K 线后除 OHLC/额量外附**信号标签**——20 根内新高/新低、放量倍数（×n），全部由已在手的 K 线数据本地计算，不加请求。 ## 价格提醒（宿主后台评估） 规则存于 `~/.dsh/market-lens/alerts.json`，**评估循环跑在宿主**——面板不开、网页不在前台，提醒照常触发。七类规则：`priceUp/priceDown`（价格≥/≤）、`pctUp/pctDown`（当日涨/跌幅≥）、`maUp/maDown`（上穿/下破 MA5/10/20/60，需拉日线，隔轮评估）、`volSpike`（量比≥，东财源提供）。触发产生事件流（保留 200 条），每条规则带独立**静默期**（默认 30 分钟）防轰炸。 展示：桌面壳底部 `shell.bottom` 状态条——🔔 摇铃动效 + 多行**向上跑马灯**（3 秒一行，涨跌红绿着色），**悬停即停**，点击行跳到行情面板并把该提醒对应的股票选为当前标的，「清除」把当前所有事件标为已读。 - 排障顺序：先看有没有 `route.reject`（护栏误伤）→ `route.status`（路径/参数错）→ `panel.*.fail`（上游源问题）→ `panel.crash`（渲染问题）。 ## 数据内容 - **预制自选**：首次打开即有 12 只中外明星股（茅台/宁德/比亚迪/招行/平安/腾讯/阿里/美团/苹果/微软/英伟达/特斯拉）+ 顶部 10 指数条。 - **财经快讯**：新浪财经滚动（支持按标的名称过滤）为主，东财 7×24 备源；60s TTL。 - **财报**：东财 F10 主要财务指标（营收/净利/EPS/BPS + 同比），A 股已支持，港/美股显式标注暂不支持。 ## 开发 ```bash node --test # 离线单测（fetch 全桩） node scripts/live-probe.mjs # 真网络冒烟（不在测试里跑，避免 CI 依赖外网） ``` 大厅版式改动必须先跑**离线自检链**（布局唯一事实源是 `client.js` 的纯函数 `ledPlan`，浏览器绘制器与本链共用）： ```bash node scripts/led-shot.mjs # 411/548/685/960 格（容器 1440/1920/2400/3360）mock 行情 → shots/plan-*.json python scripts/led-shot.py # lamp.bin 真点阵重绘 → shots/shot-*.png + 撞字审计 ``` 审计 0 碰撞才允许提交；`shots/` 为临时产物不入库。 ## 发布自检（社区市场流程） 1. 仓库 `github.com/suifei/dsh-market-lens`，public；本目录即包根（`package.json` 声明 `dsh.bundle.patch` → `./cordis.patch.yml`）。 2. `dsh-plugin` topic；`meta.title/description` 在 `locale/zh.json`、`locale/en.json`。✓ 3. 建仓满 1 天后再提收录 PR。 4. 向 `awesome-dsh-plugin/awesome-dsh-plugin` 的 `data/plugins/` 提交单文件条目 `suifei__dsh-market-lens.yml`（category 以当时 contributing.md 为准），不动自动生成的 README。 5. npm 发布（可选但推荐）：`npm view @suifei/dsh-market-lens` 确认包名可用后发布。 6. 带 UI 包自查：`dsh.bundle.patch` 存在 ✓；`dsh.client.platform: web` ✓；客户端侧无额外运行时依赖（`peerDependencies` 只列宿主侧 cordis/dsh 面）✓。 ## 首版范围与后续 **首版必做**：自选列表（过滤/排序/批量导入，预制 12 只中外明星股）+ 三市场报价 + 日/周/月 K（MA5/10/20/60 可开关、量副图）+ 指数条 + 搜索 + 财经快讯 + A 股财报指标 + 移动端布局模式切换 + 宿主缓存与多源降级 + 三个只读工具。（快讯与财报原在说明书第二版范围，按用户要求提前落地；新闻为全局滚动流 + 标的关键词过滤，非独立新闻聚合面。） **明确不做**：交易、持仓、选股、AI 投研、L2 盘口。 **后续（按数据源稳定性排序）**：分时图 → 板块/行业视图 → 热力图 → 新闻/快讯 → 自定义布局保存。原则不变：**新数据源先落在宿主侧，UI 只消费归一化结构。** ## 已知边界 - 裸 6 位代码按号段猜测交易所（`92xxxx` 北交所新代码段会被猜成 sh）；带前缀输入永远正确。 - Yahoo 在部分区域返回 403：美股自动落到腾讯，K 线历史长度可能缩短。 - 分时图未进首版；详情页暂以 K 线为主视图。 ## License MIT · 图标为本仓库原创绘制。

evidence.readmeExcerpt: # 最近会话 · dsh-recent-sessions 中文 · English > 像官方「工作区」一样长在左侧栏里的「最近会话」—— 收藏、运行中、等待你的回应、完成未读、最近活跃，一屏直达； > 不用时**一键收起到一行**，标题右侧 🔍 还能**就地搜索**，**每个会话行都有 ☆ 一点即收藏**。 示意图：演示数据，非真实会话 收起态：整段只剩一行（36px），点标题随时展开，选择会被记住；工作区立即拿回全部高度 🌐 **落地页 / 在线说明**： 给 [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) 的**左侧栏**加一个「最近会话」分区。它和官方「工作区」共用同一套网格与交互（36px 分区标题 / 34px 分组行 / 32px 会话行 / 28px 溢出行），看起来就是官方侧边栏的一部分：不另开页面、不是悬浮面板，也不改变官方会话浏览区的任何行为。 **顺手的地方**： - **每个会话行都带 ☆**——包括官方的会话列表，悬停即可一键收藏 / 取消，不用打开会话、也不用拖拽； - 整段可以收起到一行（不占工作区列表的高度，选择会被记住）； - 标题右侧的 🔍 直接把标题行变成输入框，命中文字高亮、`Enter` 打开第一条；`↑`/`↓` 可在分区内键盘浏览； - 收藏里可以拖拽排序，悬停收藏行还会出现 ↑「移到最前」； - 对某个分类手动展开或收起后，硬刷新也会保持你的选择；分区内的滚动位置也会记住； - 黄点行直接写「待授权 / 待回答」，不用点进去才知道在等什么。 - 会话行悬停时给出与官方同一套动作：**⋯ 更多 / 归档 / ☆ 收藏 / 置顶**；「⋯」菜单里有 置顶 · 收藏 · 移到最前（仅收藏行）· 归档 · 复制会话 ID； - 置顶的会话在**每个分类里排最前**，并显示与官方一致的图钉图标（置顶状态与下方官方列表是同一份）。 **它解决什么问题**：任务一多，「哪个在跑、哪个跑完了还没看、哪个在等我授权或回答、我常回访的是哪几个」就得在会话列表里翻半天。这个分区把 **收藏 / 运行中 / 等待你的回应 / 完成未读 / 最近活跃** 五类固定在最上面，配黄 / 蓝 / 绿状态点，一眼就知道下一步该点哪里；收藏可以点 ☆，也可以把会话行直接拖进「收藏」分组。 它以插件形式接管左侧栏外壳，因此这个分组**就在工作区分组上方**，而不是另开一个页面；官方会话浏览区（搜索、会话 `…` 菜单、拖拽排序、归档筛选、工作区增删改）原样保留、原样工作。 默认只统计**属于某个工作区**的会话：未分组的会话（例如在 `/tmp` 里用 CLI 跑的一次性任务）**只有在你需要回应它时**才会出现（等待授权 / 待回答），其余情况（空闲、运行中、完成未读）都留在下方官方列表的「未分组」里。 ## 视觉与交互细节 - **分区标题**与「工作区」同规格：高 36px、14px/20、`label-tertiary`、左侧 4px 内边距，标题完整显示不截断；标题可点击，右侧三个 28×28 图标动作：`搜索会话`、`收起/展开`、`在面板中打开`。 - **一键收起到一行**：点标题（或「收起」）整段折叠成一行 36px，工作区列表立刻拿回全部高度；状态记在浏览器里，下次打开保持。 - 面板页不再占用左侧面板列表的一行（它与分区重复），需要时点标题右侧的 ⤢ 打开。 - **分区内搜索**：点标题右侧的 🔍 直接把标题行变成输入框，按会话标题 / 工作区名筛选本分区里的会话；`Esc` 或 × 退出，`Enter` 打开第一条，命中文字高亮。 - **分类**与工作区分组行同规格：高 34px、16×20 图标槽、标题 14px/20；**悬停时图标换成实心三角**，点击折叠/展开；右侧显示 10px 数量。 - **默认展开规则**：**收藏永远默认收起**（为空时右侧显示「拖入或点 ☆ 收藏」，非空时显示数量）；有「等待你的回应 / 运行中 / 完成未读」时，这些分类默认展开、最近活跃默认收起；三类都没有时，最近活跃默认展开。 - **你的折叠选择会被记住**：一旦手动展开/收起了某个分类，该选择写入 `localStorage`，**硬刷新或重开页面后都会恢复**（包括"收藏是展开的"这个状态）。 - **会话行**与官方会话行同规格：高 32px、状态点占 16×20 槽、标题 14px/20、右侧 10px 相对时间；**悬停时隐藏时间、浮出 ☆**；当前打开的会话常驻选中底色。 - **溢出行**沿用官方 `展开其余 N 个会话 / 收起`（28px、12px、`label-tertiary`）。 - 行间距 2px、分组间距 4px，与官方列表同一套节奏；分类之间与工作区之间用 1px 分隔线区隔。 ## 收藏 三种方式： 1. 会话行悬停时点 `☆`（官方会话行上的新增按钮）； 2. 把会话行**拖进「最近会话」分组**（从下面官方列表直接拖上来即可）； 3. 点分区标题右侧的 ⤢ 打开面板页，在里面拖到「收藏」区，或拖到某条收藏上调整顺序。 收藏顺序即展示顺序，保存在本机浏览器（见「数据」）。 收藏不会把会话从「最近活跃」里拿走：最近活跃是**纯时间列表**（最近碰过的 5 个会话，不管有没有被收藏）；已收藏的行**只用一个信号**——行尾那颗金色 **★**（收藏按钮本身，常驻显示），不再额外叠加标记，避免一行出现两个星。 ## 安装 **插件市场（推荐）**：Plugins → Discover → **Add index source**，粘贴下面的索引地址，然后在卡片上点安装： ``` https://tianxiaz.github.io/dsh-recent-sessions/market/index.json ``` > GitHub Pages 缓存约 10 分钟，发版后很快生效。若该地址在你所在网络不通，可换用 jsDelivr 镜像（分支缓存约 12 小时）： > `https://fastly.jsdelivr.net/gh/tianxiaz/dsh-recent-sessions@main/market/index.json` **命令行**： ```bash dsh plugin --profile <你的 profile> add "git+https://github.com/tianxiaz/dsh-recent-sessions.git" ``` **本地目录**（开发/自用）： ``` plugin_manager install_bundle <绝对路径>/dsh-recent-sessions ``` 安装后**硬刷新页面**即可。 ## ⚠️ 侧栏接管说明（重要） DSH 左侧栏的两个关键位都是**单占位槽**，插件无法"在官方分组旁边插入一节"： | 槽 | 官方占用者 | 性质 | |---|---|---| | `sidebar` | `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-sidebar` 的 SidebarRoot | 整个左列外壳（品牌行、新会话、面板列表、页脚） | | `sidebar.workspaces` | `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-workspace` 的 WorkspaceBrowser | 会话浏览区 | 所以本插件的做法是：**接管外壳、复用会话区**。 - bundle patch 里 `- id: ui-sidebar` + `disabled: true`，禁用官方外壳； - 本插件注册 `sidebar` 占位，声明与官方**同名**的 8 个子槽（`brand.mark` / `brand.name` / `toggle.badge` / `panellist` / `panellist.actions` / `workspaces` / `settings` / `footer.action`），并把 `sidebar.workspaces` **原样渲染**官方 WorkspaceBrowser； - 同时提供 `shell.leading`（macOS 侧栏完全收起时的"打开侧栏 / 新会话"两个窗口按钮），否则收起后无处点开。 这意味着： - 品牌行、新会话按钮、面板图标列表、页脚由本插件渲染（几何与配色对齐官方，但**不是逐像素一致**）； - DSH 官方侧栏以后若改动，本插件需要同步更新（见下）； - 不想要了，禁用/卸载本 bundle 即可恢复官方侧栏（会同时失去面板页与 `☆` 按钮）。 **崩溃隔离**：接管意味着"插件挂了 = 左栏没有占位者"，所以侧栏整体套了一层 error boundary。任何子组件抛错时不会留下空白列，而是退化为：顶部一句提示 + 「重新加载」按钮 + **原样渲染的官方会话列表**（仍可正常选会话、切工作区）。 **空间分配**：始终优先保证工作区列表 —— 工作区至少拿到可用高度的 **55%**（且不少于 160px），「最近会话」最多占 **45%**、上限 420px 并在内部滚动；窗口被压得很矮时，最近会话会**只保留标题一行**，把高度全部让给工作区。拖动工作区里的会话时，「最近会话」还会**临时折叠成一行**，把高度让出来，标题同时变成投放区。 ## 兼容性与维护 - 目标版本：DSH `^0.2.1-rc.5`（`engines.dsh`）。 - 已知失败模式：若某版 DSH 里 `ui-sidebar` 这个行 **id 改名或消失**，patch 会 warn + skip，本插件注册 `sidebar` 时与官方外壳冲突 → 本插件整体不生效（官方 UI 保持不变）。修复：更新 `cordis.patch.yml` 里的行 id、必要时重新对齐外壳。 - 升级 DSH 后的核对清单（都在 `client.js` 的 `sidebar shell` 区）： 1. `sidebar` 槽的 owner props 是否仍是 `{ collapsed, width }`； 2. 需要声明/渲染的子槽集合是否仍是那 8 个； 3. 官方 `SidebarRoot` 的几何（logo 行 60/36px、新会话按钮 38/36px、面板行 36px、折叠内边距 18/10/6）是否变化 → 同步 `SHELL_CSS`； 4. `sidebar.panellist` 的 owner props（`size` / `active`）与 `sidebar.workspaces` 的 owner props（`wide` / `expandSidebar`）； 5. `shell.leading` 的挂载条件（macOS 且侧栏收起）； 6. 官方 WorkspaceBrowser 是否仍以 `sidebar.workspaces` 单占位方式注册。 ## 数据与隐私 - 纯前端插件，**不发起任何网络请求**（除 DSH 自身）。 - 收藏与折叠状态存在当前浏览器 `localStorage`： `dsh.recent-sessions.favorites.v1`（收藏的会话 id，按展示顺序）、`dsh.recent-sessions.inline.open.v1`（整段是否收起到一行）、`dsh.recent-sessions.cats.v1`（每个分类手动折叠/展开的选择）。 - 已归档会话不出现在快捷列表里（收藏仍保留，取消归档后自动回来）；收藏按站点区分，换浏览器/换域名不共享。 ## 许可 MIT，见 [LICENSE](./LICENSE)。

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-opencode-go-router

[![CI](https://github.com/TLEWA/dsh-opencode-go-router/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/TLEWA/dsh-opencode-go-router/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-opencode-go-router.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-opencode-go-router)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)

[English](./README.md) · [简体中文](./README.zh-CN.md)

A DeepSeek Harness (DSH) host plugin that gives an OpenCode Go conversation using a DeepSeek-series model a fresh routing id when billion-context compression loses the reusable prompt cache **and** recent requests are slow. With the optional pre-fold patch for billion-context, the switch happens at the next fold rebuild itself, before the rebuilt request is forwarded, so it adds no cache miss of its own. Without the patch the plugin falls back to a request that is already cold (a system-prompt rewrite) or very likely cold (a request after a long idle gap).

This is the npm package for the DSH plugin whose internal id is `opencode-router`. It only rotates the OpenCode Go routing header; it is not a model adapter.

## Why

OpenCode Go pins a conversation to one upstream backend with the `x-opencode-session` request header. After billion-context rebuilds the context, the next request normally warms a new prefix on that same backend. If the first request after a rebuild reports a low cache hit (25% or less by default), and the last few requests are also slow, the backend is probably a bad place for this conversation.

Rotating after that rebuild would add a second cold request: the rebuild's follow-up is cold on the old backend, and the first request on the new backend is cold again. billion-context writes a fold record only after the rebuild request has completed, so a plugin watching the ledger is always one request late. Its proxy, however, knows just before it forwards a rebuild that a fold is happening.

The optional pre-fold patch adds a loopback callback at exactly that point. The plugin publishes a local endpoint with a random bearer token, the proxy asks it whether this session has a pending switch, and if so writes the returned `x-opencode-session` onto the rebuilt request before forwarding it. The rebuild is cold on any backend; with the new route it becomes the first cold request on the new backend instead of being followed by a second one. This is the only reliable way to remove the extra miss, because the ledger cannot provide a pre-request signal.

Without the patch the plugin remembers the decision and applies it just before a request that is going to be cold anyway: a system-prompt rewrite (its prefix changes regardless of the backend), or the first request after `foldDeferIdleMs` of inactivity, when the upstream prefix cache has very likely expired. The decision and the switch can then be separated by several requests; a later healthy fold clears a pending switch.

Only OpenCode Go DeepSeek-series conversations are eligible. Other models are never routed by this plugin, even when a route exists.

A system-prompt rewrite invalidates the reusable prefix by itself. The request that carries the rewrite is cold on any backend, so when such a rewrite is detected and recent requests are slow, the plugin rotates for that same request: the route switch and the rewrite share one unavoidable cache miss. The last fold's cache condition is ignored in this path because its hit rate cannot be healthy after a rewrite; the performance condition still applies. If a fold-triggered switch is already pending, the rewrite consumes it: the route keeps the fold's cache evidence but uses the current performance window, and records `reason: "fold-deferred"`.

If consecutive switches still land on backends that miss the base targets, the plugin widens the next trigger instead of repeating equivalent switches: each completed post-switch window that remains slower than `ttftThresholdMs` or `throughputThresholdTps` adds one step, giving the next decision `stepTtftGraceMs` (2 s by default) more TTFT room and `stepThroughputGraceTps` (5 tok/s by default) less required throughput. A post-switch window that meets the base targets resets the step to zero. Failure is always judged against the base targets, never the already-widened ones.

The plugin does not compress anything itself and does not change the prompt or the conversation log. It only changes one routing header and keeps local timing counters.

## How it works

- **Cache evidence.** It reads billion-context's per-session state file (`sessions/openai/<host>_<sha256(conversationId).slice(0,24)>.json`) and looks at `metadata.cacheLedger.folds`. billion-context derives `conversationId` from the highest-priority conversation header. In a DSH setup that is `x-bili-plugin-conversation` (the DSH session id); `x-opencode-session` ranks below it, so rotating that header does **not** change the file or open a new one. A fold record's `hPct` is the cache-hit percentage of the first request sent after that rebuild.
- **Eligibility.** Only requests from a configured provider (`opencode-go` by default) whose model id starts with `deepseek` (case-insensitive) are considered. `models` can narrow this to exact DeepSeek ids. Other models are ignored, and a rotation is skipped if the latest ordinary conversation request used a non-eligible model. Auxiliary requests that declare a `purpose` do not change that state.
- **Performance evidence.** It wraps `llm/stream` only for eligible requests, timestamps the first content chunk, and records output tokens per second at the finish chunk. It keeps the last `sampleSize` valid samples per DSH session.
- **Decision.** On a new fold, it evaluates the folds *before* that fold. It records a pending switch only when the latest `foldsWindow` fold(s) all have `hPct <= cacheHitThresholdPct` **and** the recent samples are slow (average TTFT `>=` 12000 ms by default, or average throughput `<=` 60 tokens/second by default). The performance target can be widened by the failure step described above. `foldRotationMode: "immediate"` restores the 0.2.1 behavior of rotating at that fold; `"off"` disables fold-triggered switching.
- **Pre-fold hook (optional patch).** When `preFoldHook` is enabled, the plugin listens on a random port bound to `127.0.0.1` and writes a descriptor to `$DSH_HOME/storages/opencode-router/pre-fold-hook.json` with the URL and a random bearer token. The optional patch to billion-context reads that descriptor and calls `POST /pre-fold` right after it has built the rebuilt body and before it forwards that body. The endpoint accepts only loopback POST requests with the token and only consumes an already pending fold decision. If the patch is absent, nothing calls the hook and the plugin falls back to the deferred path below.
- **Applying a switch.** With the pre-fold hook active, the next fold rebuild consumes a pending decision: the plugin rotates the route, returns the new value, and the rebuilt request itself is sent on the new route. Otherwise the plugin applies the pending switch before a request that is already going to be cold: the system-prompt-rewrite path, or the first eligible request after `foldDeferIdleMs` (5 minutes by default) of session inactivity. `foldDeferMaxMs` and `foldDeferMaxRequests` can force a pending switch after a limit; both default to `0` (never force), because forcing without a cold request may recreate the extra miss. A later fold whose evidence is healthy clears the pending switch.
- **System-prompt rewrite.** From `llm/stream` it extracts the initial system prompt the same way pi-ai does (`options.system` plus leading `system` messages) and fingerprints it per session. When the fingerprint changes, it writes a route before the request headers are assembled, so the same request that carries the rewrite also carries the new routing id. This path uses only the performance condition (the fold cache condition is bypassed); without a pending fold switch the route records `reason: "system-rewrite"`. A later fold caused by that rewrite is guarded from rotating a second time for the same miss.
- **Routing.** A persisted route maps the DSH session id to a generated `ses_...` value. The `llm-pi-ai/request-headers` waterfall runs after pi-ai assembles its header set and before the request is sent, so setting `x-opencode-session` there reaches the wire. In the reference setup a companion injector such as `dsh-opencode-ip-guard` supplies a baseline value equal to the DSH session id; when a route exists this plugin replaces it, and the injector's no-overwrite fallback leaves the value alone.
- **No billion-context, no effect.** If the sessions directory or the session state file is absent, the monitor stays idle. The header hook has no route and does nothing. No exception is thrown into DSH.

The first fold seen after a plugin start is a baseline and never causes rotation; this baseline rule applies to the fold path only. A later fold that meets both conditions becomes a **pending** switch rather than an immediate one. The system-prompt-rewrite path is independent of any fold: even when the session has never recorded a fold, a changed system prompt with slow samples can rotate on the rewrite request itself (the fold cache condition is bypassed). The first system prompt seen in a session is only a fingerprint baseline; a rewrite rotation requires a subsequent observed change. The current session is considered eligible only while its latest ordinary conversation request is an OpenCode Go DeepSeek-series request.

A rotation changes only the upstream routing id. billion-context keeps writing the same state file for the DSH session, so the monitor keeps following it; after recording the fold that made a switch pending it advances its fold cursor. The same rebuild cannot make a second switch pending, but a later rebuild can. A pending switch survives ordinary healthy warm requests; it is applied at the next fold rebuild when the pre-fold hook is active, at a request treated as cold (a system-prompt rewrite) or expected to be cold (the first request after a long idle gap) otherwise, forced by a safety valve, or cleared when a later fold no longer meets the cache/performance conditions.

## Requirements

- DSH with the `llm-pi-ai` adapter and an OpenCode Go provider (default `opencode-go`) configured with at least one DeepSeek-series model (model id starts with `deepseek`).
- billion-context installed and actively saving session state.
- Optional but recommended for the exact seam: a billion-context bundle the patch script recognizes. Without the patch the plugin still works with the deferred fallback.
- DSH 0.2.1-rc.5 or newer, below 0.3.0.
- Node.js 20 or newer.

## Install from npm

```bash
dsh plugin add dsh-opencode-go-router --profile <profile>
```

Or add `dsh-opencode-go-router` from the DSH plugin manager's add-plugin box. The package declares `dsh.bundle.patch`, so a normal install creates the `opencode-router` row; do not add a separate profile row for it.

## Pre-fold patch (optional)

The patch is what makes the rebuild request itself use the new route. It edits billion-context's bundled proxy, so npm install does not and should not apply it automatically. Run it once per billion-context installation, then restart or reload the billion-context proxy process.

From the DSH profile directory:

```bash
cd "$DSH_HOME/profiles/<profile>"
node node_modules/dsh-opencode-go-router/scripts/patch-billion-context.mjs --check
node node_modules/dsh-opencode-go-router/scripts/patch-billion-context.mjs --apply
```

From this repository:

```bash
node scripts/patch-billion-context.mjs --check
node scripts/patch-billion-context.mjs --apply
```

The script searches every profile under `$DSH_HOME/profiles/*/node_modules/billion-context/dist/index.js`; use `--file <path>` or `--profile <name>` to narrow it. `--check` exits `0` when already patched, `1` when unpatched, and `4` when the bundle has no unique `outbound=rebuilt;` anchor and is therefore unsupported. `--apply` keeps a `.opencode-router.bak` next to the bundle and is idempotent. `--revert` restores that backup. A billion-context upgrade replaces `dist/index.js`, so re-run `--check` and `--apply` after upgrading.

The patched proxy calls only the loopback URL and bearer token in the plugin's descriptor. If the plugin is disabled or the descriptor is missing, the callback quietly does nothing and the request follows the unpatched path.

## Install from a local checkout (development)

1. Keep this repository somewhere stable, for example `C:/Users/me/DSHs/opencode-router`.
2. In the profile's `package.json`:
   - add `dsh-opencode-go-router` to `dsh.profile.bundles`;
   - add `"dsh-opencode-go-router": "link:C:/Users/me/DSHs/opencode-router"` to `dependencies`.
3. Make the profile's `node_modules/dsh-opencode-go-router` point at the repository (a directory junction/symlink is enough on Windows).
4. Do **not** add a standalone row for this plugin to the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`. The package declares `dsh.bundle.patch: ./cordis.patch.yml`, which inserts the plugin row itself. A profile row added without an `insert` is only an override and cannot create the row.
5. Restart DSH. In the plugin manager, `dsh-opencode-go-router` should appear as a profile bundle with one row (`include:opencode-router`). If the host was already running before the bundle declaration existed, reload it through the plugin manager or restart DSH.
6. Read the live state at `http://127.0.0.1:<DSH-web-port>/opencode-router/status`.

To change defaults, add an override by row id to the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`:

```yaml
- id: opencode-router
  config:
    cacheHitThresholdPct: 25
```

Because the plugin entry point reloads `lib/impl.js` with a cache-busting query on every `apply`, editing the implementation and touching the plugin config is usually enough to try new code. In a running host, toggling the profile bundle off and on through the plugin manager also reloads the static imports (`lib/core.js`, `lib/store.js`, `lib/monitor.js`); the 0.1.2 -> 0.1.3 threshold change was verified that way. If the host keeps reporting the old version, restart DSH.

## Configuration

| Key | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | `true` | Master switch. When false, hooks pass through and the monitor does not run. |
| `providers` | `["opencode-go"]` | Providers eligible for routing; the model must still be a `deepseek*` id. |
| `models` | `[]` | Optional exact DeepSeek model allow-list; empty means any `deepseek*` model of the provider. |
| `cacheHitThresholdPct` | `25` | A fold counts as "cache lost" when `hPct <= this`. Not applied to a system-prompt rewrite rotation. |
| `systemRewriteBypassCache` | `true` | Rotate on a system-prompt change even when the last fold's cache hit is healthy; the performance condition must still be slow. |
| `foldsWindow` | `1` | How many recent folds must all be below the cache threshold. |
| `foldRotationMode` | `"defer"` | `defer` applies a fold-triggered switch only before a request that is already cold; `immediate` rotates right after the fold (0.2.1 behavior); `off` disables fold-triggered switches (system-prompt rewrites still rotate). |
| `foldDeferIdleMs` | `300000` | In `defer` mode, rotate before the first eligible request after this much session idle time. `0` disables the idle trigger. |
| `foldDeferMaxMs` | `0` | Force a pending switch once it is this old. `0` disables the safety valve. |
| `foldDeferMaxRequests` | `0` | Force a pending switch before the request after this many eligible requests have gone out. `0` disables the safety valve. |
| `preFoldHook` | `true` | Serve the loopback `POST /pre-fold` endpoint used by the optional billion-context patch. `false` disables the seam and leaves only the deferred path. |
| `preFoldHookPath` | `$DSH_HOME/storages/opencode-router/pre-fold-hook.json` | Descriptor file written for the patched proxy. Override only when the proxy reads it from a custom path. |
| `ttftThresholdMs` | `12000` | Base average time to first content token at or above this is slow. |
| `throughputThresholdTps` | `60` | Base average output tokens/second at or below this is slow. |
| `stepTtftGraceMs` | `2000` | Each consecutive failed switch widens the next TTFT target by this much. |
| `stepThroughputGraceTps` | `5` | Each consecutive failed switch lowers the next throughput target by this much (floor `0.01`). |
| `sampleSize` | `5` | Number of recent requests used for the performance decision. |
| `requireFullSamples` | `true` | Require all `sampleSize` samples before rotating. |
| `routingIdPrefix` | `"ses_"` | Prefix of generated routing ids. |
| `statePath` | `$DSH_HOME/storages/opencode-router/state.json` | Persisted routes and timing samples. |
| `dryRun` | `false` | Log rotations without selecting the new header value. |
| `debug` | `false` | Extra info logs. |
| `overrideExistingHeader` | `true` | Replace an already present `x-opencode-session`. Set false to preserve it. |
| `pollIntervalMs` | `2000` | Poll interval while a session is active. |
| `requestCheckDelaysMs` | `[400, 1500]` | Extra state-file checks after a request finishes. |
| `biliSessionsDir` | `null` | Override billion-context's sessions root. |
| `biliProtocol` | `"openai"` | State subdirectory. |
| `biliUpstreamHost` | `"opencode.ai"` | Host label used in the state filename. |
| `maxSamples` | `20` | Maximum samples kept per session. |
| `sessionActiveMs` | `600000` | Stop polling a session after this idle time. |
| `minRotationGapMs` | `0` | Minimum time between rotations for one session. |

## Status route

`GET /opencode-router/status` returns JSON with the effective config, persisted routes, rotation history, and per-session monitor state:

- `history` — recent silent switches, newest first, with `sessionId`, `at`, `reason`, `foldSeq`, `cacheHitPct`, `step`, the routing `value`, before/after TTFT and throughput, sample progress, and a `backfilled` marker; a deferred fold switch records `reason: "fold-deferred"`, and one applied by the pre-fold hook records `reason: "fold-preflight"`;
- `eligibility` — the configured providers and the fixed `deepseek` model prefix;
- `baselineReady` and `lastFoldSeq` — fold cursor;
- `latestFold` — latest fold record (including `hPct`);
- `watchingId` — DSH session id whose billion-context state file is being followed;
- `route` — current rotated routing id, or `null`; its `reason` is `cache-and-performance`, `fold-deferred`, `fold-preflight`, or `system-rewrite`, and `step` is the failure step used for that switch;
- `targetActive` — whether the latest ordinary conversation request was an eligible OpenCode Go DeepSeek request; `false` blocks rotation;
- `systemPromptFp` — fingerprint of the latest observed initial system prompt, or `null`;
- `systemRewriteBypassCache`, `systemRewriteRotations`, `lastSystemRewriteAt` — rewrite-rotation settings and counters;
- `foldRotationMode`, `pendingRotation`, `deferredRotations`, `lastDeferredAt` — fold-switch mode, the pending switch (age, fold number, cache hit, step, requests seen, and trigger averages), how many pending switches have been created, and when the latest one was created;
- `preFoldHook` — loopback endpoint state: `enabled`, `listening`, `path`, `url`, `port`, request/rejection/rotation counters, `lastRequestAt`, `lastError`, and `lastDecision`;
- `preflightRotations`, `lastPreflightAt` — switches consumed by the pre-fold hook and when the latest one happened;
- `stepping` — `step`, `consecutiveFailures`, base and effective TTFT/throughput thresholds, and the per-step grace values;
- `samples` — count, average TTFT, average throughput;
- `rotations`, `lastRequestAt`, `lastTickAt`, `lastError`;
- `routing` — header-hook counters and the latest decision: `checks`, `applications`, `lastCheckedAt`, `lastCheckedSessionId`, `lastAppliedAt`, `lastAppliedSessionId`, `lastAppliedValue`, `lastReason`. `lastReason` is `applied`, `no-route`, `existing-header`, `no-headers`, `disabled`, or `not-target`.

The route is localhost-only when the host's web server is bound to localhost. Treat the JSON as diagnostics.

## Settings page

In the DSH Web client, open the plugin manager and select this bundle. Its detail page renders a **Silent switch performance log** above the bundle configuration rows.

For each silent switch it shows the time, a short session id, the trigger (`Fold + speed`, including a deferred fold switch, `Fold rebuild seam` for a pre-fold switch, or `System rewrite`), the fold number and cache hit behind the decision, the failure step if it was above zero, average TTFT and throughput before the switch, the first `sampleSize` eligible samples after it, and the percentage change. The header also shows the most recently active session's step and effective thresholds, and the panel explains the per-step grace. Rows refresh every five seconds from `GET /opencode-router/status`. The after window is frozen once it has `sampleSize` samples, so later traffic does not rewrite history.

Routes created before 0.2.0 are backfilled as one row per still-known route and marked `Reconstructed`; their after values come from samples retained after that rotation. The panel lives in the Web client and does not affect host routing.

## Privacy and safety

- Stored data is limited to DSH session ids, generated routing ids, fold numbers, cache percentages, TTFT, throughput, rotation history, and timestamps. No prompts, messages, tool output, or API keys are stored.
- Every host callback catches its own errors. A missing or malformed billion-context state file only produces a log entry.
- The pre-fold endpoint binds only to `127.0.0.1`, accepts only POST, and requires a 32-byte random bearer token from the descriptor. The descriptor is written with user-only permissions where the platform supports them and is removed on dispose. The patch refuses any callback URL that is not loopback HTTP.
- Rotating a header is a routing hint, not a guarantee that the gateway picks a different physical backend. If the gateway ignores unknown or new session values, the plugin cannot force a move.
- billion-context's state file is an internal format. If its layout changes, the monitor may see no folds and stay idle; the plugin will not corrupt anything.

## Development

```bash
node --test
```

The suite covers fold parsing, the cache/performance decision, the consecutive-failure stepping rule, deferred fold switches and their safety valves, the pre-fold seam and its loopback endpoint authentication, the billion-context patch idempotency/backup/restore, system-prompt extraction/fingerprinting, the system-rewrite decision, DeepSeek-only eligibility, state persistence, rotation history, the monitor state machine, header routing, stream measurement, and the client bundle registration.

## License

MIT
